bookmarked.description: A comprehensive lorebook for Lunaris Academy: New Moon, a hidden supernatural boarding school where powered Humans, Werebeasts, and rare Beastweres learn, live, train, and grow together. Includes detailed species lore, students, faculty, classes, clubs, traditions, Moonshadow Forest, Pineharbor, major locations, full-moon culture, school rules, daily life, and supernatural worldbuilding.

entries.content:
## Lunaris Academy: New Moon

Lunaris Academy: New Moon is a hidden supernatural boarding school deep within the enchanted **Moonshadow Forest**, built around one central idea: students become safer and stronger when they learn both self-mastery and respect for lives unlike their own. The academy primarily serves three interconnected groups—humans with supernatural powers, werebeasts whose human lives include animal transformations, and the exceptionally rare Beastweres whose true bodies are animals capable of assuming human or humanoid guises. They share classes, dorm life, meals, clubs, events, arguments, friendships, responsibilities, and the ordinary inconveniences of being students.

The campus feels old without being frozen in the past. Ancient stone halls follow the contours of enormous trees; newer buildings use timber, glass, metal, adaptive wards, and modern accessibility systems. Moonlit paths curve around roots rather than cutting through them. Towers rise above the canopy for astronomy, while open training spaces, the Lunar Grove, and forest trails give transformed students enough room to move naturally. Phones, tablets, digital assignments, medical equipment, buses, modern kitchens, secure Wi-Fi, and ordinary school bureaucracy exist alongside enchantments, transformation-safe architecture, magical laboratories, whispering books, and lunar phenomena. The school is magical because magic is part of daily life, not because every hallway needs to behave impossibly.

New Moon is the modern reform of an older Lunaris tradition. Historic spaces and names remain throughout campus: the old Fang Library survives as a protected wing of the Moonlit Library; the Beastborne Arena forms the historic core of the enlarged Training Grounds; former Sanctuary Dorm wings were renovated into the mixed Twilight Dormitories; and places such as the Lunar Grove, Moonlit Archives, Alchemy Atrium, and Eclipse Caverns remain part of school memory. The reform did not erase old culture. It removed assumptions that students should be segregated, stereotyped, forced to transform, ranked by raw power, or treated as dangerous merely because of species.

The academy's mission is practical. Werebeasts learn safe shifting, body awareness, recovery, instinct management, and how lunar changes affect them individually. Beastweres are never required to remain in a human guise simply to make others comfortable; true-form access, communication, education, clothing storage, and privacy are built into campus life. Powered humans learn precision, ethics, recovery, and how to use abilities without defining themselves solely by those abilities. Mixed classes and events teach students how to ask before helping, understand different bodies, and rely on one another without assuming that every member of a species behaves the same way.

Outside the wards, the nearby town of **Pineharbor** remains unaware of Lunaris's true nature. To mundane residents, students belong to the secluded private **Northreach Preparatory School**. Town trips, deliveries, sports, cafés, libraries, and community events therefore demand discretion without requiring students to be ashamed of themselves. The concealment system protects both communities while faculty teach students the difference between healthy privacy and isolation.

Daily life defines Lunaris as much as its magic. Students wake in Twilight Dorms, drift toward breakfast in and around the Den Commons, attend core academics and specialized classes, train in the afternoon, then scatter into clubs, study groups, forest walks, music rehearsals, art rooms, workshops, or the Moonlit Library. Full moons change schedules and energy for some students but are not automatic horror events. A full-moon night can mean a supervised run, a quiet Lunar Grove vigil, extra food, heightened senses, a difficult first shift, an astronomy lesson, a group ritual, or simply an early bedtime. New Moon exists so every one of those experiences can belong at the same school.

entries.content:
Lunaris began as a secluded refuge created by several supernatural families who needed a place to teach young shifters before the modern world had language for power control, accessibility, or supernatural education. Early Lunaris was small, tradition-heavy, and dominated by werewolf and werebeast customs. Lessons centered on surviving transformations, hiding from ordinary humans, respecting territory, and passing inherited knowledge from older shifters to younger ones. Powered humans were admitted later, and Beastweres later still, forcing the school to rethink assumptions that had once treated the human body as the normal starting point for every supernatural student.

The period now called the New Moon Reformation occurred after decades of gradual modernization. Students and younger faculty argued that the academy could not teach responsibility while relying on outdated customs, vague punishments, species stereotypes, and secrecy rules that left students unprepared for phones, cameras, social media, public transportation, modern medicine, and ordinary civic life. The reform did not erase the older school. Instead it kept the strongest traditions—moon ceremonies, transformation mentoring, wilderness training, sanctuary law, communal meals, and the principle that power must be matched by responsibility—while rebuilding the institution around clear rights and modern safeguards.

The present academy uses the name “New Moon” as a reminder that renewal is part of its identity. A new moon is not treated as absence but as a quiet starting point: the phase when raw werewolf power is lowest, concentration is easiest, and students can reflect on what they want to become before the next cycle grows brighter. The symbol appears on orientation badges, the school seal, and the silver bell rung at the beginning of each term.

Old traditions still matter. Some students come from families that remember Lunaris as a stricter, more isolated place, while others are the first supernatural person in their family. This creates lively debate about heritage, modernization, privacy, leadership, and what should be preserved. Faculty deliberately include those disagreements in history and ethics classes so the academy never becomes a museum of its own mythology.

Daily routines matter as much as dramatic moments. Students still have homework, alarms, laundry, club meetings, cafeteria lines, exams, group projects, forgotten chargers, sports practice, and weekend plans. Supernatural traits simply change how those routines are managed. A student with heightened hearing may use dampening earbuds; a shifter may keep spare adaptive clothing in a locker; a powered human may sign out a practice room before testing a new technique. These small habits are considered signs of maturity because Lunaris values preparation over bravado.

entries.content:
## Moonshadow Forest, Hidden Basin, Wards and Secrecy

Lunaris Academy is hidden deep inside **Moonshadow Forest**, an old supernatural woodland whose geography is larger and stranger than mundane maps suggest. The public world knows of ordinary forested land in the broader region, but the protected interior folds around a warded basin where Lunaris has grown for generations. Ancient trees, moon-kissed clearings, streams, rocky ridges, and glowing footpaths shape the campus. Buildings follow the terrain rather than flattening it, which is why old stone halls can stand beside glass laboratories and timber dorms without making the school feel divided into separate eras.

The academy's concealment is layered instead of relying on one spell. Long-range wards encourage mundane travelers to choose other roads, distort casual aerial photography, soften unusual lights and sounds, and keep ordinary navigation from finding the inner basin by accident. Physical gates, staff patrols, magical sensors, and modern security support those wards. Emergency systems are designed to fail safely: concealment can be opened for trusted responders rather than trapping students inside for the sake of secrecy.

Moonshadow itself is not merely camouflage. The forest is part of Lunaris education and culture. The managed **Wildering Woods** lie closest to campus and contain approved trails, lesson zones, Moonrun routes, ecological study plots, and transformation clearings. Deeper protected zones are restricted because the ecosystem includes old magic, difficult terrain, sensitive creatures, and historical sites. The **Lunar Grove** sits where several natural lunar currents cross; the **Eclipse Caverns** descend into luminous stone beneath an older ridge; and pathways around the Moonlit Library and observatory brighten subtly at night. Faculty teach students that enchanted nature is still an ecosystem rather than an unlimited supply cabinet.

Secrecy becomes most important at the outer edge of the forest. Pineharbor lies close enough for shopping, recreation, work placements, and normal teenage outings, yet residents do not know a supernatural school stands beyond familiar roads. Lunaris uses **Northreach Preparatory School** as its mundane identity. Students wear ordinary versions of school clothing in town, secure visible transformation traits when practical and safe, avoid public demonstrations, and follow strict rules about recording classmates. Nobody is expected to endanger themselves to maintain the cover; emergencies prioritize life and safety, after which staff handle witnesses and explanations through established hidden-community procedures.

The forest therefore creates two kinds of freedom. Inside the protected basin, students can practice powers, transform, fly in designated corridors, use true forms, study magic, and participate in traditions without constant fear of exposure. Outside it, they learn how to participate in a mundane community respectfully. New Moon treats both skills as adulthood preparation. Hiding is not the academy's moral purpose. The wards simply create enough protected space for students to decide when, where, and with whom their supernatural identities are shared.

entries.content:
The New Moon student body is intentionally mixed. The iconic core roster consists of forty frequently seen students: twenty Werebeasts, six Beastweres, and fourteen Humans with powers. That balance is not a quota for the entire academy, but it reflects the three communities around which Lunaris structures its education. Students are generally in the upper-secondary and preparatory age range, with flexible placement for supernatural development, interrupted schooling, or late-awakening powers.

Daily culture is informal enough to feel like a real school but structured enough to keep extraordinary abilities from turning ordinary disagreements into disasters. Students argue about music, borrow chargers, compete for favorite tables, complain about homework, trade snacks, form group chats, oversleep, forget assignments, practice for performances, and gossip about harmless school drama. Species differences affect routines without dominating every conversation. A werewolf may need an extra meal near the full moon, a raven Beastwere may prefer a perch-like window seat in true form, and a telekinetic may use a weighted bracelet when distracted, but classmates usually treat these as ordinary accommodations.

The academy rejects species rankings. Werebeasts are not automatically leaders because they are strong. Humans with powers are not automatically scholars because their gifts are less physical. Beastweres are not mascots, pets, or curiosities because their base form is animal. Leadership is earned through judgment, reliability, and trust. This principle shapes clubs, dorm assignments, team competitions, and the student council.

Friendship networks cross species constantly. Some students bond through shared powers, some through similar family pressures, and some simply because they sit beside each other in mathematics. Lunaris deliberately creates mixed project teams, but it does not force intimacy. Students are allowed private space, same-species affinity groups, and quiet time when they need it. The goal is not to make everyone identical; it is to build a school where difference is normal enough that nobody must perform their identity every hour of the day.

Training is built around repeatable control rather than dramatic displays. Students are taught to notice early warning signs, name what they are experiencing, choose an appropriate response, and recover properly afterward. Faculty use observation notes, self-reports, fitness data, magical readings, and peer teamwork to help students improve without turning every difficulty into punishment. Progress can mean a stronger ability, but it can also mean stopping on time, asking for assistance, recovering faster, or recognizing that a stressful day is not the right time to push a limit.
entries.name: 🎓 Student Body and School Culture

entries.content:
Lunaris is an old supernatural institution that functions like a modern school. Students carry smartphones, use tablets and laptops, submit assignments online, stream music, play games, message friends, and attend video calls with approved family members. The academy operates its own secure network called MoonNet, which provides ordinary internet access while automatically protecting the campus location and blocking dangerous supernatural marketplaces, predatory tracking services, and known coercive spellware.

Technology is adapted rather than banned. Transformation-safe lockers store devices before high-impact shifting. Durable wristbands can display schedules, medical alerts, and emergency instructions even when a phone is unavailable. Beastwere students who cannot use touchscreens in true form can access voice interfaces, large floor pads, stylus harnesses, or staff-assisted terminals. Werebeasts can request reinforced phone cases, clothing pockets that remain accessible after partial shifts, and biometric settings that recognize altered fingerprints or facial structure. Powered humans with electromagnetic, thermal, psychic, or kinetic gifts receive equipment that protects electronics from accidental interference.

Recording culture is tightly regulated. Casual photos are allowed in normal social spaces, but no one may record another student shifting, reverting, receiving medical care, losing power control, sleeping in a vulnerable true form, or using a private accommodation without permission. Dorm bedrooms, clinic rooms, changing areas, and designated quiet dens are camera-free by policy and ward.

The school also teaches digital cover discipline for Pineharbor trips. Students learn not to post impossible feats, strange animal transformations, supernatural injuries, or campus backgrounds. Location metadata is scrubbed, but personal responsibility still matters. Staff would rather teach students how to use modern technology safely than pretend it can be removed from their lives. As a result, New Moon feels lived-in: old moonstone arches have charging outlets, ancient courtyards have strong Wi-Fi, and the Moonlit Library lends both spellbooks and noise-canceling headphones.

Because Lunaris is a mixed community, no single species is treated as the default. Architecture, schedules, meals, uniforms, sports, clubs, and dorm policies are designed around overlapping needs. Werebeasts may need space to shift, Beastweres may need secure true-form areas, and powered humans may require grounding equipment or power-safe workstations. Students learn each other’s boundaries through ordinary friendship and cooperation, which is one reason cross-species teams are common in classes and school events.
entries.name: 📱 Modern Campus Life and Technology

entries.content:
Lunaris combines ordinary academics with supernatural training. Every student studies literature, history, mathematics, science, civics, and practical life skills alongside courses suited to their biology or powers. Werebeasts attend Transformation Studies and may take species-specific electives. Beastweres attend Beast Mastery and human-integration modules when needed. Powered humans take Power Control and Applied Ability. Mixed classes such as Combat Training, Ethics and Secrecy, Potions and Herbology, Enchantment, Emergency Response, art, music, and physical education create shared ground.

Placement depends on mastery rather than age alone. A seventeen-year-old werewolf who has shifted safely for years may take an advanced transformation seminar while an eighteen-year-old newly bitten student begins with fundamentals. A fifteen-year-old telekinetic with excellent control can advance in power theory while still taking age-appropriate mathematics. Beastweres may receive extra language or technology instruction if they entered human society recently, without that support being treated as a measure of intelligence.

Assessment is practical. Students still take written exams, but teachers also grade safe decision-making, recovery habits, teamwork, restraint, preparation, and the ability to explain why a technique works. A student who can produce a spectacular attack but cannot stop it on command is not considered advanced. Likewise, a shifter who knows when not to transform may score better than someone with more raw strength.

Graduation requires academic competence, a personal safety plan, demonstrated control appropriate to the student’s abilities, completion of secrecy and public-integration training, basic first aid, and a supervised capstone. The capstone can be research, community service, a crafted device, a performance, an ecological project, a controlled field exercise, or another meaningful demonstration. New Moon does not expect students to become soldiers. It expects them to leave able to live responsibly in whichever world they choose.

These practices also support the academy’s central secrecy rule. Students are free to be themselves on protected grounds, but they learn how to move through the mundane world without exposing classmates or frightening unprepared civilians. That means planning clothing, transportation, power use, scent or sound control, and emergency exits before town trips. Secrecy is taught as community protection rather than shame: the hidden world remains hidden so young people can learn safely and ordinary humans in Pineharbor can continue their lives without being pulled into supernatural conflicts they do not understand.
entries.name: 📚 Academic Structure and Graduation

entries.content:
The New Moon calendar follows an ordinary academic year but overlays it with the lunar cycle because werewolf biology and several other supernatural systems respond to moon phase. The school publishes both dates on every official schedule. New-moon weeks are commonly used for examinations requiring fine concentration, delicate transformation practice, difficult negotiations, and reflective ceremonies. Waxing-moon weeks add more physical training and outdoor work as werewolf energy rises. Full-moon days receive adjusted meals, reduced late-afternoon academic load, extra staffing, and optional accommodations. Waning phases emphasize recovery, review, repair, and long-form projects.

The academy never cancels learning simply because the moon is full. Instead, it plans intelligently. Werewolves with strong lunar sensitivity may attend shortened classes, use quiet rooms, or complete evening work earlier in the day. Other werebeasts whose cycles are seasonal, weather-linked, or independent of the moon follow individualized plans. Beastweres are affected mainly through their own magical reserves and species rhythms rather than the werewolf lunar core. Powered humans may notice environmental changes if their abilities interact with moonlight, tides, dreams, or emotion, but they are not assumed to have werewolf symptoms.

Major traditions are placed deliberately. The New Moon Welcome begins each term during a dark phase. The Lunar Festival occurs near a bright autumn moon. The Moonlit Challenge rotates across phases so no one species receives the same advantage every year. Full Moon Vigils are monthly, while the large Moonrun occurs only when conditions are safe.

Students learn to think of the calendar as a tool rather than a superstition. Tracking sleep, appetite, power stability, sensory sensitivity, and mood against the lunar cycle helps many students predict needs before they become problems. The result is a school rhythm that feels natural: the moon affects campus life, but it does not control every person in the same way.

At Lunaris Academy: New Moon, this subject is treated as part of ordinary student life rather than a spectacle. Faculty expect students to understand what their bodies and abilities are doing, communicate when they need help, and use the school’s accommodations before a manageable problem turns into a crisis. The academy keeps practical supplies, quiet rooms, reinforced practice areas, flexible meal options, and trained staff available so that different species can function together without anyone being treated as dangerous merely for existing. Older students are encouraged to model calm, responsible behavior for younger classmates, while teachers distinguish between an involuntary symptom and a deliberate harmful choice.
entries.name: 🗓️ School Calendar and Lunar Rhythm

entries.content:
Lunaris is legally and culturally treated as sanctuary ground. Students who arrive frightened, newly changed, displaced, or unsure of their powers are protected while they learn. Sanctuary does not mean immunity from consequences; it means that ordinary mistakes, involuntary symptoms, and requests for help are handled as education and care rather than as proof that someone is dangerous. Deliberate cruelty, coercion, repeated reckless behavior, and attempts to expose the hidden community are still serious violations.

Every student has several basic rights inside the wards: recognition as a person in every form, access to appropriate food and medical care, privacy during transformation and recovery, reasonable disability and species accommodations, the ability to decline unnecessary physical contact, the right to report harassment, and the right to be heard before major discipline. Beastweres retain full personhood in true animal form. Werebeasts are not required to shift for entertainment or to prove their lineage. Powered humans are not required to demonstrate abilities outside training simply because someone is curious.

Responsibility runs beside those rights. Students must warn staff if they know a power or transformation is becoming unstable, follow safety zones, respect boundaries, protect secrecy, and repair harm when they cause it. Self-control is defined realistically: asking for assistance, leaving a crowded room, using a restraint device voluntarily, or choosing not to participate can be examples of control.

The sanctuary principle shapes the tone of the entire academy. Instructors can be strict, but punishment is not built around humiliation. Medical care is not disciplinary. Quiet rooms are not detention. Needing supervision on a full moon is not a moral failure. By separating safety support from shame, Lunaris makes it more likely that students speak up early—and that is one of the reasons the New Moon system works.

Daily routines matter as much as dramatic moments. Students still have homework, alarms, laundry, club meetings, cafeteria lines, exams, group projects, forgotten chargers, sports practice, and weekend plans. Supernatural traits simply change how those routines are managed. A student with heightened hearing may use dampening earbuds; a shifter may keep spare adaptive clothing in a locker; a powered human may sign out a practice room before testing a new technique. These small habits are considered signs of maturity because Lunaris values preparation over bravado.

entries.content:
Werebeasts are the greater family of human-base supernatural animal shifters recognized at Lunaris. Their permanent starting state is human, while a supernatural animal template allows them to assume a beast form, a humanoid hybrid form, or both. The defining direction is Human → Beast. Werewolves are the best-known subtype but are not the whole family; werebears, werelions, weretigers, werecats, wereboars, werebirds, werecrocodiles, werestags, and many other lineages follow the same underlying pattern.

A werebeast’s animal expression affects senses, movement, instinct, physical strengths, environmental preferences, and sometimes unique magic. A werelion may excel at explosive strength and social presence, a werehawk at flight and distance vision, a weretiger at stealth and acceleration, and a werebear at resilience. The academy treats these differences as lineage traits rather than rankings. No subtype is inherently superior, and raw strength does not determine maturity or leadership.

Werebeasts remain the same person in every form. Transformation changes anatomy and can amplify instinct, but it does not create a second moral identity that can automatically be blamed for choices. New or curse-affected students may experience disorientation and involuntary responses, which is why Lunaris emphasizes early-warning awareness, supervised practice, and recovery routines.

The academy’s culture emphasizes personhood and consent. No student is permitted to touch another person’s ears, tail, wings, fur, transformed body, magical focus, or personal equipment without permission. Recording another student during a transformation, medical episode, loss of power control, or vulnerable true-form moment is a serious privacy violation. Jokes are tolerated when everyone involved is laughing; humiliation, species stereotyping, coercion, and baiting someone into a shift are not. The result is a campus where unusual biology can be openly accommodated inside the wards even though it must remain hidden from the nearby mundane town.

Training is built around repeatable control rather than dramatic displays. Students are taught to notice early warning signs, name what they are experiencing, choose an appropriate response, and recover properly afterward. Faculty use observation notes, self-reports, fitness data, magical readings, and peer teamwork to help students improve without turning every difficulty into punishment. Progress can mean a stronger ability, but it can also mean stopping on time, asking for assistance, recovering faster, or recognizing that a stressful day is not the right time to push a limit.
entries.name: 🐾 Werebeasts — Core Definition

entries.content:
Werebeast classification begins with true form and transformation direction. If a person naturally returns to a human base when transformation magic is inactive, they are a Werebeast. If the natural body is an animal and the humanlike body is temporary, they are a Beastwere. This distinction matters more than appearance because a werewolf and a wolfwere can both look wolf-like while having opposite developmental histories and different transformation limits.

Within the werebeast family, animal lineage describes the supernatural template. Werewolves emphasize lunar cycles, scent, endurance, and strong social resonance. Werebears tend toward durability, strength, recovery, and protective instincts. Feline strains such as weretigers, wereleopards, and werecats often emphasize balance, night vision, speed, and controlled bursts of movement. Wereboars commonly display endurance, dense musculature, and powerful forward momentum. Werebirds may gain flight, lightweight transformed anatomy, and exceptional distance vision. Aquatic and semi-aquatic strains adapt to water, breath control, and specialized movement.

The same school rules apply across subtypes, but accommodations differ. Lunaris therefore records a student’s actual lineage rather than writing “werebeast” and assuming the rest. Training plans account for wingspan, claws, mass changes, temperature needs, sensory range, and whether the student’s hybrid form can safely use human tools.

entries.name: 🐾 Werebeast Taxonomy and Major Subtypes

entries.content:
Most werebeasts can develop three useful expressions. Human form is the stable base body and requires no transformation energy. Hybrid form blends human structure with lineage traits such as claws, fur, feathers, scales, altered eyes, ears, tails, wings, digitigrade legs, fangs, increased muscle, or specialized sensory organs. Beast form reorganizes the body into a complete supernatural version of the associated animal. Some powerful lineages develop an Apex or Primal form that is larger and more demanding than the ordinary beast state.

At Lunaris, transformation is taught as a physical process rather than stage magic. Bone, muscle, mass distribution, balance, skin, and sensory systems reorganize according to the supernatural template. Students learn in reinforced rooms with clear floor markings, stretch-safe uniforms, hydration stations, and observers trained to recognize distress. Early lessons focus on partial changes—eyes, hands, balance, hearing—before full shifts are attempted.

Triggers vary. Some students shift by choice, some react to strong emotion, some werewolves experience lunar pressure, and some cursed lineages have narrow involuntary triggers. The academy never assumes that one student’s experience defines the species. A transformation plan lists known triggers, safe exits, preferred anchors, and whether the student wants verbal coaching, quiet space, or a familiar peer nearby.

entries.name: 🐾 Werebeast Forms and Transformation

entries.content:
Werebeasts are living organisms whose human bodies contain a supernatural animal template. Even without shifting, that template can raise strength, reflexes, balance, smell, hearing, night vision, endurance, bone density, temperature tolerance, or other traits appropriate to the lineage. Full transformation multiplies some of those advantages while also changing metabolic demand. A student who can run for miles as a wolf or sustain a large bear form may need far more food and rest than their human appearance suggests.

Regeneration is common but not unlimited. Cuts, sprains, fractures, bruises, and many internal injuries can repair faster than in ordinary humans, especially after rest and adequate nutrition. Shifting sometimes assists recovery by rebuilding the body toward its stable template, but the school does not treat transformation as a substitute for medical care. Severe injuries, toxins, magical interference, exhaustion, or silver can slow the process substantially.

Lunaris meal planning accounts for high post-shift calorie needs. Carnivorous lineages often prefer protein and iron after training, while herbivore-aligned or omnivorous strains have different recovery foods. Students are not pressured into stereotyped diets; the infirmary and nutrition staff track what actually supports each body. Hunger is treated as a safety concern because depleted students can become irritable, unfocused, and harder to stabilize during transformation.

entries.content:
Werebeast instinct is an added layer of perception and impulse, not a replacement personality. Predator lineages may experience pursuit focus, chase responses, territorial awareness, or protective aggression. Herd-oriented lineages may become more group-conscious. Burrowing, nesting, denning, climbing, swimming, hoarding, migration, or high-place seeking can appear depending on the animal template. These behaviors can be subtle in human form and stronger while shifted.

Lunaris teaches students to identify instincts without treating them as commands. A chase impulse can be redirected into track practice. Territorial discomfort can be handled by establishing personal space and clear dorm boundaries. A student who becomes overwhelmed by smell or sound can use filters, quiet corridors, or scheduled decompression. Emotional regulation classes distinguish ordinary anger, panic, embarrassment, and excitement from supernatural amplification so students learn what is actually happening.

Sensory overload is especially common after a first shift or when a human-form student suddenly gains access to much stronger hearing or smell. Faculty reduce light, noise, crowding, and verbal demands rather than forcing the student to “tough it out.” The goal is to build tolerance gradually while preserving the useful information those senses provide.

entries.content:
Werebeasts can come from inherited lineages, permanent supernatural curses, ritual transformations, or infectious strains such as some forms of lycanthropy. Born werebeasts usually develop passive senses or instincts before complete shifting, giving families time to introduce control gradually. Newly changed students may instead encounter adult-level instincts and transformation demands very quickly, which is one reason Lunaris keeps a separate adjustment program for recent transformations.

Family heritage affects animal lineage, strength, magical traits, and cultural expectations, but it does not determine personality. Children from supernatural families may inherit an active werebeast template, dormant traits, or ordinary human biology. Mixed animal lineages usually express one dominant template rather than a chaotic physical blend, though rare magical variations exist. The academy records family history when useful for medicine and training but does not use lineage prestige in admissions or student status.

Werebeasts age normally through childhood and adolescence. Once the supernatural template stabilizes, regenerative biology often slows later physical decline and can support a longer healthy lifespan than an ordinary human, though werebeasts are not naturally immortal. Chronic silver exposure, repeated uncontrolled shifts, severe magical suppression, and constant overexertion can damage long-term health.

Coming-of-age traditions vary by family: first controlled shift, first solo run, a chosen animal-form name, a family meal, or simply completing a safety plan. Lunaris allows students to honor those traditions without forcing one clan’s custom on everyone else.

Werebeast culture is built around the idea that the animal form is genuinely part of the person. Healthy traditions ask how instinct can be integrated responsibly rather than how it can be erased. Different lineages produce different customs: pack-oriented students may value shared meals and group runs, solitary predators may guard personal space, bird lineages may think in routes and vantage points, and aquatic lineages may organize life around water access. Lunaris allows these differences without assuming every werebeast follows wolf culture.

Deliberately creating a new cursed or infectious werebeast is a serious responsibility. Territory does not grant ownership over other people. Young or newly changed shifters receive protection while learning. Sanctuary spaces such as schools, clinics, and emergency dens are protected. Beastweres are recognized as related reverse-shifters rather than animals to be hunted or owned.

The academy translates those old laws into modern policy. Students may not bait someone into transforming, use species slurs, steal adaptive clothing, hide silver in a prank, or expose a classmate online. Leadership challenges are handled through elections, supervised competitions, debate, or formal mediation rather than uncontrolled violence.

entries.content:
Heightened smell makes social space different for many werebeasts. Familiar people, recent stress, illness, fear, another shifter’s lineage, a recent transformation, and the difference between a resident and a visitor can often be detected through scent. These impressions are not perfect lie detectors and are never treated as permission to invade privacy. Perfume, weather, crowds, magic, illness, and deliberate masking can all interfere with scent.

Body language also carries extra information. Ears, tails, posture, shoulders, gaze, breathing, wing position, or the way a student places themselves near an exit can communicate comfort long before words do. Lunaris teaches mixed-species students enough of these signals to avoid obvious misunderstandings without turning classmates into biology lessons. A tucked tail, flattened ears, bristled fur, or rigid posture means “give space,” not “tease harder.”

Territory at school is translated into reasonable personal boundaries. Dorm rooms, beds, desks, lockers, favorite study corners, and club workspaces can acquire strong familiar scent and emotional association. Students may decorate or arrange those spaces in ways that help them feel secure, but they cannot claim common hallways or prevent others from using shared facilities.

The school’s sensory etiquette is simple: ask before touching, ask before moving someone’s belongings, and do not weaponize scent or sound to provoke a reaction. This makes old territorial instincts compatible with modern communal living.

Some rooms include window platforms, low den-like alcoves, or floor sleeping options according to student preference rather than species stereotype.

Adaptive uniforms use hidden expansion seams, breakaway panels, stretch enchantments, and replaceable fasteners. Students are encouraged to shift out of delicate clothing rather than destroy it repeatedly. Clothing rules are about safety and ordinary school appropriateness, not forcing one body shape to fit a rigid design.

Combat skills are optional parts of a broader curriculum and are taught under supervision rather than treated as the purpose of being a werebeast.

Contact severity varies by lineage, but silver can burn, interfere with regeneration, destabilize transformation, and make wounds heal slowly. Some lineages have additional plant, mineral, magical, or environmental vulnerabilities, and those are recorded privately in health plans.

They share the general werebeast traits of living biology, rapid healing, heightened senses, transformation, and silver sensitivity, while adding a particularly strong connection to lunar cycles, scent communication, endurance, pack resonance, and social stabilization.

Some can transform almost effortlessly at any phase of the moon, while others experience strong involuntary pressure during bright lunar nights. Full-moon influence can intensify instinct and physical output, but it does not automatically erase memory, ethics, or responsibility.

entries.content:
Werewolves commonly develop a human base form, a humanoid wolf form, a full quadrupedal wolf form, and in some powerful lines an Apex or Primal wolf expression. The humanoid form combines upright posture and hand use with fur, claws, fangs, digitigrade legs, enhanced musculature, wolf senses, and a heavier frame. The full wolf form favors running, tracking, scent work, and agile terrain movement. Primal expressions are larger and more demanding, so Lunaris restricts them to reinforced fields unless an emergency requires otherwise.

The supernatural structure linking those forms is commonly called the lunar core. It is not a literal organ visible on an X-ray; it is a magical-biological system connecting regeneration, transformation, wolf instinct, and lunar sensitivity. Damage from silver, wolfsbane, certain suppression spells, or severe exhaustion can disrupt the core and make shifting painful or unstable.

Students learn to read the lunar core indirectly through physical signs: rising body temperature, pressure behind the senses, stronger scent perception, restless legs, sharpened hearing, changes in appetite, or the feeling that a shift is “closer” than usual. New Moon instructors teach those signals before advanced combat or endurance work.

Around the new moon, raw output and regenerative speed are often lower while fine control and calm concentration are easier. Through the waxing phases, senses, physical energy, instinctive awareness, and transformation pressure gradually rise. The full moon produces the strongest combination of power, recovery, social resonance, restlessness, and desire for movement. The waning phase usually brings a noticeable release of pressure.

Some wolves experience a state traditionally called Howl Frenzy: not mindless rage, but an intense collection of impulses to run, howl, seek familiar company, defend territory, test strength, or remain outdoors. Students are taught to recognize the state early and choose safe outlets such as the Moonrun Trail, the Howling Fields, a supervised training block, quiet den space, or time with trusted friends. Rare curse strains can cause more severe involuntary transformations, and those students receive individualized medical plans.

Pack resonance carries broad impressions such as distress, injury, direction, nearness, calm, or collective urgency. It is not unrestricted telepathy. Specific thoughts, private memories, and secrets remain private unless another power is involved.

At Lunaris, pack resonance is treated carefully because teenage friendship groups do not automatically become formal packs. Students can be close without creating a supernatural bond, and no one may pressure another wolf into a ritual connection. Some family packs remain active across distance, some students form small campus packs, and others prefer to remain independent. Lone wolves are not considered defective.

New Moon’s full-moon support teams often pair inexperienced wolves with a trusted peer or staff mentor if the student requests it.

Howling is one way wolves synchronize emotion and location. The academy’s designated howl periods prevent a dorm-wide chorus from waking everyone at random, but spontaneous howls are not treated as shameful. The cultural rule is consideration: express wolf nature without making the entire campus absorb it at three in the morning.

entries.content:
Traditional werewolf culture often uses the words Alpha, Beta, Omega, and Lone Wolf, but Lunaris teaches them as social roles rather than biological castes. An Alpha is a recognized coordinator or protector, not a person magically entitled to command everyone nearby. Betas are trusted organizers, scouts, defenders, or second voices. Omegas traditionally serve as stabilizers, healers, mediators, and balance-keepers in some cultures. Lone Wolves live outside an active pack by choice or circumstance.

Modern packs vary widely. Some families keep ceremonial hierarchies. Others elect a leader for a limited term, share authority among adults, or only appoint a field leader during emergencies. School clubs and dorm groups are never allowed to imitate dominance systems that override ordinary student rights. A charismatic student can be influential, but they cannot claim authority over classmates because of scent, strength, age, or supernatural pressure.

Lunaris leadership courses deliberately challenge simplistic “strongest wolf wins” thinking. Students study mediation, logistics, first aid, planning, ethics, and the burden of being responsible for others. A leader who cannot listen or stop a fight is considered poorly trained no matter how physically powerful they are.

Independent wolves receive equal respect. Some students work better with a few close friends than a formal pack, and some need quiet after growing up under rigid family structures. The academy’s goal is healthy connection without compulsory hierarchy.

entries.content:
Werewolf traditions interpret the moon as both a biological influence and a cultural symbol. The White Moon represents clarity, restraint, healing, and harmony between human judgment and wolf instinct. The Crimson Moon represents intensity, courage, hunger, competition, and the need to direct strong emotion responsibly. The Eclipsed Moon represents contradiction, change, and the acceptance that identity can hold more than one form without becoming divided.

Lunaris adapts those older traditions into school-safe community rituals. Before a full-moon evening, students may attend the Moonrise Meal, a high-energy communal dinner. At dusk the Silver Bell sounds three times, marking the beginning of enhanced campus staffing. The optional Howl Circle gives wolves a place to vocalize together without turning the dorms into chaos. The supervised Moonrun opens later on approved trails. Students who prefer quiet can attend the White Moon Room for tea, music, stretching, and low-light relaxation.

No ritual requires a student to transform, howl, join a pack, or participate in spiritual language they do not share. The same event can be cultural for one student, practical for another, and simply enjoyable for a third. After sunrise, the Dawn Table provides breakfast and an informal check-in.

Rare eclipses and unusual lunar events are treated as special observances with extra safety planning, not excuses for reckless behavior. The tradition that matters most is preparation: know yourself, support your community, and greet the moon with intention instead of fear.

The student receives a private room, adaptive clothing, hydration and nutrition support, an instructor, and clear instructions about what sensations are normal. Friends may be present only if the student wants them there. No recordings are allowed. The goal is to make the first experience understandable and safe.

A newly turned student remains the same person. The bite does not transfer the source wolf’s personality, rank, memories, or ownership. New Moon is particularly firm on this point because folklore often confuses lineage with social control.

Protein, iron, fat, salt, fluids, and sufficient total calories matter more than performative ideas about what a wolf “should” eat. Raw food is not required, and Lunaris kitchens prioritize safe preparation. Students can choose ordinary cooked meals, high-protein snacks, vegetarian plans if compatible with their physiology, or medical nutrition support.

Sleep needs often shift with lunar phase. Some wolves become restless at night during bright phases and compensate with earlier sleep, quiet afternoon rest, or reduced evening workload. After intense shifting, deep sleep is common. The dorm system keeps blackout curtains, sound-dampened rooms, cooling blankets, and optional floor mats or den-like alcoves available.

Strong smell and hearing can make crowded hallways exhausting. Scent-free clinic hours, quiet lunch seating, noise filters, and outdoor routes help students regulate without isolating themselves. Faculty understand that overload can look like irritability or distraction before a student recognizes it.

Silver can interfere with regeneration and the lunar core, making even a minor wound slow to heal. Wolfsbane can cause pain, disorientation, weakened senses, impaired transformation, and serious illness depending on dose and strain. Because reactions vary, the academy treats both substances as controlled hazards rather than props for pranks.

Students are taught what exposure feels like and when to seek help. Unauthorized silver blades, silver dust, concentrated wolfsbane, and anti-shifting restraints are prohibited in dorms and clubs. Science classes may use sealed samples under instructor supervision. Medical staff keep counteragents and extraction equipment in the Silverwing Infirmary.

New-moon conditions can reduce maximum power and healing speed without making wolves helpless. Shape-binding magic, exhaustion, deprivation, and forced transformation can also create dangerous weakness. The school’s safety curriculum focuses on prevention and escape rather than teaching students to obsess over how to harm each other.

entries.name: 🌑 Werewolf Weaknesses and Safety

entries.content:
Modern werewolf life is a constant exercise in switching between environments. Inside Lunaris, wolf traits can be openly accommodated. Students can use scent-friendly outdoor routes, reinforced gyms, adaptive clothing, moon-cycle schedules, and designated areas for howling or shifting. In Pineharbor, the same student may need to appear completely ordinary, ride a bus, order food, browse a store, and ignore a scent trail that would be effortless to follow in the woods.

The school trains practical skills: maintaining a normal speaking volume when hearing is sharpened, not reacting visibly to distant sounds no human should notice, planning meals before a long outing, carrying spare clothing, recognizing when the moon phase will make a late return difficult, and knowing how to explain a minor unusual behavior without inventing elaborate lies. Students are encouraged to use simple cover stories and leave rather than improvise dramatic excuses.

Because it stays closer to the true template, a trait guise often lasts longer than a perfect human appearance.

Duration depends on age, health, magical strength, practice, body-size difference, stress, injury, and how much detail the student is trying to maintain. A trained Beastwere may remain human for hours. A beginner may have only a short window. Memory remains continuous, but balance, appetite, vocal habits, and sensory priorities can feel different in a human body.

This distinction shapes identity. A raven Beastwere who spent childhood flying and perceiving distance from above does not suddenly lose those habits because a human guise provides feet and hands. A feline Beastwere may still prefer quiet elevated spaces. A canid may orient strongly to scent and group position. A rabbit-based student may notice exits and sudden movement automatically. These are not proof that the student is less intelligent; they are the normal result of developing through another species’ body.

Lunaris medical records therefore list true-form biology first and transformed-body notes second. Medication, diet, temperature, and injury assessment can differ between forms. A dose appropriate to a human-sized guise may not be appropriate after reversion.

entries.content:

A lynx may develop balance and spatial judgment.

Transformation adds a second kind of flexibility. Human guise allows speech, tool use, writing, public travel, and participation in spaces built for people. True form can pass through environments where a human would be conspicuous. Lunaris treats this observational advantage ethically: students may not use animal form to spy in bedrooms, clinics, private meetings, exams, or other protected spaces. Personhood brings ordinary privacy responsibilities even when the body is small enough to go unnoticed.

Kaelen Wildshade produces foxfire illusions, Selar Emberpaw uses shadow camouflage, and other Beastweres may develop memory echoes, silence fields, pathfinding, luck-sense, or other gifts. Two members of the same animal species can therefore have very different supernatural talents.

entries.content:
Beastwere humanoid forms consume a finite transformation reserve. The more radical the change from the true animal body, the more energy it usually costs. Full human imitation requires restructuring scale, skeleton, musculature, hands, face, voice, gait, and mass distribution, while a trait guise can preserve more of the original template and remain stable longer.

The reserve behaves more like stamina than a battery with a universal number. Stress, hunger, illness, injury, silver, magical suppression, lack of sleep, and repeated transformations can shorten the remaining duration. Students learn personal warning signs: altered eye color, returning ears or tail, claws replacing nails, speech becoming difficult, balance shifting, or a sudden drop in body temperature. Those signs are a cue to move to a safe area and revert deliberately.

Forced reversion is not failure. It is the biological fail-safe that returns the person to the body requiring no transformation energy. The danger comes from environment: a small animal may suddenly lose hands, a bird may be unable to carry a backpack, or a large cat may alarm an unprepared civilian. Lunaris keeps form-safe rooms, labeled storage, and peer assistance procedures for exactly that reason.

entries.content:

The Law of the Guise permits human appearance for ordinary secrecy and daily life while prohibiting harmful impersonation or identity theft. The Law of Shelter requires safe places where an exhausted Beastwere can revert without becoming vulnerable.

No one may photograph a true-form student for social media simply because the animal body looks cute or unusual. A teacher cannot require a human guise when the task can reasonably be completed in another way. Emergency responders check for identification charms before assuming an animal on campus is non-sapient wildlife.

The academy also enforces the Law of Capture: intentionally trapping a Beastwere in true form to control, sell, experiment on, or exploit them is a severe offense. Shape-binding magic receives the same caution as physical restraint.

Rights are paired with responsibility. Beastweres must follow the same privacy, property, academic honesty, and secrecy rules as everyone else. Small size or unnoticed animal form is never an excuse for trespassing.

entries.name: 🔮 Humans with Powers — Core Definition

entries.content:
Powered human abilities have many origins. Some students come from families in which a particular elemental or psychic gift appears across generations. Others awaken unpredictably during adolescence. Some develop magic through disciplined study after discovering sensitivity to supernatural energy. A few gain permanent abilities through unusual events, enchanted artifacts, dimensional exposure, or contact with powers that changed them without making them a different species.

Lunaris uses functional categories for scheduling rather than rigid labels. Projection powers send energy or matter outward. Manipulation powers control an existing element or force. Internal enhancement changes the user’s own body without creating a werebeast form. Perception powers gather information through dreams, emotion, memory, or distant sensing. Construction powers create barriers, tools, summons, or devices. Mobility powers alter movement through portals, gravity, teleportation, or air control. Support powers heal, stabilize, protect, or enhance others.

A single student may cross categories. Theo’s magitech combines construction, enchantment, and engineering. Cassia’s Dreamweaving mixes perception, emotional influence, and controlled dream-space alteration. Faculty care less about naming the perfect category than understanding triggers, range, limits, recovery, and failure conditions.

This makes honesty useful: students are more likely to admit that an ability feels wrong when asking for help does not automatically mean punishment.

entries.content:
Humans with powers occupy a distinct place at Lunaris because they can often pass through mundane society without visible transformation while still carrying abilities that could expose the hidden world instantly. They may also be physically less durable than large werebeasts or lack a Beastwere’s alternate body. The academy answers that difference with training and design rather than ranking.

Mixed teams are standard. A werebear can provide physical protection while a human force-field user covers distance. A Beastwere scout can find a route while a portal user moves the group. A dreamweaver can calm sleep after a difficult full moon while a werewolf mentor provides familiar grounding. Each student is expected to understand what they contribute and where they should not pretend to be invulnerable.

School culture pushes back against two stereotypes: that powered humans are fragile “normal people,” and that they are automatically smarter or more civilized than shifters. Both ideas are considered lazy. Individual ability, judgment, experience, and character matter more than race.

Town outings require particular restraint because a human-looking student can be tempted to use small powers casually. Telekinetically grabbing a dropped phone may seem harmless until someone notices it crossed six feet of air. New Moon teaches subtlety, cover habits, and the confidence to solve ordinary problems in ordinary ways when secrecy requires it.

These practices also support the academy’s central secrecy rule. Students are free to be themselves on protected grounds, but they learn how to move through the mundane world without exposing classmates or frightening unprepared civilians. That means planning clothing, transportation, power use, scent or sound control, and emergency exits before town trips. Secrecy is taught as community protection rather than shame: the hidden world remains hidden so young people can learn safely and ordinary humans in Pineharbor can continue their lives without being pulled into supernatural conflicts they do not understand.

At Lunaris Academy: New Moon, this subject is treated as part of ordinary student life rather than a spectacle. Faculty expect students to understand what their bodies and abilities are doing, communicate when they need help, and use the school’s accommodations before a manageable problem turns into a crisis. The academy keeps practical supplies, quiet rooms, reinforced practice areas, flexible meal options, and trained staff available so that different species can function together without anyone being treated as dangerous merely for existing. Older students are encouraged to model calm, responsible behavior for younger classmates, while teachers distinguish between an involuntary symptom and a deliberate harmful choice.

entries.content:
## Moonspire Hall

Moonspire Hall is the architectural heart of Lunaris Academy: New Moon, a broad stone-and-glass academic building raised around the academy's original moonstone tower. Older arches, carved lunar symbols, and thick timber coexist with elevators, accessible ramps, digital noticeboards, warded Wi-Fi equipment, and modern classrooms. The building holds administration, major lecture rooms, staff offices, counseling spaces, and several shared study lounges, making it the place almost every student crosses several times a day.

**Layout and atmosphere:** The central atrium rises three stories beneath a circular skylight. Two academic wings spread east and west, while the older tower contains the headmistress's office, records archive, faculty conference rooms, and the protected ward controls. Wide corridors include recessed alcoves for students whose wings, tails, large bodies, mobility aids, or sensory needs make narrow passing periods difficult.

**Daily use:** Morning announcements appear on enchanted displays and ordinary school tablets. Students meet tutors between classes, argue over group projects in the atrium, wait outside the dean's office, and gather under the skylight when rain makes the outdoor courtyards impractical. The building is deliberately mundane enough to feel like a real school despite its old supernatural architecture.

**Safety and accommodations:** Structural wards limit destructive power use without suppressing harmless traits. Emergency shutters can isolate a damaged hallway, but there are no cage-like containment rooms. Scent-neutral ventilation, low-light routes, reinforced floors, and several quiet rooms allow mixed species to use the hall without being forced into a single body plan.

**Role in academy life:** Moonspire is the academy's crossroads. Formal decisions happen here, but so do lost homework, hallway gossip, club posters, awkward apologies, hurried breakfasts, and students racing a bell. The New Moon Charter is engraved beside the atrium stairs as a reminder that the school exists to educate and protect rather than control.

The academy’s culture emphasizes personhood and consent. No student is permitted to touch another person’s ears, tail, wings, fur, transformed body, magical focus, or personal equipment without permission. Recording another student during a transformation, medical episode, loss of power control, or vulnerable true-form moment is a serious privacy violation. Jokes are tolerated when everyone involved is laughing; humiliation, species stereotyping, coercion, and baiting someone into a shift are not. The result is a campus where unusual biology can be openly accommodated inside the wards even though it must remain hidden from the nearby mundane town.
entries.name: 📍 Moonspire Hall

entries.content:
## The Den Commons

The Den Commons is the social heart of Lunaris Academy and the place where a normal school day most visibly begins. It occupies a broad, warm hall between the Twilight Dormitories and the central academic paths, close enough that half-awake students can reach it without crossing the entire campus. The room's centerpiece is an enchanted hearth whose steady **silver flame** gives off controlled warmth without sparks, smoke, or dangerous heat. Old Lunaris tradition treats the flame as a symbol of unity: three very different student populations sharing one room without needing to become alike.

**Layout and breakfast use:** Long communal tables occupy the dining side of the hall in the morning, while reinforced couches, deep cushions, low platforms, window seats, and open floor areas form the lounge side. Serving counters connect to Moonstone Dining Hall's kitchens, so breakfast spills naturally into the Commons rather than forcing everyone into a formal cafeteria atmosphere. Tables can adjust in height and spacing for wheelchairs, large transformed bodies, true-form Beastweres, and ordinary student groups. A kitchenette, water stations, charging lockers, noticeboards, games shelves, and two quiet side rooms keep the space useful after breakfast service ends.

**Daily rhythm:** Between roughly 6:30 and 8:00 a.m., the Den is loud with trays, homework panic, club announcements, last-minute tutoring, and arguments about who used the last clean mug. Werebeasts with high metabolic needs can choose substantial protein-rich meals; students such as Luna and Finn often prefer fruit, vegetables, breads, or lighter dishes; powered humans choose from the same broad menu according to individual needs rather than species stereotypes. Evelyn is frequently seen with warm tea, Theo with something portable because he overslept, and full-moon mornings bring extra recovery food for anyone who spent the night training or shifting.

After classes the furniture becomes primarily social. Students plan Moonlit Challenges, work on group projects, rehearse club ideas, watch films, play games, celebrate birthdays, or simply exist near other people. Beastweres may relax in true form without being treated as pets or curiosities. Rough shifting, combat practice, intrusive scent-marking, coercive magic, and uncontrolled power demonstrations stay out of the main lounge; a marked hobby area permits harmless fine-control practice.

The Den matters because most coexistence at Lunaris is mundane. A student learns another species' boundaries by sharing breakfast, saving a seat, moving a bag from a tail-safe walkway, or discovering that someone needs quiet after a difficult shift. Faculty deliberately avoid overprogramming the room. It belongs to student life first. Many of Lunaris's strongest friendships begin not during a grand ritual, but while someone is eating cereal at an unreasonable hour under the silver flame.
entries.name: 📍 The Den Commons

entries.content:
## Moonlit Library and the Historic Fang Wing

The **Moonlit Library** is Lunaris Academy's central scholarly space: a vast stone-and-timber library whose vaulted ceilings glow with soft silver light after sunset. It is quieter than the Den Commons but almost as social. Study tables cluster beneath high windows, movable partitions create group rooms, and shelves stretch through several connected wings holding ordinary textbooks beside magical histories, field journals, grimoires, maps, supernatural law, literature, science, and carefully controlled rare works.

The oldest section is still known as the **Fang Library**, the name used for Lunaris's original major archive. Rather than replacing it, New Moon incorporated the historic stackhouse into the modern library. Fang shelves were designed to adapt to very different users: some lower or widen for small or true-form students; reading stands can hold books open for paws or claws; voice-index stations assist students who cannot easily manipulate paper; and reinforced aisles accommodate larger werebeast bodies. Modern accessibility tools—scanners, tablets, audio editions, magnification, tactile labels, and secure digital catalogues—operate beside enchanted shelving.

The library's magic is useful but not omniscient. Some old books whisper a requested passage when opened correctly, reveal hidden annotations under moonlight, translate obsolete script imperfectly, or rearrange indexes when a subject changes. Students are taught source criticism because an enchanted book can still be biased, mistaken, outdated, or dramatic. Evelyn is famous for cross-referencing old texts rather than trusting them. Theo uses technical archives, Cassia and Rhea work near the dream and astral collections, and many werebeast students research lineage without being told that ancestry determines personality.

Deep within the Fang Wing lies the secured **Moonlit Archives**, a separate historical collection with its own entry and access rules. Rare transformation records, early Lunaris charters, old lunar observations, and dangerous or fragile works are not casually circulated. The Archives' full-moon association comes from old lunar locking wards, not from a rule that knowledge should be inaccessible most of the month.

Day to day, the Moonlit Library supports tutoring, quiet club meetings, independent study, detention-by-research, exam panic, and ordinary reading. Conversation is allowed in marked collaboration zones; the central stacks remain quiet. Strong scents, uncontrolled heat, wet transformed bodies, and damaging magic are kept away from collections, while drying rooms and form-safe reading spaces make those rules practical rather than exclusionary.

The library embodies New Moon's relationship with the school's past. Old Lunaris knowledge is preserved, but it is catalogued, questioned, made accessible, and taught alongside modern scholarship. A whispered medieval grimoire and a current digital ethics text may sit only a corridor apart because students are expected to understand both.
entries.name: 📍 Moonlit Library

entries.content:
## Twilight Dormitories and the Legacy Sanctuary Wings

The **Twilight Dormitories** are Lunaris Academy's main student residence complex, a collection of connected stone-and-timber houses set just beyond the busiest academic paths. Gentle enchanted moonlight brightens corridors at night without replacing ordinary lamps, and the buildings use modern fire safety, secure access, Wi-Fi, laundry rooms, shared kitchens, lounges, study rooms, and accessible bathrooms alongside supernatural accommodations.

Older records call these buildings the **Sanctuary Dorms**. In that era, residence wings were divided primarily by species—human, werebeast, and hybrid or other supernatural categories. New Moon kept the buildings but rejected compulsory species segregation. The old wings now function as mixed residence houses, and rooms are assigned around age, compatibility, accessibility, sleep needs, sensory requirements, medical considerations, and student preference. A werewolf does not automatically room with another werewolf; a Beastwere is not placed somewhere merely because staff consider the space animal-safe.

Rooms are built for personal life rather than containment. Standard rooms include beds, desks, wardrobes, charging points, storage, and enough clearance for safe partial transformation. Some have widened doors, reinforced flooring, high perches, low sleeping platforms, waterproof sections, blackout curtains, temperature control, or secure true-form resting areas. Beastweres can live in their natural bodies and are given storage for humanoid clothing rather than being expected to maintain a guise after curfew. Werebeasts keep adaptive clothing and shift kits nearby. Powered humans can request grounded outlets, heat-safe surfaces, sound dampening, or other power-specific modifications.

Dorm culture is ordinary and messy: alarms, roommate negotiations, laundry disputes, borrowed chargers, exam-night snacks, music through walls, homesickness, private jokes, and the occasional student sprinting toward breakfast with one shoe. Quiet hours protect sleep but are flexible around approved full-moon schedules and medical recovery. Shifting in hallways, intimidation by size or scent, entering another room without permission, hidden recording, and using powers on roommates are treated seriously.

House advisers live nearby, but students retain privacy. Staff enter rooms for emergencies, safety inspections, or clearly announced maintenance rather than constant surveillance. Low-sensory lounges and private regulation rooms are available when social spaces become too much.

Twilight is where New Moon's reform becomes most personal. The academy once tried to make students feel safe by separating difference. It now aims for a harder form of safety: letting students live together while giving every body enough room, every person clear boundaries, and everyone somewhere they can close a door and simply be off duty.
entries.name: 📍 Twilight Dormitories

entries.content:
## Wildering Woods

The **Wildering Woods** are the managed inner preserve of Moonshadow Forest immediately surrounding Lunaris Academy. They are not the whole forest and they are not an unregulated wilderness. Marked trails, transformation clearings, ecology plots, emergency beacons, lesson zones, and supervised night routes wind through ancient trees, glowing plants, streams, mossy stone, and patches of old lunar magic. Beyond the managed boundary, deeper Moonshadow territory becomes increasingly restricted.

By day the woods function as an outdoor classroom. Beast Mastery students track, navigate, study habitats, and practice true-form movement; Transformation Studies uses secluded clearings for controlled shifts; Herbology and Herbal Alchemy identify plants without stripping the landscape; survival classes teach weather, orientation, and first aid; and ordinary students walk the trails simply because the forest is beautiful. Faculty distinguish responsible tracking and ecological observation from harming wildlife. Hunting live animals is not a school exercise.

At night the atmosphere changes without becoming inherently dangerous. Moonlit paths brighten, nocturnal creatures become active, and approved routes open for the Wild Run Club, lunar observation, quiet walks, and supervised werebeast or Beastwere exercise. Mira, Zeke, Esme, Finn, and other students often use these routes in very different ways: running, flying, tracking, meditating, or moving through a form that feels more comfortable outside than in a building. Human students can join with normal equipment or approved mobility and safety enchantments; nobody needs an artificial animal form to participate.

The woods contain several important sublocations. The Lunar Grove lies in a protected clearing where natural lunar currents are unusually stable. Eclipse Caverns open beneath a rocky ridge. Howling Fields and Moonrun Trail sit closer to campus for high-energy exercise. Hidden historical markers, old foundations, and magical plant colonies provide endless rumors, but students are expected to obey closure signs even when a rumor claims a shortcut is 'secret.'

Safety systems remain deliberately unobtrusive. Trail markers use visual, tactile, scent-safe, and magical cues. Locator devices are required for certain night events, and staff can close sections for weather, magical instability, nesting wildlife, or full-moon crowd control. Emergency shelters contain water, blankets, first aid, adaptive clothing, and communication charms.

Wildering Woods represents the academy's belief that instinct and nature do not need to be suppressed to be responsible. Students are given room to run, climb, fly, transform, explore, and be quiet—but also taught that freedom in a living forest carries duties to classmates, wildlife, boundaries, and the land itself.

entries.content:
## New Moon Training Grounds and the Historic Beastborne Arena

The **New Moon Training Grounds** form Lunaris Academy's main complex for physical education, controlled combat, rescue practice, transformation movement, and high-output power training. The oldest open-air ring at its center is still called the **Beastborne Arena**, preserving the name of Lunaris's original large training ground. New Moon expanded around it rather than replacing it.

The Beastborne Arena is broad, open to the sky, and surrounded by magically reinforced boundaries designed to absorb impacts, redirect stray energy, and open immediately for emergency access. Its floor can change between packed earth, grass, padded mat, sand, shallow water channels, and obstacle layouts. Adjacent zones include sparring circles, climbing structures, sprint lanes, aerial markers, archery ranges, rescue rubble, enchanted practice dummies, and power-testing stations. Larger transformed students have adequate turning radius, while human-scale technical drills occur in separated lanes.

**Instructional philosophy:** Alistair Valerius's Combat Training classes treat strategy, restraint, and respect as equal to power. Every formal bout starts and ends with acknowledgement of the opponent. Students learn hand-to-hand fundamentals, defensive positioning, magical shields, archery or weapon safety where appropriate, team tactics, and how to stop when conditions change. The advanced Feral Combat Training track uses full transformed movement and higher-output abilities but remains nonlethal and heavily supervised.

Werebeasts do not automatically dominate every exercise. A bear form may excel at load-bearing while a powered human controls terrain, a Beastwere scouts a route, and an unpowered technique solves the actual objective. Many scenarios reward rescue, evacuation, protection, communication, or reaching a checkpoint with the whole team. Raw damage scores are rarely the point.

The Arena is also a social landmark. Famous friendly rivalries develop here, club exhibitions draw spectators, and Moonlit Challenge practice often begins on its field. Jace enjoys demonstration bouts, Zeke brings spectacular fire discipline drills, Evelyn builds defensive ice structures, Kaelen uses misdirection, and students such as Selene may participate as support observers during transformation-heavy exercises.

Rules are strict: no surprise attacks outside marked drills, no coercive powers, no targeting known medical vulnerabilities, no forcing transformations, no continuing after a stop signal, and no public humiliation as training. Adaptive protective equipment is available for claws, wings, horns, tails, unusual temperatures, and sensory needs.

The Beastborne name survives because Lunaris respects its history. The training philosophy changed. New Moon no longer asks which species is strongest; it asks whether a student can use what they have deliberately, safely, and in cooperation with people whose abilities work differently.

## Lunar Observatory

The Lunar Observatory crowns a low hill north of Moonspire Hall and serves both scientific astronomy and supernatural lunar study. Its silver dome is visible from most of campus but kept below the tree line from distant Pineharbor roads.

**Layout and atmosphere:** Inside are two telescope domes, a planetarium classroom, rooftop observation deck, data lab, small weather station, and circular seminar room used by Seraphina. One telescope is entirely mundane and research-grade; the other can measure certain magical light signatures without pretending they replace astronomy.

**Daily use:** The Astronomy Club gathers here weekly, werewolf students chart personal lunar responses, and classes compare folklore with observed cycles. Cassia sometimes assists dream studies during meteor showers, while ordinary students simply come to see Saturn's rings or photograph an eclipse.

**Safety and accommodations:** The roof has wind barriers, harness anchors, low-light pathways, and flight-safe approach markers. During intense lunar events, attendance is voluntary; students who find the moon overstimulating can use interior filtered windows or receive the same lesson through recorded telescope data without being recorded themselves.

**Role in academy life:** The observatory keeps Lunaris from reducing the moon to werewolf symbolism. It is a real celestial body, a cultural symbol, a magical influence for some beings, and a source of beauty for anyone who wants to look up.

The academy’s culture emphasizes personhood and consent. No student is permitted to touch another person’s ears, tail, wings, fur, transformed body, magical focus, or personal equipment without permission. Recording another student during a transformation, medical episode, loss of power control, or vulnerable true-form moment is a serious privacy violation. Jokes are tolerated when everyone involved is laughing; humiliation, species stereotyping, coercion, and baiting someone into a shift are not. The result is a campus where unusual biology can be openly accommodated inside the wards even though it must remain hidden from the nearby mundane town.

Training is built around repeatable control rather than dramatic displays. Students are taught to notice early warning signs, name what they are experiencing, choose an appropriate response, and recover properly afterward. Faculty use observation notes, self-reports, fitness data, magical readings, and peer teamwork to help students improve without turning every difficulty into punishment. Progress can mean a stronger ability, but it can also mean stopping on time, asking for assistance, recovering faster, or recognizing that a stressful day is not the right time to push a limit.
