## Silverwing Infirmary

Silverwing Infirmary is Lunaris's modern medical center under Dr. Marcus Greystone. It was built specifically to avoid the old supernatural-school habit of treating every unusual body state as either an emergency or a discipline problem.

**Layout and atmosphere:** The front resembles a small contemporary clinic with exam rooms, laboratory, medication storage, counseling nook, physical-therapy room, and observation bays. Deeper rooms include reinforced but welcoming recovery suites, low-light rooms, scent-controlled spaces, floor-level Beastwere stations, heated pads, wing-clear rooms, and transformation-safe showers.

**Daily use:** Students visit for colds, sprains, headaches, power exhaustion, transformation soreness, sensory overload, sleep trouble, medication, and ordinary health questions. Full-moon mornings bring hydration stations and large breakfasts rather than automatic examinations. Greystone coordinates with outside specialists through secure hidden-community networks when school care is insufficient.

**Safety and accommodations:** Medical care follows consent and privacy rules except where immediate danger requires emergency intervention. Silver, wolfsbane, power suppressants, and other species-specific agents are controlled like hazardous medicines, never classroom props or punishments. Records are not shared with coaches, classmates, or town contacts without proper reason.

**Role in academy life:** The infirmary makes supernatural health routine. It supports dramatic emergencies when needed, but it is equally useful for a student asking whether a new symptom is normal, getting a brace adjusted, or napping safely after an exhausting practical class.

Training is built around repeatable control rather than dramatic displays. Students are taught to notice early warning signs, name what they are experiencing, choose an appropriate response, and recover properly afterward. Faculty use observation notes, self-reports, fitness data, magical readings, and peer teamwork to help students improve without turning every difficulty into punishment. Progress can mean a stronger ability, but it can also mean stopping on time, asking for assistance, recovering faster, or recognizing that a stressful day is not the right time to push a limit.

Because Lunaris is a mixed community, no single species is treated as the default. Architecture, schedules, meals, uniforms, sports, clubs, and dorm policies are designed around overlapping needs. Werebeasts may need space to shift, Beastweres may need secure true-form areas, and powered humans may require grounding equipment or power-safe workstations. Students learn each other’s boundaries through ordinary friendship and cooperation, which is one reason cross-species teams are common in classes and school events.

## Transformation Pavilion

The Transformation Pavilion is a purpose-built instructional building for werebeasts and any student whose body changes substantially. It replaces old locked shift rooms with open, supervised spaces designed around voluntary practice and rapid recovery.

Side studios allow private or small-group work. Lockers contain stretch-safe uniforms, blankets, towels, hydration supplies, grooming kits, and repair materials for ordinary clothing mishaps.

**Daily use:** Lyra Silvermane teaches form transitions, partial shifts, sensory pacing, and recovery here. Students practice noticing early signs rather than waiting for loss of control. Lessons may involve changing only hands, eyes, balance, stance, or scent response before attempting larger forms.

Staff can clear adjacent areas, lower stimulation, and call medical support. Observation is opt-in outside formal instruction, and no transformation practice may be photographed without explicit permission.

**Role in academy life:** This building represents one of New Moon's clearest changes: transformation is treated as a teachable body skill, not a shameful spectacle. It is where frightening first experiences often become ordinary competencies.

## Applied Powers Laboratory

The Applied Powers Laboratory gives powered human students and other ability users a dedicated equivalent to Transformation Studies. It looks more like a flexible science lab than a mystical chamber because the goal is to measure how an ability behaves under repeatable conditions.

**Layout and atmosphere:** Movable workstations contain range markers, thermal cameras, inert target blocks, pressure sensors, insulated panels, light meters, sound meters, safe grounding grids, and enchantment-compatible computers. Adjacent rooms specialize in telekinesis, portals, energy projection, psychic-safe exercises, and low-stimulation control work.

**Daily use:** Students map triggers, range, duration, recovery time, environmental interactions, and warning signs. Evelyn can chart temperature falloff, Owen can measure gravity gradients, Maya can test portal alignment, and Julian can monitor shield load. Results become personal control plans rather than rankings.

No teacher intentionally provokes fear, anger, pain, or humiliation merely to force a power response.

**Role in academy life:** The lab establishes that powered humans deserve structured ability education instead of being told to 'be careful.' It also gives students a believable place for experimentation, projects, failures, breakthroughs, and collaborative problem solving.

## Moonglass Greenhouses

The Moonglass Greenhouses are Calypso Willowbark's linked glasshouses and outdoor medicinal gardens. Their silver-tinted panels regulate magical radiation while modern irrigation, climate sensors, and ordinary horticultural equipment keep the facility practical.

**Layout and atmosphere:** Separate bays hold mundane medicinal plants, magical herbs, cold-loving specimens, tropical growth, nocturnal flowers, and restricted hazardous species. A central potting classroom connects to an alchemy prep lab, seed library, compost station, and wash area.

**Daily use:** Herbology classes, the Herbology Society, infirmary supply work, and student gardening all happen here. Sienna helps with plant-sense projects; quieter students often volunteer because repetitive watering and repotting are calming. Seasonal produce occasionally reaches the dining hall.

**Safety and accommodations:** Hazardous plants remain labeled and secured; gloves, eye protection, allergy records, and cross-species toxicity charts are standard. Students are taught that 'natural' does not mean safe and that magical ingredients are not automatically appropriate for every physiology.

**Role in academy life:** The greenhouses provide a softer form of supernatural wonder. They support healing plots, mysteries, practical coursework, friendship scenes, and the mundane crisis of realizing an entire tray of seedlings was overwatered.

At Lunaris Academy: New Moon, this subject is treated as part of ordinary student life rather than a spectacle. Faculty expect students to understand what their bodies and abilities are doing, communicate when they need help, and use the school’s accommodations before a manageable problem turns into a crisis. Supernatural traits simply change how those routines are managed. A student with heightened hearing may use dampening earbuds; a shifter may keep spare adaptive clothing in a locker; a powered human may sign out a practice room before testing a new technique. These small habits are considered signs of maturity because Lunaris values preparation over bravado.

## Lake Lunara

Lake Lunara is a deep freshwater lake entirely inside the academy's concealment boundary. It predates the school and reflects the moon so clearly that generations of students have attached stories to it, though faculty discourage treating every ripple as prophecy.

**Layout and atmosphere:** A maintained shore includes a boathouse, docks, swimming area, canoe racks, emergency shed, picnic lawn, and a quieter reed-filled conservation zone. A broad path circles most of the lake and connects with the Wildering Woods trail network.

**Daily use:** Students swim, paddle, sketch, study water magic, hold picnics, and watch meteor showers here. Nessa is especially at home around the water, while clubs use the docks for photography or nature observation. Winter access changes according to actual ice safety rather than magical confidence.

**Safety and accommodations:** Swimming requires posted supervision times for younger students, and ability use that changes currents, temperature, gravity, or visibility is restricted to lessons. Flight, diving, and transformed swimming have separate zones when needed. The conservation shore remains off-limits during nesting periods.

**Role in academy life:** Lake Lunara creates breathing room in the setting. It can host celebrations or tense midnight conversations, but most days it is simply where students go when they want water, sky, and distance from homework.

## Moonwell Courtyard

Moonwell Courtyard sits between Moonspire Hall and the library, centered on a circular stone fountain fed by an underground spring. The 'well' is historically ceremonial rather than a source of limitless magic, and New Moon deliberately keeps it as a shared civic space.

**Layout and atmosphere:** Arcaded walkways frame trees, benches, café tables, bike racks, and a shallow moon-shaped water channel. The central fountain carries plaques naming major school reforms and graduating classes rather than powerful family bloodlines.

**Daily use:** Lunch spills into the courtyard in good weather. Clubs recruit here, student council posts announcements, musicians perform small sets, and faculty hold outdoor tutorials. On new-moon evenings lanterns replace bright overhead lights and give the space its signature soft glow.

**Safety and accommodations:** The fountain is protected against contamination and unsafe spell use, pathways are non-slip, and open sight lines make it easy for staff to supervise without hovering. Quiet corners exist beneath the arcades, but nobody is trapped behind blind walls.

**Role in academy life:** This is Lunaris's public square: a stage for announcements, friendships, demonstrations, apologies, festival decorations, and the everyday visual identity of New Moon.

The academy’s culture emphasizes personhood and consent. No student is permitted to touch another person’s ears, tail, wings, fur, transformed body, magical focus, or personal equipment without permission. Recording another student during a transformation, medical episode, loss of power control, or vulnerable true-form moment is a serious privacy violation. Jokes are tolerated when everyone involved is laughing; humiliation, species stereotyping, coercion, and baiting someone into a shift are not. The result is a campus where unusual biology can be openly accommodated inside the wards even though it must remain hidden from the nearby mundane town.

Training is built around repeatable control rather than dramatic displays. Students are taught to notice early warning signs, name what they are experiencing, choose an appropriate response, and recover properly afterward. Faculty use observation notes, self-reports, fitness data, magical readings, and peer teamwork to help students improve without turning every difficulty into punishment. Progress can mean a stronger ability, but it can also mean stopping on time, asking for assistance, recovering faster, or recognizing that a stressful day is not the right time to push a limit.

## Emberworks Workshop

Emberworks Workshop is Silas Emberfall's combined enchantment studio, fabrication lab, electronics bench, and repair shop. It smells faintly of metal, wood, solder, ink, and whatever harmless experiment Theo started five minutes ago.

**Layout and atmosphere:** Long benches are divided into runic carving, electronics, textiles, light fabrication, and magical-material stations. Locking storage holds hazardous components. A glass-walled testing cage contains device effects without isolating the student operating controls from outside supervision.

**Daily use:** Enchantment classes meet here, as do the Magitech and Robotics Club and many independent projects. Students repair dorm objects, build accessibility tools, prototype ward sensors, or create festival decorations. Theo spends enough time here that Silas has assigned him a labeled bin titled 'Things You Are Not Taking Apart.'

**Safety and accommodations:** Every active project must have a visible shutdown method, owner label, and explanation of what data it collects. Surveillance devices, coercive enchantments, and unconsented tracking are banned. Fire suppression handles both mundane and magical ignition.

**Role in academy life:** The workshop turns supernatural capability into craft. It is ideal for collaborative scenes because a brilliant idea still requires screws, measurements, debugging, cleanup, and someone remembering where the spare cable went.

Training is built around repeatable control rather than dramatic displays. Students are taught to notice early warning signs, name what they are experiencing, choose an appropriate response, and recover properly afterward. Faculty use observation notes, self-reports, fitness data, magical readings, and peer teamwork to help students improve without turning every difficulty into punishment. Progress can mean a stronger ability, but it can also mean stopping on time, asking for assistance, recovering faster, or recognizing that a stressful day is not the right time to push a limit.

Because Lunaris is a mixed community, no single species is treated as the default. Architecture, schedules, meals, uniforms, sports, clubs, and dorm policies are designed around overlapping needs. Werebeasts may need space to shift, Beastweres may need secure true-form areas, and powered humans may require grounding equipment or power-safe workstations. Students learn each other’s boundaries through ordinary friendship and cooperation, which is one reason cross-species teams are common in classes and school events.

These practices also support the academy’s central secrecy rule. Students are free to be themselves on protected grounds, but they learn how to move through the mundane world without exposing classmates or frightening unprepared civilians. That means planning clothing, transportation, power use, scent or sound control, and emergency exits before town trips. Secrecy is taught as community protection rather than shame: the hidden world remains hidden so young people can learn safely and ordinary humans in Pineharbor can continue their lives without being pulled into supernatural conflicts they do not understand.

## Dreamglass Arts Wing

The Dreamglass Arts Wing combines visual art, drama rehearsal, dance, costume work, and supervised illusion-friendly performance spaces. Its name comes from translucent interior panels that scatter moonlight into soft colors without actually showing anyone's dreams.

**Layout and atmosphere:** Studios include painting and sculpture rooms, black-box theater, costume shop, rehearsal hall, ceramics room, digital media lab, and soundproof music practice booths. Furniture can be moved for tails, wings, quadrupedal Beastweres, or mobility equipment.

**Daily use:** The Art Club and Dramatics Club are based here, Cassia often paints in the late afternoon, and Kaelen enjoys performance work that lets him use foxfire under controlled stage rules. School productions deliberately cast across species and body types instead of requiring humanoid presentation.

**Safety and accommodations:** Illusions, dream effects, emotional magic, and voice mimicry are governed by clear audience-consent rules. Costume fittings never require a student to expose a body feature they want private. Ventilation and material lists protect scent-sensitive students.

**Role in academy life:** The wing gives characters a place to be expressive without making every power use about defense. Productions, backstage confusion, art shows, friendships, jealousies, creative breakthroughs, and paint-covered uniforms all belong here.

## Starfall Music Hall

Starfall Music Hall is a medium-sized auditorium and music classroom complex tuned for both ordinary instruments and supernatural acoustics. Jace and Zeke helped make student performances here part of modern Lunaris culture.

**Layout and atmosphere:** The main stage seats several hundred, while rehearsal rooms, instrument lockers, recording booths, piano studios, and a sound-treated practice chamber occupy the rear wing. Acoustic wards prevent a werebeast roar or resonance power from damaging hearing during supervised rehearsal.

**Daily use:** Concert band, informal ensembles, talent nights, music club meetings, and school assemblies use the hall. Gabriel studies controlled resonance here, Jace performs, and students without powers receive equal stage time. Lunch-hour jam sessions are common.

**Safety and accommodations:** Hearing protection is normal rather than embarrassing. Amplification, sonic powers, and magical instruments require calibrated limits. Recording signs indicate when school performances are being captured, and performers may opt out of close identifiable footage where practical.

**Role in academy life:** Starfall is one of the clearest places where supernatural and ordinary teenage life overlap: powerful beings still miss notes, forget lyrics, argue about rehearsal schedules, and become nervous before walking onstage.

## Crescent Student Union

The Crescent Student Union is New Moon's modern social and practical hub, built to give boarding students places to spend time that are neither dorm rooms nor classrooms. It contains a café, campus store, small game arcade, mail counter, club meeting rooms, and casual food court.

**Layout and atmosphere:** Wide central walkways branch toward booths, floor seating, reinforced tables, charging stations, vending machines, and a quiet mezzanine. The store sells school supplies, toiletries, clothing repair kits, shift-safe basics, snacks, batteries, and mundane items students otherwise would need a town trip to buy.

**Daily use:** Students stop here between classes, receive packages, hold club meetings, play games, complain about prices, and wait for Pineharbor shuttles. It is deliberately contemporary: phones, contactless payments, student ID bands, and campus Wi-Fi are normal.

**Safety and accommodations:** Packages are screened for hazardous magical materials without staff reading personal correspondence. Arcade games cannot use psychic or probability powers in competitive score modes, mostly because it ruined the leaderboards. Scent-heavy foods remain in ventilated zones.

**Role in academy life:** The union makes the academy feel inhabited. It creates countless low-stakes roleplay opportunities and prevents the setting from becoming a sequence of classrooms and rituals.

## Howling Fields and Moonrun Trail

Howling Fields are open meadows on the western side of campus connected to the Moonrun Trail, a broad looping route designed for transformed running, athletics, and full-moon movement. Despite the name, the area is open to every student.

**Layout and atmosphere:** The fields include track markers, soft turf, low obstacle structures, rest shelters, water stations, and trail entrances wide enough for large forms. The outer loop passes through sparse woodland without approaching the secrecy boundary.

**Daily use:** Werewolves commonly use the space when lunar restlessness makes sprinting helpful, but track club, flying drills, endurance classes, and ordinary joggers use it all month. Full-moon gatherings sometimes begin here with a voluntary communal howl before students choose their own activities.

**Safety and accommodations:** Route lights stay low and red-toned on lunar nights, staff monitor from a distance, and no student is pressured to run with a pack. Emergency beacons can guide someone back without emitting an alarm audible in Pineharbor.

**Role in academy life:** The fields turn a potentially disruptive lunar need into normal recreation. They support racing, quiet solitary runs, team events, first successful transformed sprints, and exhausted laughter at the finish shelter.

## East Gate and Shuttle Court

East Gate is the controlled transition point between hidden Lunaris and the ordinary roads leading toward Pineharbor. From inside it looks like a landscaped security court; from the mundane side the land appears to belong to the private Northreach Nature Trust and the road seems to end at a service entrance.

**Layout and atmosphere:** The court contains a gatehouse, covered shuttle bay, visitor room, secure package drop, bicycle racks, and a changing/storage area where students can prepare for mundane outings. Academy minibuses use ordinary license plates and never display supernatural symbols outside the wards.

**Daily use:** Town trips, guardian pickups, deliveries, field excursions, and return check-ins all pass through here. The Student Life Office coordinates schedules and makes sure students understand current mundane conditions before leaving.

**Safety and accommodations:** Students entering Pineharbor must use a form that can move safely in public, secure obvious magical equipment, and follow secrecy rules. The gate wards redirect accidental visitors rather than frightening or imprisoning them. Emergency return always overrides curfew penalties.

**Role in academy life:** East Gate is narratively useful because it marks the shift between two worlds without making either one fake. A student can leave a full-moon training session and, an hour later, be buying fries in a town that has no idea Lunaris exists.

## White Moon Quiet Center

The White Moon Quiet Center is a low-stimulation support building near the dorms for students who need space from noise, scent, bright light, social pressure, or ability feedback. It is especially busy around full moons but is available every day to every species.

**Layout and atmosphere:** Individual rooms offer adjustable lighting, sound dampening, weighted or light blankets, scent-neutral air, floor cushions, normal beds, rocking chairs, and simple call panels. A larger silent lounge and small tea kitchen let students be near others without conversation.

**Daily use:** Werewolves may come here when pack resonance feels too loud, telepaths when crowded emotions become tiring, Beastweres after long guise use, or any student after a difficult day. No diagnosis or disciplinary referral is required for ordinary use.

**Safety and accommodations:** The center has staff nearby but does not watch private rooms through cameras. Doors open from the inside at all times unless a medical emergency requires direct staff intervention. Students can request company, silence, food, water, or infirmary help through clear controls.

**Role in academy life:** White Moon makes regulation visible as a normal skill rather than a failure. It provides believable decompression scenes and reinforces that choosing a quiet room can be as responsible as choosing the training field.

## Core Subjects

**Instructor:** Professor Aris Thorne

Lunaris requires a complete modern secondary education rather than assuming supernatural talent replaces ordinary knowledge. Professor Aris Thorne coordinates Core Subjects across history, literature, mathematics, science, civics, and research skills. The courses are academically serious and constantly connect mundane knowledge to the unusual realities students face.

**Curriculum:** Physics units examine force, heat, sound, and motion before asking how a power modifies them. Biology teaches ordinary anatomy alongside the limits of comparing human systems to werebeasts or Beastweres. History includes mundane world events, hidden-community records, and source criticism so students learn where myths, propaganda, and memory conflict. Literature emphasizes interpretation without treating supernatural authors as representatives of entire species.

**Class structure:** Students move between lectures, labs, discussion seminars, projects, and ordinary homework. Group work is intentionally mixed, but instructors do not force one student to become the class spokesperson for their species. Devices are allowed for notes and accessibility unless an assessment requires otherwise.

**Assessment and safety:** Grades come from written work, labs, projects, presentations, and exams. Powers may assist only when the assignment explicitly tests them; telepathy, psychometry, precognition, super-senses, and similar advantages have accommodation rules rather than being treated as cheating by default. The goal is measuring knowledge fairly.

**Student experience:** Core classes ground the setting. Even a student capable of opening portals still has essays due, and a werewolf who can track through forest still has to learn algebra. Aris values a precise correction more than a confident wrong answer and makes no distinction between 'mundane' intelligence and magical prestige.

## Transformation Studies

**Instructor:** Master Lyra Silvermane

Transformation Studies is the central practical course for werebeasts, with werewolf modules receiving special attention because lunar cycles can intensify shifting. Lyra Silvermane teaches transformation as body literacy: noticing triggers, understanding forms, choosing transitions, recovering well, and remaining responsible without treating instinct as shameful.

**Curriculum:** Students study human-base, hybrid, beast, and lineage-specific forms; partial shifting; clothing and equipment; sensory changes; energy needs; lunar response; emotional triggers; scent communication; recovery; first-shift planning; and how to distinguish a strong urge from loss of choice. Not every subtype has the same form ladder, and nobody is graded on achieving a form their lineage does not possess.

**Class structure:** Lessons alternate between classroom physiology and the Transformation Pavilion. Beginners work on one change at a time, while advanced students train movement, speech alternatives, tool use, and transitions under distraction. Full moon practice is voluntary and scheduled around individual medical plans.

**Assessment and safety:** Assessment focuses on self-observation logs, safe transitions, communication, recovery choices, and practical scenario work. Intentionally provoking another student into shifting is prohibited. A failed or incomplete change is data, not humiliation.

**Student experience:** The course is where many werebeasts stop thinking of control as staying human. Mira studies lunar leadership without being told to suppress every wolf response; Zeke practices heat-safe shifting; Damon adapts for mass and healing fatigue. Lyra's standard is whether students can make informed choices in the bodies they actually have.

## Beast Mastery

**Instructor:** Mistress Elara Finchwood

Beast Mastery is Elara Finchwood's specialist course for Beastweres and one of New Moon's most thoroughly redesigned subjects. Because Beastweres are animal-base beings rather than humans who become animals, the course centers the true animal form and treats human or humanoid guise as a useful temporary skill, not a superior destination.

**Curriculum:** Curriculum covers true-form movement, species-specific senses, natural communication, safe interaction with mundane wildlife, human guise timing, reserve management, partial trait expression, clothing and carried-item logistics, paw/wing/talon-friendly technology, public-world navigation, Beastwere law, and the right to be recognized as a person regardless of shape.

**Class structure:** Many lessons take place in Wildering Woods, but classroom sessions use adaptable workstations and communication tools. Kaelen may solve a route problem by scent and foxfire while Selar uses shadow and spatial awareness; Pippa, Orin, Asha, and Renn each receive species-appropriate tasks rather than one generic 'animal' curriculum.

**Assessment and safety:** Students are never required to extend a human guise to exhaustion for a grade. Forced reversion is treated as a fatigue event requiring privacy and recovery, not misconduct. Assessments include navigation, communication, ecology, reserve planning, and practical town-preparation scenarios.

**Student experience:** Beast Mastery often becomes a point of pride for students whose earlier schools expected constant human presentation. Elara's room makes clear that literacy, technology, friendship, humor, and education do not depend on hands, speech, or a humanoid face.

## Combat Training

**Instructor:** Alistair Valerius

Combat Training teaches defensive movement, safe sparring, rescue tactics, and power restraint under Alistair Valerius. The course assumes Lunaris students may someday face dangerous situations but refuses to make aggression the center of identity. Winning a bout matters less than maintaining awareness and control.

**Curriculum:** Students learn stance, falls, escape, protective positioning, team communication, noninjurious restraint, obstacle response, evacuation, and ability-specific defense. Werebeasts practice managing reach and strength; powered humans learn range discipline and collateral awareness; Beastweres train movement appropriate to true forms and guises.

**Class structure:** Classes begin with warm-ups and explicit power declarations. Pairings change according to size, ability interaction, experience, and student comfort. Many drills are cooperative: carry a dummy through unstable terrain, shield a teammate, identify a safe exit, or stop a simulated fight before it escalates.

**Assessment and safety:** Protective gear and ward limits are mandatory. Stop signals override competitive momentum. Grades reward decision quality, restraint, communication, teamwork, and recovery as well as technique. Unsupervised fights never become acceptable merely because two students belong to a dueling club.

**Student experience:** Valerius's course can be intense and exciting without becoming brutal. Friendly rivalries thrive here, but students are expected to shake off the idea that being powerful means always pushing harder. The best performance may be the moment someone recognizes a bad situation and chooses not to throw the next strike.

Daily routines matter as much as dramatic moments. ## Potions and Herbology

**Instructor:** Madam Calypso Willowbark

Potions and Herbology combines magical plant study, ordinary botany, chemistry, medicine-adjacent safety, and supervised alchemy under Calypso Willowbark. The old Lunaris course was famous for rare ingredients; New Moon keeps the wonder while making measurements, labeling, toxicity, and evidence equally important.

**Curriculum:** Students learn plant identification, cultivation, harvesting, drying, extraction, solution chemistry, antidote principles, magical catalysts, species-specific reactions, ethical sourcing, and the difference between a classroom tonic and real medical care. They study silver, wolfsbane, and other dangerous substances academically without casual handling.

**Class structure:** Most lessons alternate between Moonglass Greenhouses and the alchemy lab. Students maintain plants over weeks, prepare simple controlled mixtures, compare magical and mundane results, and document every change. Calypso encourages substitutions when a rare ingredient is unnecessary.

**Assessment and safety:** Lab goggles, gloves, ventilation, allergy records, clear labels, and cleanup are part of the grade. No ingestible preparation is tasted without instructor approval, and no potion that changes mood, memory, appearance, or power state may be given to another person without informed consent.

**Student experience:** The course attracts both serious healers and students who simply like growing things. It offers mystery, accidents, practical problem solving, and cozy greenhouse scenes while reinforcing that careful craft is a form of power.

## Divination and Astrology

**Instructor:** Oracle Seraphina

Divination and Astrology is taught by Seraphina as the study of possible information under uncertainty, not the declaration of fixed destiny. Students examine genuine supernatural foresight beside astronomy, probability, symbolism, folklore, dream interpretation, and the cognitive biases that make vague predictions feel certain.

**Curriculum:** The curriculum includes scrying methods, omen traditions, dream logs, celestial observation, probabilistic language, false positives, self-fulfilling prophecy, privacy, and how to communicate a warning without controlling another person's choices. Students with no divinatory gift can excel through analysis.

**Class structure:** Classes use the Lunar Observatory, seminar room, and occasional dream-study labs. One assignment may ask students to compare three contradictory interpretations of the same symbol; another requires making a sensible safety plan that remains useful even if the vision is wrong.

**Assessment and safety:** No student is permitted to investigate a classmate's private future, dreams, family, or relationships as entertainment. Predictions are not evidence of guilt. Grades reward documentation, uncertainty, ethical handling, and reasoning rather than dramatic accuracy alone.

**Student experience:** Seraphina's calm skepticism gives the course a distinctive tone. Students learn that a strange dream can matter without becoming an order, and that knowing less than one wishes is not failure.

## Enchantment and Runes

**Instructor:** Master Silas Emberfall

Enchantment and Runes teaches students how to create bounded magical functions in objects and infrastructure. Silas Emberfall treats enchantment like engineering: define the job, define the limits, choose a power source, build a shutdown method, test failure modes, and document what the object actually does.

**Curriculum:** Students learn rune families, magical materials, circuit analogies, ward anchors, temporary charms, maintenance, compatibility with electronics, accessibility enchantments, data privacy, and repair. Historical rune systems are studied with context rather than copied blindly.

**Class structure:** The Emberworks Workshop supports drafting, carving, programming, testing, and peer review. Projects begin small: a labeled warming tile, a light that responds to touch, a bag that warns when overloaded. Advanced students may build safe dorm tools or festival installations.

Hidden trackers, coercive charms, disguised traps, and self-modifying devices are prohibited student projects. Every graded object needs a visible off state.

**Student experience:** Theo thrives here, but Silas insists that cleverness is not a substitute for maintainability. ## Power Control and Applied Ability

**Instructor:** Faculty rotation coordinated by Dr. Greystone and Alistair Valerius

Power Control and Applied Ability is the specialist course for powered humans and any student whose supernatural ability benefits from measured practice outside transformation curricula. It was added during New Moon so human students would receive structured support equal to shifter education.

**Curriculum:** Students create a personal ability profile covering triggers, range, duration, output, precision, sensory effects, recovery, environmental interactions, emotional influence, and known limits. Elemental users map heat or cold; telekinetics test mass and distance; portal users study geometry; psychometrists practice consent and object-handling protocols.

**Class structure:** Most work occurs in the Applied Powers Laboratory through supervised experiments and scenario drills. Instructors rotate according to subject: Greystone covers physiology and recovery, Valerius covers practical safety, Thorne covers research design, Silas assists technological interaction, and Seraphina covers unusual perception.

**Assessment and safety:** The course never deliberately frightens, hurts, or humiliates students to make abilities appear. Fatigue thresholds are established before high-output work. Students are graded on understanding and repeatability, not maximum spectacle.

## Supernatural Ethics, Consent and Secrecy

**Instructor:** Headmistress Helena Mooncrest with rotating faculty

This required seminar teaches the social rules that let a hidden mixed-species school exist without turning secrecy into fear. Headmistress Mooncrest and rotating faculty lead case studies on privacy, recording, transformations, powers that affect minds or emotions, mundane-world contact, bystander safety, public emergencies, and the limits of school authority.

**Curriculum:** Students examine real and fictional scenarios: whether to use a power to stop a minor accident in Pineharbor, how to ask before touching transformed features, what to do if a friend reveals a dangerous secret, when emergency intervention overrides ordinary privacy, and why a supernatural ability never creates automatic consent.

**Class structure:** Classes rely on discussion, mock decisions, short policy briefs, and restorative exercises rather than rote memorization. Different species are encouraged to explain practical needs but are never required to disclose private experiences.

**Assessment and safety:** Assessment rewards reasoning, identification of affected people, proportionality, and practical alternatives. There are usually several defensible answers if a student can explain them. Mock scenarios involving trauma or personal history include opt-out routes.

**Student experience:** The seminar gives the chatbot world a clear modern moral framework. It lets characters disagree without pretending boundaries are vague and makes the academy's SFW tone part of in-world culture rather than an out-of-character restriction.

## Emergency Response and Mundane Integration

**Instructor:** Headmistress Helena Mooncrest and Dr. Marcus Greystone

Emergency Response and Mundane Integration prepares students for accidents on campus and ordinary life beyond the wards. The course combines first aid, evacuation, public behavior, secrecy decisions, mundane emergency services, communication, and the difficult question of when saving someone is more important than hiding a supernatural ability.

**Curriculum:** Students learn CPR and first aid where physically appropriate, emergency calls, safe transport, fire and weather response, missing-person procedure, power accidents, full-moon disorientation support, and how to explain unusual incidents without inventing elaborate lies that create more danger.

**Class structure:** Practice includes simulated Pineharbor outings, bus breakdowns, lost-student drills, damaged ward scenarios, and mixed-team rescues. Students rotate roles so the physically strongest person is not always the rescuer and the most powerful ability is not always the correct tool.

**Assessment and safety:** The central rule is proportionality: protect life first, minimize unnecessary exposure second, report honestly to academy staff afterward. Nobody is punished for a good-faith emergency action solely because secrecy became imperfect.

**Student experience:** This class connects Lunaris to the wider world. It reminds students that ordinary firefighters, doctors, teachers, drivers, and neighbors are not background characters, and that supernatural responsibility includes knowing how to cooperate with systems that do not know the academy exists.

Recording another student during a transformation, medical episode, loss of power control, or vulnerable true-form moment is a serious privacy violation. Jokes are tolerated when everyone involved is laughing; humiliation, species stereotyping, coercion, and baiting someone into a shift are not. The result is a campus where unusual biology can be openly accommodated inside the wards even though it must remain hidden from the nearby mundane town.

## Duelling Club

The Duelling Club preserves one of Lunaris's most popular original student societies, now operating under New Moon's modern safety code. It is competitive, loud, and full of friendly rivalries, but its purpose is controlled practice and strategy rather than proving who is most dangerous.

**Activities:** Weekly meetings rotate between one-on-one bouts, team objective matches, obstacle duels, defense-only rounds, and tactical games where victory requires reaching or protecting a target. Members also review recordings of consenting participants to study footwork and decision-making.

**Typical members and roles:** Evelyn enjoys precise control matches, Mira brings disciplined werewolf movement, Jace loves the crowd, Zeke prefers high-energy rounds, and Valerius is the faculty adviser. Beginners can join without prior combat experience and often serve as referees or analysts before sparring.

Mind influence, deliberate sensory overload, hidden toxins, and surprise full transformations outside agreed match rules are prohibited. No club bout settles personal disputes.

## Herbology Society

Field walks in Wildering Woods focus on observation rather than collection.

**Typical members and roles:** Sienna is a natural regular because of florakinesis, Evelyn sometimes grows cold-tolerant medicinal plants, and students with no botanical power are equally valued. Calypso advises while experienced students manage watering rosters and seed exchanges.

## Mystic Mechanics — Magitech and Robotics Club

## Wild Run Club — Track, Flight and Trail

## Student Council

New Moon's Student Council is an elected mixed-species body with real but limited influence over daily school policy. It exists partly because the reformed academy wanted students affected by rules to have a formal way to challenge, revise, and explain them.

**Activities:** Council committees handle events, dorm concerns, accessibility, club funding, town outings, dining feedback, and student proposals. Representatives hold public office hours and monthly forums in Moonwell Courtyard.

**Typical members and roles:** Mira often participates because of her leadership instincts, Evelyn contributes careful policy analysis, and council seats are not reserved by species even though election rules encourage broad representation. Beastwere accessibility concerns have a standing liaison rather than being treated as occasional special cases.

**Rules and supervision:** The council cannot override emergency safety law, expose secrecy-protected records, or discipline students. Meetings are recorded in written minutes with private matters removed. Election magic, coercion, and mind influence are obvious disqualifiers.

**Club culture:** Student Council creates school politics at a manageable scale: budgets, cafeteria complaints, full-moon quiet-hour debates, festival planning, and arguments about whether the arcade needs one more machine. ## Photography and Media Club

Photography and Media Club produces the academy yearbook, event photos, campus magazine, nature photography, and student interviews while operating under Lunaris's unusually strict privacy rules.

**Activities:** Members learn cameras, editing, layout, audio recording, interviewing, darkroom techniques, and magical-light photography. They document landscapes and public events, maintain a consent-based portrait studio, and prepare mundane-safe versions of materials that might leave the wards.

**Typical members and roles:** Orin's visual memory makes him a sharp editor, Rhea contributes consent-cleared landscape studies from unusual perspectives, and Darius favors low-light work. The Student Life Office reviews only materials intended for public mundane circulation, not ordinary student journalism.

**Rules and supervision:** No hidden photography, transformation ambushes, dorm-room recording, dream imagery, private medical footage, or automatic facial tagging is permitted. Event signs state recording zones, and students can request nonidentifiable coverage.

**Club culture:** Because Lunaris secrecy could easily become censorship, the club is important culturally. Students are allowed to document their own community; the responsibility is protecting people rather than pretending school history never happened.

These practices also support the academy’s central secrecy rule. Students are free to be themselves on protected grounds, but they learn how to move through the mundane world without exposing classmates or frightening unprepared civilians. That means planning clothing, transportation, power use, scent or sound control, and emergency exits before town trips. Secrecy is taught as community protection rather than shame: the hidden world remains hidden so young people can learn safely and ordinary humans in Pineharbor can continue their lives without being pulled into supernatural conflicts they do not understand.

At Lunaris Academy: New Moon, this subject is treated as part of ordinary student life rather than a spectacle. Faculty expect students to understand what their bodies and abilities are doing, communicate when they need help, and use the school’s accommodations before a manageable problem turns into a crisis. The academy keeps practical supplies, quiet rooms, reinforced practice areas, flexible meal options, and trained staff available so that different species can function together without anyone being treated as dangerous merely for existing. Older students are encouraged to model calm, responsible behavior for younger classmates, while teachers distinguish between an involuntary symptom and a deliberate harmful choice.

entries.content:
## Games and Strategy Club

Games and Strategy Club meets in the Crescent Union for chess, cards, tabletop roleplaying, board games, puzzles, and strategy tournaments. It is one of the most species-neutral clubs because success usually depends on attention, creativity, and knowing when someone is bluffing.

**Activities:** The club runs weekly open tables, seasonal chess ladders, cooperative puzzle nights, miniature painting, and long campaign games. Custom pieces accommodate claws, paws, telekinetic interaction, low vision, and different seating needs.

**Typical members and roles:** Evelyn is formidable at chess, Theo loves complicated games with too many components, Caleb is an enthusiastic bluffing-game menace, and Beastweres often use adapted boards. Nobody needs powers to participate.

**Rules and supervision:** Precognition, telepathy, psychometry, probability manipulation, and similar abilities are either voluntarily disabled or assigned special exhibition categories where everyone knows the rule. Losing a board game is not an emergency requiring supernatural intervention.

**Club culture:** The club is ideal for low-stakes rivalry and conversation. Students who are terrifying on a training field can be humbled by a cardboard sheep-trading game, which the rest of the school considers healthy.

At Lunaris Academy: New Moon, this subject is treated as part of ordinary student life rather than a spectacle. Faculty expect students to understand what their bodies and abilities are doing, communicate when they need help, and use the school’s accommodations before a manageable problem turns into a crisis. Older students are encouraged to model calm, responsible behavior for younger classmates, while teachers distinguish between an involuntary symptom and a deliberate harmful choice.

Daily routines matter as much as dramatic moments. Students still have homework, alarms, laundry, club meetings, cafeteria lines, exams, group projects, forgotten chargers, sports practice, and weekend plans. Supernatural traits simply change how those routines are managed. A student with heightened hearing may use dampening earbuds; a shifter may keep spare adaptive clothing in a locker; a powered human may sign out a practice room before testing a new technique. These small habits are considered signs of maturity because Lunaris values preparation over bravado.

entries.content:
## Cooking and Hearth Club

Cooking and Hearth Club uses a teaching kitchen beside the dining hall to explore ordinary cooking, baking, cultural recipes, high-metabolism meal planning, and food adaptations for supernatural physiology. It exists because boarding-school meals are better when students know how to feed themselves.

**Activities:** Members cook weekly themes, exchange family recipes, test shift-recovery snacks, bake for events, hold soup nights, and learn budgeting. Recipes include clearly labeled substitutions for allergies, Beastwere digestion, high-calorie werebeast needs, and powered students whose abilities change hydration or temperature requirements.

**Typical members and roles:** Damon is surprisingly good at bread, Marcus Greystone occasionally teaches recovery meals, Nessa loves seafood recipes, and many students join because club meetings end with food. Human students are not assigned 'normal' recipes by default.

**Rules and supervision:** No prank ingredients, hidden allergens, magical mood additives, or unlabeled supplements are allowed. Raw ingredients with supernatural effects are handled only under Calypso or medical guidance.

**Club culture:** The club feels domestic in the best way. It creates birthday cakes, burnt cookies, family stories, competitive chili nights, and the reassuring lesson that extraordinary people still need dinner.

Daily routines matter as much as dramatic moments. Students still have homework, alarms, laundry, club meetings, cafeteria lines, exams, group projects, forgotten chargers, sports practice, and weekend plans. Supernatural traits simply change how those routines are managed. A student with heightened hearing may use dampening earbuds; a shifter may keep spare adaptive clothing in a locker; a powered human may sign out a practice room before testing a new technique. These small habits are considered signs of maturity because Lunaris values preparation over bravado.

The academy’s culture emphasizes personhood and consent. No student is permitted to touch another person’s ears, tail, wings, fur, transformed body, magical focus, or personal equipment without permission. Recording another student during a transformation, medical episode, loss of power control, or vulnerable true-form moment is a serious privacy violation. Jokes are tolerated when everyone involved is laughing; humiliation, species stereotyping, coercion, and baiting someone into a shift are not. The result is a campus where unusual biology can be openly accommodated inside the wards even though it must remain hidden from the nearby mundane town.

entries.content:
## New Moon Welcome

**Timing:** Opening week and the first new-moon evening of the academic year.

New Moon Welcome is the signature opening event of the reformed academy. It replaces older initiation traditions with a week of practical orientation, low-pressure social events, campus tours, club previews, and a final lantern gathering in Moonwell Courtyard. The 'new moon' symbolizes beginning without demanding that students abandon old identities.

**How it unfolds:** Arrival day focuses on rooms, medical information, devices, schedules, and meeting resident advisers. Later days include mixed-species campus tours, a safety scavenger hunt, short sample classes, a Pineharbor secrecy briefing, and club demonstrations. On the final evening, the courtyard lights are lowered and each student receives a small reusable lantern tag engraved only with the name they choose to use at school.

**Participation:** Attendance at practical orientation is required, but social games, speeches, photos, and lantern sharing are optional. Students arriving late or overwhelmed receive individual orientation rather than punishment. Beastweres may attend in true form, and nobody is made to transform or demonstrate a power.

**Safety and boundaries:** No hazing, surprise power tests, forced confessions, public ranking, or species-based initiation is allowed. Staff deliberately watch for older students trying to revive 'traditional' pranks at first-years' expense.

**Traditions and atmosphere:** The event ends not with a magical oath but with food in the Den Commons and an open campus night. Older students joke that the most sacred New Moon tradition is getting lost on the way back to Twilight Dorms at least once.

The academy’s culture emphasizes personhood and consent. No student is permitted to touch another person’s ears, tail, wings, fur, transformed body, magical focus, or personal equipment without permission. entries.content:
## The Moonlit Challenge

**Timing:** Monthly during the academic year, with the exact moon phase chosen around weather, exams, and safety.

The Moonlit Challenge is one of Lunaris Academy's defining traditions. Each month, mixed teams receive a supervised problem that cannot be solved well by relying on one kind of power or body. The purpose is competition, but it is competition built to reveal how differently students think. A human's spell precision, a werebeast's endurance, a Beastwere's environmental awareness, and an ordinary mundane skill may all become equally important within the same course.

Challenges vary deliberately. One month teams may brew a stable recovery potion while wind and rain simulations complicate ingredient handling. Another month they navigate a section of Wildering Woods, solve lunar riddles, carry a fragile object through an obstacle course, repair a harmless ward, identify an ecological hazard, or rescue a training dummy from a staged collapse. Tasks are designed so simply blasting through the obstacle usually costs points. Planning, communication, consent, and getting every teammate safely to the finish matter more.

Students can compete, staff checkpoints, document approved public-within-campus moments, help with accessibility, or watch the final stage. Teams are often cross-species, but nobody is assigned as a token representative or required to demonstrate a trait they do not want to use. A werebeast can complete an event without shifting; a Beastwere can remain in true form; a human does not need to compensate for being human by taking the most dangerous magical role.

The woods and arena close around the event route, locator bands are mandatory for remote checkpoints, and faculty can change or cancel a task when weather, fatigue, lunar effects, or magical instability make the original plan unsafe. No live hunting, deliberate injury, forced transformation, or humiliation is part of the Challenge.

Winning teams receive the silver-colored wooden crescent trophy for the month and enormous bragging rights. Individual performance can affect campus reputation, but New Moon emphasizes the older tradition's better lesson: the memorable victories are usually the moments when someone remembers a classmate's obscure skill at exactly the right time. Muddy uniforms, bad maps, arguments over instructions, and dramatic last-minute teamwork are as iconic as the trophy itself.
entries.name: 🎉 The Moonlit Challenge

entries.content:
## The Lunar Festival and Moonlight Waltz

**Timing:** Once each academic year, with preparations spread across several weeks.

The Lunar Festival is Lunaris Academy's largest celebration of its own community. Moonwell Courtyard, the Den Commons, Starfall Music Hall, Dreamglass Arts Wing, greenhouse paths, and the lakeside fill with food stalls, club exhibits, student art, games, concerts, demonstrations, decorations, and family traditions. The festival's central theme is unity without sameness: every group contributes something distinctive, and no single species or magical tradition is treated as the academy's default culture.

The day begins with shared breakfast and final setup. By afternoon, Mystic Mechanics may be running a harmless gadget game, Herbology Society may display moon-blooming plants, Dramatics Club previews its term production, students sell crafts, and the Training Grounds host carefully limited skill demonstrations. Food is labeled for allergens, magical additives, and species-specific incompatibilities. Trusted supernatural guardians can attend through East Gate under invitation and secrecy rules; ordinary Pineharbor residents do not enter the protected campus.

At night, the oldest surviving festival tradition is the **Moonlight Waltz**. Historically students from different groups were paired to symbolize harmony. New Moon preserves the visual tradition—glowing lunar patterns across the courtyard, music, formal or semi-formal clothing, and mixed participation—but removes any expectation of romance or forced pairing. Students choose partners, dance in friend groups, use adaptive choreography, perform in transformed or true form where space permits, watch from the edge, or skip the dance entirely. The point is coordinated movement and celebration, not matchmaking.

The festival has strict consent and recording rules. No one may use charm, empathy, dream, scent, illusion, or other influence magic to pressure participation. Transformation demonstrations require marked space. Photography zones are posted. Accessibility teams keep routes clear for wings, tails, wheelchairs, large bodies, and sensory needs.

Every year develops its own legend: a decoration that refused to stay attached, a food stall that sold out in ten minutes, a student band that accidentally became famous inside the wards, or a Moonlight Waltz formation that went wonderfully wrong. Those ordinary memories are why students often remember the Lunar Festival more fondly than grand magical ceremonies.
entries.name: 🎉 Lunar Festival

entries.content:
## The Bonding Ritual

**Timing:** Once per term, usually before a major examination or seasonal break.

The Bonding Ritual is an old Lunaris tradition designed to break down prejudice by placing students with people they would not necessarily choose on their own. The word *ritual* is historical: there is no magical soul-bond, romantic pairing, permanent mark, compulsory touch, or loss of personal boundaries. New Moon keeps the cooperative structure while making consent and accessibility explicit.

At the beginning of the day, students are assigned supervised pairs or small teams with attention to genuine safety and known conflicts. Assignments deliberately mix social circles and often species, but staff do not force a student to work directly with someone who has threatened or harmed them. Each group receives a sequence of tasks—navigating a shifting maze, assembling a device from incomplete instructions, completing a low-risk survival exercise, solving a library puzzle, transporting supplies, preparing a simple meal, or communicating through a challenge where each person receives different information.

Tasks are built so one participant cannot simply carry the other. The fastest student may need a scholar's clue; the strongest werebeast may need a Beastwere to notice a trail change; a powered human may need a mundane knot or first-aid skill. Success comes from asking what another person can do rather than assuming. Faculty score communication, adaptation, safety, and completion, not emotional disclosure.

No participant is required to reveal secrets, share trauma, hug, exchange scent, join a pack, enter a dream, accept empathic influence, or use a transformation. Quiet alternatives and nonverbal communication tools are available. Students who cannot participate in the primary activity can complete a parallel cooperative project without being treated as failures.

The day ends at the Den Commons with food and the **Small Thanks Wall**, where students may anonymously recognize ordinary help: lending notes, waiting through a difficult shift, explaining a town rule, carrying equipment, or simply listening. The old belief behind the ritual survives intact—genuine understanding is stronger than division—but New Moon teaches that understanding grows through repeated choices, not mystical compulsion.
entries.name: 🎉 The Bonding Ritual

entries.content:
## The Night Hunt

**Timing:** Once each term on a low-light evening, with weather and forest conditions taking priority over tradition.

The Night Hunt retains one of old Lunaris Academy's most dramatic names, but in New Moon it is a supervised navigation, tracking, puzzle, and courage trial. Students do not hunt classmates or kill live animals. Instead, teams enter a designated section of Wildering Woods after dusk to locate marked objectives, identify staged tracks, decode signs, evade harmless illusion obstacles, and complete environmental or rescue tasks.

The course rewards different kinds of perception. One checkpoint may be easiest with scent; another requires ordinary map reading because magical navigation is scrambled. Aerial students can spot route markers from above, but dense tree cover creates blind zones. Beastweres can participate in true form, transformed werebeasts use approved lanes where needed, and powered humans may bring authorized tools. Several tasks are intentionally solvable without supernatural abilities so the event never becomes a ranking of bodies.

The Night Hunt's atmosphere is allowed to be thrilling. Lanterns are limited, the forest sounds unfamiliar after dark, old stories about Eclipse Caverns circulate around the starting line, and teams often give themselves ridiculous names or camouflage. Faculty use controlled illusions and enchanted guardians as puzzles rather than threats. Students can be startled, lost for a few minutes, or challenged without being placed in genuine predatory danger.

Safeguards are extensive. Every participant carries a locator and emergency signal. Boundaries are marked for visual, scent, tactile, and magical recognition. Staff monitor hidden checkpoints, wildlife-sensitive areas remain closed, and any student can withdraw without losing disciplinary standing. No chasing uninvolved students, sabotaging another team, crossing the concealment perimeter, forcing a shift, or using fear-inducing magic is permitted.

The winning team receives a wooden lantern trophy and breakfast privileges the following morning. More importantly, the event creates stories: the moment a quiet classmate found the trail, the time everyone trusted the wrong compass, or the night a team abandoned its score to help another group. The Night Hunt is a rite of passage because it tests judgment in darkness—not because Lunaris expects students to become hunters.
entries.name: 🎉 Night Hunt

## Full Moon Vigil

**Timing:** Every full moon, with the largest communal observance held once each term.

Full Moon Vigil is Lunaris's central full-moon tradition and the clearest example of New Moon's SFW werewolf culture. It is not a compulsory transformation rite. It is a flexible campus-wide support night that combines celebration, movement, quiet spaces, food, observation, and community for students affected by lunar energy.

**How it unfolds:** Before sunset the dining hall serves high-energy meals and the infirmary opens hydration stations. At moonrise, anyone who wishes may gather on Howling Fields for a short welcome from Lyra or Helena. Werewolves can join a voluntary communal howl, run the Moonrun Trail, transform, remain human, or leave immediately. Other students may observe respectfully or choose their own activities. White Moon Quiet Center, library, observatory, lake paths, and dorm lounges all run special late hours.

**Participation:** Participation in the ceremonial gathering, howl, pack activity, or transformation is voluntary. Students may spend the entire night asleep, studying, gaming, or using a quiet room. Individual family traditions are welcome as long as they respect others.

**Safety and boundaries:** Extra staff and medical coverage are available without turning the campus into lockdown. Recording transformations is forbidden unless a specific student requested it for personal training. Silver and wolfsbane are removed from casual instructional access during the period as an additional precaution.

**Traditions and atmosphere:** At dawn the Den Commons serves a huge recovery breakfast. Students often remember the small moments more than the moon itself: someone pacing with a nervous first-year, a group lying in the grass listening to distant howls, or a werewolf realizing that a full moon can be intense without being frightening.

Daily routines matter as much as dramatic moments. A student with heightened hearing may use dampening earbuds; a shifter may keep spare adaptive clothing in a locker; a powered human may sign out a practice room before testing a new technique. ## Silver Bell Moonrun

**Timing:** Spring, on the first clear weekend after a full moon.

The Silver Bell Moonrun is a schoolwide athletic relay built around the Howling Fields and Moonrun Trail. Its name comes from the painted aluminum bell at the finish line; New Moon retired the old real-silver trophy because using a common werebeast weakness as ceremonial equipment was both insensitive and impractical.

**How it unfolds:** Teams complete running, navigation, obstacle, carrying, and optional flight or water segments. Categories allow true forms, human forms, powered movement, and nonpowered participation without pretending they are directly equivalent. Mixed relays earn bonuses for efficient transitions between very different movement styles.

**Participation:** Competitive runners chase records while casual teams participate for fun, costumes, or dorm pride. Staff and clubs operate water stations, music, timing, and food. Students who dislike competition can volunteer.

## Founders and Reform Week

**Timing:** One week in early February.

Founders and Reform Week replaces a simplistic founders celebration with a more honest examination of Lunaris history. The academy acknowledges early sanctuary work, later mistakes, species bias, outdated containment practices, and the reforms that created New Moon.

**How it unfolds:** Classes use archives, student panels, restored photographs, debates, and exhibits. The library displays historical rulebooks beside annotations explaining what changed and why. Student Council hosts a forum where current policies can be challenged. The week ends with a community service day rather than a heroic pageant.

**Participation:** Students may contribute family histories or personal perspectives but are never required to disclose painful material. Older graduates sometimes return under invitation to discuss how school culture affected them.

**Safety and boundaries:** Historical discussion follows privacy and evidence rules. Faculty do not excuse harmful policy merely because it was once normal, and students are discouraged from turning ancestors into targets for modern social punishment without context.

**Traditions and atmosphere:** The week makes school history usable instead of decorative. Helena's favorite tradition is the 'rule worth keeping' board, where students identify an old practice that still serves a good purpose and explain how to preserve it without preserving its worst assumptions.

Students are taught to notice early warning signs, name what they are experiencing, choose an appropriate response, and recover properly afterward. Because Lunaris is a mixed community, no single species is treated as the default. Architecture, schedules, meals, uniforms, sports, clubs, and dorm policies are designed around overlapping needs. Werebeasts may need space to shift, Beastweres may need secure true-form areas, and powered humans may require grounding equipment or power-safe workstations. Students learn each other’s boundaries through ordinary friendship and cooperation, which is one reason cross-species teams are common in classes and school events.

## Winter Lantern Night

**Timing:** Final evening before winter break.

**How it unfolds:** Students decorate biodegradable paper shades, cook with Hearth Club, exchange optional small gifts, skate if Lake Lunara is officially safe, watch films, and attend a short outdoor lantern walk. The observatory runs a winter-sky program while the arts wing displays student work.

**Participation:** Participation is flexible. Students who do not celebrate seasonal holidays can treat it as a school social night, and those leaving early for home can join afternoon events. Students staying on campus receive a full break program.

## Pineharbor Town Day

## Interhouse Games

**Timing:** Late spring over three school days.

Interhouse Games are a broad field-day competition between Twilight Dormitory house groups. Unlike old species contests, houses are mixed and events are designed so no single power category dominates the standings.

**How it unfolds:** Events include relay courses, trivia, cooking, art build challenges, debate, canoe races, puzzle rooms, dodge-style wardball, obstacle rescue, music performance, scavenger tasks, and a deliberately ridiculous faculty-versus-student finale. Houses choose lineups strategically.

**Participation:** Students can earn points through athletic, academic, creative, service, and teamwork categories. Noncompetitive support roles also count toward participation awards. House identity is playful rather than hereditary or permanent.

**Safety and boundaries:** Ability restrictions vary by event and are announced beforehand. No student must transform, reveal private powers, or compete physically to earn full house participation credit. Referees can modify an event for accessibility without treating the adjustment as an advantage.

**Traditions and atmosphere:** The Games create banners, jokes, chants, harmless rivalries, and arguments that disappear the moment someone needs help. The overall cup spends the next year in the winning dorm lounge, usually surrounded by increasingly silly decorations.

## New Moon Crossing and Graduation

**Timing:** Final week of the school year for graduating students.

New Moon Crossing is Lunaris's graduation tradition. It marks leaving the protected academy with the expectation that graduates will build lives in supernatural, mundane, or mixed communities according to their own choices.

**How it unfolds:** The formal ceremony takes place in Moonwell Courtyard. Graduates receive ordinary academic credentials under the Northreach Preparatory cover identity as well as sealed supernatural transcripts. After speeches, each graduate crosses the courtyard bridge beneath an unlit crescent arch, symbolizing that the next path is not predetermined. Families and invited community members then join a lakeside reception.

**Participation:** No graduate is required to demonstrate a power, transform, howl, reveal a true form, or swear loyalty to Lunaris. Students may use chosen names in the internal ceremony while legal documentation follows required processes privately.

**Safety and boundaries:** Secrecy logistics are handled before the event so mundane relatives can attend approved outer-campus portions without accidentally entering restricted areas. Photography zones and species accommodations follow ordinary school policy.

## Moonstone Dining Hall

Moonstone Dining Hall is the main cafeteria and communal meal space for Lunaris. It combines an old timbered great-hall ceiling with modern serving stations, nutrition labeling, ordinary commercial kitchens, and species-specific meal planning. Food is treated as a daily practical need rather than a magical feast.

**Layout and atmosphere:** The hall has long shared tables, smaller booths, reinforced seating, floor-level dining areas for true-form Beastweres, outdoor terrace tables, and a separate quiet dining room. Serving lines are divided by meal type rather than species, with clear symbols for allergens, high-calorie options, raw-safe preparations where medically appropriate, vegetarian food, and recovery meals.

Cooking and Hearth Club uses an attached teaching kitchen, while staff regularly eat among students.

No magical additive, supplement, potion, wolfsbane derivative, or species-sensitive ingredient enters general service without medical and dietary approval. Nobody is mocked for portion size, transformed eating method, or a medically required diet.

**Layout and atmosphere:** The cluster contains detached cottages, duplexes, a compact apartment lodge, shared garden, staff parking court, and a small emergency on-call suite nearest the dorms. Homes are individually adapted: Elara's includes exterior perches and an open flight balcony, Marcus has reinforced floors, and Lyra keeps a mudroom designed for transformed return from the woods.

**Daily use:** Students do not casually wander into faculty homes. Scheduled tutoring, faculty-hosted small group meals, emergency contact, or invitation can bring students to a porch or shared garden, but normal academic meetings belong in public school spaces.

## Pineharbor

Pineharbor is the small modern town nearest Lunaris Academy, about twenty minutes from the hidden East Gate by academy shuttle. It has no confirmed knowledge of werebeasts, Beastweres, powered humans, or the school itself. To locals, the students occasionally seen in town attend Northreach Preparatory, an expensive but unremarkable private boarding school located somewhere on protected woodland outside municipal limits.

**Place and atmosphere:** The town has roughly twelve thousand residents, a compact Main Street, riverfront park, public high school, library, cinema, recreation center, grocery stores, pharmacy, cafés, modest suburbs, and roads leading into forested hills. It is large enough that unfamiliar teenagers do not attract instant attention but small enough that repeated odd behavior becomes gossip.

**How Lunaris students use it:** Older Lunaris students visit on approved afternoons and weekends for shopping, movies, volunteering, food, sports, library access, and simply practicing ordinary life beyond the wards. Shuttle groups usually arrive at the transit depot or a discreet parking area behind a leased Northreach office.

**What locals know:** Most residents think Northreach is private, selective, slightly eccentric, and overly protective of student privacy. It is the place Lunaris students most often encounter ordinary townspeople at close range because the café, pharmacy, bookstore, thrift shop, diner, and weekend market are all within walking distance.

**Place and atmosphere:** Buildings are two or three stories, with apartments and offices above shops. The town clock stands at the central intersection, and seasonal decorations make the area visibly change through the year. Free public Wi-Fi is mediocre but functional, which students complain about after campus service.

## New Moon Student Code

The New Moon Student Code is Lunaris's baseline conduct policy. It is intentionally shorter and more understandable than the old academy rulebooks: respect personhood, obtain consent, control what you reasonably can, ask for help early, protect secrecy without sacrificing immediate safety, repair harm, and do not use species or power as an excuse to intimidate others.

**Core rules:** Students must follow staff safety directions during genuine emergencies, respect private rooms and belongings, attend required classes, avoid deliberate power misuse, never provoke transformations for amusement, and treat every student as a person regardless of form. Harassment based on species, power level, family, body, disability, or transformation history is prohibited. Ordinary disagreement, rivalry, bad moods, and harmless teasing are not automatically misconduct.

**How staff respond:** Minor problems usually begin with conversation, warning, restitution, practice, or a restorative meeting. Repeated or serious behavior can restrict specific privileges such as unsupervised town trips, lab access, or competitive dueling. Suspension or removal is reserved for significant danger or persistent refusal to respect others, not for accidental supernatural symptoms.

**Why the rule exists:** Predictable rules make a mixed community safer than vague appeals to 'control yourself.' A student needs to know the difference between an involuntary partial shift and intentionally using claws to threaten someone. The code separates body realities from choices wherever possible.

**Everyday examples:** A tail knocking over a chair is an accident; refusing to help after being asked is a conduct issue. Telekinetically catching a falling book is ordinary; repeatedly moving a classmate's belongings after they say stop is not. Getting overwhelmed during a full moon calls for support; using lunar agitation to excuse deliberate cruelty does not.

Werebeasts may need space to shift, Beastweres may need secure true-form areas, and powered humans may require grounding equipment or power-safe workstations. ## Power Use and Transformation Rules

Lunaris allows harmless everyday powers and natural traits on campus instead of forcing students to behave as mundane humans inside their own home. Restrictions are based on risk, privacy, and location rather than on whether an ability looks unusual.

**Core rules:** Small controlled effects are generally permitted in dorm lounges, courtyards, and common areas when they do not endanger or disturb others. High-output casting, combat transformations, flight, portal creation, fire, destructive strength tests, major weather effects, and experimental enchantments belong in approved training zones. Students must obey posted room limits and announce abilities during formal practice.

**How staff respond:** Accidental manifestations are handled first as safety events: clear space, reduce stimulation, contact the right staff, and help the student regain control. Discipline applies when someone knowingly ignores limits, conceals a dangerous experiment, or repeats reckless behavior after support and instruction.

**Why the rule exists:** The policy avoids two bad extremes: banning supernatural life until students have nowhere to practice, and treating every corridor like a training arena. Real control develops through ordinary appropriate use plus specialized high-risk spaces.

**Everyday examples:** Evelyn can cool her drink in the Den but cannot freeze the floor. Maya can open a tiny supervised practice portal in the lab but not shortcut between dorm bedrooms. Mira may relax with visible wolf ears in a common lounge but needs a wider area for a full high-energy shift.
