Extreme heat and total cremation can permanently destroy the cursed tissue. Certain anti-undead magic can also sever the curse from the body and produce true death.
entries.name: 🩸Ghoul Immortality & Regeneration

entries.content:
Every Ghoul can manifest an individual supernatural gift beyond the race's shared hunger, senses, claws, immortality, and regeneration.

These gifts vary enormously. Known expressions include telepathy, heightened supernatural charm, pyrokinesis, blood manipulation, spirit perception, shadow abilities, unusual regeneration, emotion sensing, and extremely rare reality-altering effects.

A personal gift often reflects some aspect of the Ghoul's mortal identity, strongest obsession, circumstances of death, emotional nature, or the particular form of the curse that transformed them.

Training expands precision and versatility, while feeding determines how much supernatural output the Ghoul can sustain.

Two Ghouls may possess similar abilities, but exact expression is rarely identical.
entries.name: 👑Ghoul Unique Powers

entries.content:
Sunlight weakens and injures Ghouls but does not normally destroy them instantly.

Direct exposure causes pain, skin irritation, blistering, muscle weakness, slowed regeneration, and eventually deep burns. Long exposure can leave a Ghoul partially immobilized.

Severity varies by individual curse strength and unique gifts. Some can tolerate overcast daylight or brief direct exposure, while others become incapacitated quickly.

Clothing, shade, enclosed vehicles, subterranean spaces, and supernatural protection reduce exposure.

Sunlight damage consumes flesh-derived reserves as the body attempts to repair itself, so a hungry Ghoul is significantly more vulnerable during the day.
entries.name: ☀Ghoul Sunlight Weakness

entries.content:
Fire is one of the most reliable methods of permanently damaging a Ghoul.

Ordinary cuts and fractures are restored according to the undead template, but burned tissue is much harder for the curse to reconstruct. Deep burns heal slowly and can remain scarred even after feeding.

Enough heat can overwhelm regeneration entirely.

Complete cremation is a reliable method of true death because it destroys the cursed tissue faster than the Ghoul can restore a coherent body.

Ghouls with fire-related personal gifts may possess greater tolerance, but actual immunity is rare.
entries.name: 🔥Ghoul Fire Weakness

entries.content:
Pure silver disrupts the curse animating Ghoul tissue.

Contact causes painful burning and leaves marks that persist much longer than ordinary injuries. Silver blades and projectiles penetrate more effectively than comparable steel weapons because regeneration struggles to close the contaminated wound.

Silver embedded in the body can continuously suppress healing until removed.

The metal is not automatically fatal on contact. Its value is that it turns normally temporary injuries into wounds the Ghoul cannot immediately erase.

Because the effect is supernatural rather than purely chemical, sufficiently powerful Ghoul mutations or unique gifts can alter the severity without removing the general racial vulnerability.
entries.name: 🍴Ghoul Silver Weakness

entries.content:
Ghoulhood is a curse of undeath rather than a naturally contagious virus.

A new Ghoul is normally created when a living or recently dead human is subjected to a deliberate Ghoul curse, necromantic rite, powerful supernatural contamination, or an inherited curse that activates at death.

The transformation reanimates the body, suppresses ordinary aging and sleep, hardens bones and teeth, alters the senses, and installs the permanent hunger for humanoid flesh.

A Ghoul bite alone does not normally transform a victim. This is one of the major practical differences between Ghouls and Zombies.

The new Ghoul generally awakens with personal memories intact, making the first hunger psychologically destabilizing because the individual understands what the body now demands.

The personal supernatural gift usually manifests during transformation or within the first major feeding period.
entries.name: 🪦Ghoul Origin & Transformation

entries.content:
Ghouls often organize into **covens**, packs, houses, or underground communities because reliable feeding access, secrecy, and protection are easier to maintain collectively.

A coven can function simultaneously as family, feeding cooperative, political organization, and territorial authority. Membership may be voluntary, inherited through a sire or creator relationship, or earned through usefulness and loyalty.

Covens commonly maintain access to cemeteries, morgues, battlefields, medical waste, criminal disposal routes, or other sources of human remains.

Status tends to depend on age, control of hunger, unique supernatural power, useful skills, territory, knowledge, and the ability to secure food without exposing the wider species.

Independent Ghouls also exist. They are often called solitary or covenless Ghouls and may live successfully if they can maintain feeding and secrecy alone.

This entry describes Ghoul social structure generally; named local covens are not part of the global race definition.
entries.name: 🏙Ghoul Society & Covens

entries.content:
Ghoul culture is shaped by immortal memory, sleeplessness, and the ethics of feeding on the dead.

Many Ghouls treat remains as food rather than as symbolically untouchable bodies, creating a cultural divide between undead necessity and living-human burial customs.

Well-organized communities develop rules for acquisition, corpse ownership, cemetery access, treatment of known deceased persons, and whether killing for food is acceptable.

Because they never sleep, Ghouls have enormous uninterrupted stretches of time for reading, crafts, surveillance, art, research, work, and long-term planning.

Older Ghouls may remember historical periods firsthand and preserve knowledge that has vanished from human archives.

Feasts can carry social or ritual importance, especially when a large body supply is shared after war, disaster, or sanctioned acquisition.
entries.name: 📚Ghoul Culture

entries.content:
Ghoul law exists to prevent hunger from destroying whatever coexistence or secrecy the species has managed to build.

Common principles include:

1. **Law of Secrecy** — Do not publicly expose Ghoul existence or leave unmistakable supernatural feeding evidence.
2. **Law of Remains** — Claimed or legally acquired bodies cannot simply be stolen from another Ghoul or community.
3. **Law of the Living** — Killing living humans solely because a corpse supply is inconvenient is restricted or forbidden in organized communities.
4. **Law of Hunger Responsibility** — A Ghoul who knows starvation is eroding control must seek food, confinement, or help before becoming Hollow in public.
5. **Law of Silver and Fire** — Using anti-Ghoul weaknesses against another Ghoul outside legitimate defense is treated as aggravated assault or attempted execution.
6. **Law of Creation** — Deliberately creating a new Ghoul carries responsibility for its first feeding, education, and control.
7. **Law of Coven Sanctuary** — Neutral feeding sites, healers, refuges, and protected burial stores are not ordinary battlegrounds.
8. **Law of the Dead Mind** — Magical extraction of memories from consumed remains is regulated where such abilities exist.

Punishment can include feeding restrictions, confinement, territory loss, exile, magical binding, or true execution by fire or anti-undead magic.
entries.name: ⚖Ghoul Laws

entries.content:
Zombies are viral living-dead whose bodies remain ambulatory after biological death or near-death because a supernatural infection rewrites the nervous system and metabolism.

Unlike Ghouls, their dietary requirement is extremely specific: **Zombies must eat human brains.** Other human flesh does not maintain higher cognition.

A well-fed Zombie can retain normal intelligence, personality, speech, emotional range, employment, relationships, technical skill, and social behavior closely enough to pass for an unusually pale living human.

The popular image of a shambling mindless Zombie represents the **starved feral endpoint**, not the healthy baseline of the race.

Zombies spread primarily through infected bodily fluids. Scratches, bites, contaminated blood, open wounds, and intimate fluid exchange can transmit the virus to living humans.

Because infection can spread accidentally, Zombie society places unusually heavy importance on food access and transmission control.
entries.name: 🧟Zombies

entries.content:
Zombie transformation produces a distinctive but often concealable phenotype.

Skin becomes pale and cool, frequently approaching a gray or porcelain tone. Natural hair progressively loses pigment until it becomes **chalk-white or nearly white** regardless of its original color.

The resting heartbeat slows to approximately **six beats per minute**. Blood pressure and circulation become correspondingly low because ordinary oxygen delivery is no longer the body's primary survival mechanism.

The eyes usually remain normal enough to pass as human when the Zombie is calm and fed. During extreme hunger or Full-On Zombie Mode, the eyes can become unnaturally red and dark vascular patterns become visible through the face.

Body temperature remains below the normal human range, and pulse checks can easily cause an uninformed medical professional to assume the person is dying or already dead.
entries.name: 🧟Zombie Appearance & Vitals

entries.content:
Zombie physiology is organized around a transformed brain and nervous system rather than a normal living metabolism.

The virus drastically reduces the body's need for oxygen, blood pressure, and continuous organ function. The heart continues beating very slowly, but circulation mainly distributes residual fluids and supports tissue maintenance rather than sustaining ordinary human life.

Blood loss is rarely fatal by itself. Zombies can survive surgeries, wounds, organ trauma, and physical damage that would kill a human through shock or exsanguination.

Pain is still perceived, but the body does not automatically shut down from pain, blood loss, or ordinary trauma.

The brain remains the central organ. Memory, identity, motor control, viral regulation, and undead animation all depend on enough intact neural tissue.

Complete destruction of the Zombie's brain or brainstem is therefore one of the most reliable methods of permanent death.
entries.name: 🧟Zombie Physiology

entries.content:
Human brain tissue is the only food capable of fully sustaining a Zombie's transformed nervous system.

A healthy Zombie must consume a substantial amount of **human brain at least once per week**. One full adult brain generally contains enough specialized neural material to maintain higher cognition for roughly a weekly cycle, although activity, injury, Full-On Zombie Mode, and individual metabolism can shorten that period.

Other human flesh may be swallowed but does not provide the neurological factors the virus requires. Animal brains are similarly inadequate as a long-term substitute.

Brain tissue maintains language, memory stability, impulse control, executive function, emotional regulation, and the ability to suppress feral hunting behavior.

Regular access to brains is therefore both a nutritional issue and a public-safety issue. A Zombie deprived of brains is not merely hungry; its higher mind is progressively shutting down.
entries.name: 🧠Zombie Brain Diet

entries.content:
Zombie taste is heavily dulled compared with human taste.

Ordinary sweet, salty, bitter, sour, and savory flavors become muted enough that normal meals may seem bland or nearly flavorless.

Extreme capsaicin remains one of the few sensations strong enough to cut through the sensory dulling. As a result, Zombies commonly season food—and especially prepared brain dishes—with **very hot sauce, chilies, or intense spice**.

Ordinary food can still be eaten socially and may provide limited physical bulk, but it does not replace the human-brain requirement.

Individual Zombies often develop extremely high spice tolerance because their altered pain and taste systems respond differently from living humans.

Food culture in organized Zombie communities therefore tends to revolve around disguising brain dishes as ordinary cuisine and using aggressive seasoning to restore a sense of flavor.
entries.name: 🧠Zombie Taste & Food

entries.content:
When a Zombie consumes human brain tissue, fragments of the deceased person's stored neural information can temporarily imprint onto the Zombie's transformed brain.

The most dramatic expression is a **vision**: a sudden involuntary flashback experienced from the deceased person's perspective. A smell, location, person, phrase, emotional situation, or object associated with the original memory can trigger one.

Visions can contain images, sounds, emotions, sensory details, and fragments of events the Zombie never personally experienced.

The Zombie does not receive the donor's entire autobiography in an organized form. The transferred information is fragmented and often appears unpredictably.

Repeated portions from the same brain can deepen the imprint and increase the chance that relevant memories surface.

Because visions can reveal crimes, secrets, hidden locations, relationships, or final moments, some Zombies become unusually effective investigators.
entries.name: 🧠Zombie Memory & Vision Absorption

entries.content:
Brain consumption can temporarily transfer more than memories.

A Zombie may inherit fragments of the deceased person's personality, habits, preferences, emotional reactions, native language, procedural memory, or trained skills.

A brain from a martial artist may temporarily improve fighting technique. A forensic specialist may provide investigative habits. A multilingual person may make an otherwise unknown language temporarily accessible. A musician may transfer instrument familiarity.

These borrowed traits do not permanently replace the Zombie's identity. They overlay it.

The strength and duration of the imprint varies with the amount consumed, the donor's expertise, emotional intensity, and the Zombie's own neural stability.

Strong personality traits can become inconvenient or dangerous because the Zombie may temporarily behave in ways that feel natural even though the impulses belong to someone else.

Most imprints gradually fade as the consumed neural material is metabolized.
entries.name: 🧠Zombie Trait & Skill Absorption

entries.content:
Brain-derived memories, skills, and personality traits are temporary because the Zombie virus uses consumed neural tissue as both nutrition and informational substrate.

Fresh imprints are strongest during the first days after feeding. They weaken as the brain material is metabolized and are usually largely replaced by the next major feeding.

A Zombie's own personality remains the underlying identity. Borrowed traits may influence mood, body language, cravings, phobias, hobbies, vocabulary, and instinctive decisions without permanently rewriting the self.

Extremely traumatic donor memories can persist longer because strong emotional encoding creates deeper neural resonance.

Experienced Zombies learn to identify the difference between **my memory** and **brain memory**, reducing confusion when visions occur.

Psychological support is important for Zombies who routinely consume brains from violent deaths, because repeatedly experiencing strangers' trauma can produce genuine secondary trauma.
entries.name: 🧠Brain Imprint Duration & Integration

entries.content:
A Zombie deprived of human brain tissue progressively loses higher cognitive function.

**Early Deprivation:** irritability, brain fixation, poorer concentration, intrusive hunger, reduced emotional control.

**Cognitive Slippage:** memory problems, simplified speech, impulsive decisions, reduced empathy, and difficulty suppressing hunting instincts.

**Feral Transition:** language collapses, posture and movement become more predatory, social identity fades, and the Zombie begins actively hunting humans for brains.

**Full Feral State:** only basic recognition, hunger, threat response, and simple learned behavior remain.

The original personality is not necessarily erased immediately. It becomes inaccessible as the undead brain loses the biochemical and supernatural support required for higher cognition.

Timely brain feeding can reverse much of the process before permanent neural damage occurs.
entries.name: 🧟Feral Zombie Degeneration

entries.content:
**Full-On Zombie Mode**, commonly abbreviated **FOZM**, is an emergency predatory state triggered by extreme anger, terror, pain, adrenaline, mortal threat, or overwhelming protective instinct.

The eyes turn vivid blood-red. Dark veins become prominent across the face and around the eyes. Muscular output, speed, agility, reflexes, and pain tolerance increase dramatically.

FOZM temporarily removes many of the body's ordinary self-protective restraints. A Zombie can strike harder, run faster, continue fighting through major injury, and react with predatory speed.

The state consumes brain-derived neurological reserves rapidly and intensifies hunger afterward.

A disciplined Zombie can learn to enter or suppress FOZM deliberately, but emotional triggering remains possible.

FOZM is not the same as starvation-induced ferality. A well-fed intelligent Zombie in FOZM can still recognize allies, make decisions, and remember what happened afterward.
entries.name: 🔴Full-On Zombie Mode — FOZM

entries.content:
A calm, well-fed Zombie is physically tougher than a human but does not constantly display extreme superhuman strength.

Their undead tissues resist fatigue, blood-loss shock, pain collapse, and oxygen deprivation. This allows them to continue exerting themselves after injuries that would disable a living human.

FOZM unlocks the race's major combat enhancement: superhuman strength, speed, agility, reaction time, coordination, and pain tolerance.

The exact output varies by individual fitness and neurological reserves. A trained athlete turned Zombie remains more technically capable than an untrained Zombie even when both enter FOZM.

Physical enhancement consumes stored brain-derived resources. Repeated FOZM episodes without feeding accelerate cognitive hunger and feral degeneration.

Zombies therefore possess enormous emergency performance but pay for it through increased neurological feeding demand.
entries.name: 🔴Zombie Physical Abilities

entries.content:
Zombies possess extreme trauma tolerance rather than the near-instant regenerative biology of some other undead.

They do not die simply because blood volume falls below human-survival limits, and ordinary shock responses are dramatically reduced.

Severe wounds still damage tissue and can impair movement. A destroyed knee remains mechanically damaged until repaired, even if the Zombie stays conscious.

Medical treatment, surgery, stitching, stabilization, and time can therefore matter. Zombies can survive procedures that would be impossible on living patients because anesthesia, blood pressure, and blood replacement are less critical.

Brain feeding accelerates general tissue maintenance but primarily supports the nervous system rather than rebuilding an entire body instantly.

Complete brain destruction, total cranial destruction, or cremation remains capable of permanent death.
entries.name: 🩸Zombie Trauma Resistance & Regeneration

entries.content:
Zombie transformation is caused by a supernatural virus carried in Zombie bodily fluids.

Transmission can occur through scratches contaminated with infected fluid, bites, blood-to-blood exposure, open wounds, contaminated medical material, and intimate adult fluid exchange.

Casual skin contact, conversation, sharing a room, or touching intact dry skin does not normally transmit the virus.

The infectious dose matters. Deep contaminated wounds and direct blood exposure carry much greater risk than brief surface contact.

Once established, the virus moves toward the nervous system and begins rewriting metabolism, circulation, pigmentation, and brain chemistry.

A newly infected person may initially appear ill rather than undead, making early transmission difficult to recognize without supernatural or medical testing.
entries.name: 🦠Zombie Virus & Infection

entries.content:
Creating a new Zombie through infection is commonly called **siring** even though no bloodline bond is required.

After infection takes hold, the victim passes through fever, neurological disturbance, reduced pulse, falling body temperature, pallor, altered appetite, and progressive sensory changes.

Hair pigmentation fades toward chalk-white as the transformed metabolism stabilizes.

The first intense craving for human brain tissue marks the point at which the new Zombie's higher cognition becomes nutritionally dependent on feeding.

The newly transformed person normally retains pre-infection memories and identity as long as the brain remains adequately fed.

Unlike a vampire sire bond, the Zombie who transmitted the virus does not automatically gain psychic control over the new Zombie.

Because scratches and fluid exchange can spread the condition accidentally, responsible Zombies are expected to disclose and manage transmission risk with informed adult partners and medical personnel.
entries.name: 🦠Zombie Siring & Transformation

entries.content:
Zombie communities treat infection control as a basic survival requirement.

Fresh wounds should be covered before close physical contact. Blood and other potentially infectious fluids require careful handling. Shared needles and unsterilized invasive tools are high-risk.

Scratching is particularly dangerous because Zombie nails or fingers can carry infected bodily fluid into broken skin even when the injury appears minor.

Intimate adult relationships require awareness that fluid exchange can transmit the virus. Barrier methods reduce risk but do not make every type of exposure impossible.

Medical workers who knowingly treat Zombies use specialized contamination protocols and clearly separate infectious material from ordinary clinical waste.

Deliberately infecting someone without consent is treated as one of the most serious Zombie crimes because the condition permanently changes diet, physiology, secrecy obligations, and risk to others.
entries.name: 🦠Zombie Infection Control

entries.content:
Zombie senses change rather than uniformly becoming superhuman.

Smell becomes unusually sensitive to exposed human brain tissue and certain neurological chemicals. A hungry Zombie may detect a fresh brain with startling accuracy.

Taste becomes dramatically weaker except for extreme spice.

Pain perception is partially dulled, especially during FOZM, allowing continued movement through injuries that would incapacitate a human.

Vision and hearing remain near-human in ordinary conditions, though FOZM sharpens visual tracking, reaction speed, and threat awareness.

Brain imprints can temporarily create sensory habits belonging to the donor, such as a musician's pitch discrimination, a detective's observational patterning, or an athlete's spatial awareness.
entries.name: 🧟Zombie Senses

entries.content:
Functional Zombie society depends on a stable, concealed supply of human brains.

Organized communities may obtain brains from morgues, donated bodies, medical systems, supernatural food networks, criminal sources, or other controlled channels.

A legitimate supply is enormously valuable because it prevents otherwise rational Zombies from degenerating into dangerous feral predators.

Brains may be portioned, preserved, frozen, cooked, or incorporated into heavily seasoned dishes as long as enough viable neural material remains to support the virus.

Supply workers, medical personnel, and supernatural administrators often become some of the most politically important members of Zombie society because food distribution is directly tied to public safety.

Black-market brains also exist, particularly where legal or ethical supply is insufficient.
entries.name: 🏙Zombie Society & Brain Supply

entries.content:
Zombie cuisine develops around two facts: brains are mandatory and ordinary taste is severely dulled.

Recipes are designed to disguise texture, preserve neural material, and carry intense spice. Brain tacos, curries, stir-fries, soups, sandwiches, pastas, dumplings, and other preparations can all function if enough actual human brain remains.

Hot sauce is culturally ubiquitous because capsaicin produces a sensory intensity Zombies can still perceive strongly.

Different brains can also produce different psychological experiences because donor traits and memories accompany the meal. Choosing a brain is therefore partly nutritional and partly a decision about what temporary personality influence the Zombie is willing to tolerate.

Responsible communities label donor information where possible so consumers can avoid brains associated with severe trauma, dangerous addictions, or skills that may interfere with current responsibilities.

Eating becomes both nutrition and temporary identity management.
entries.name: 🌶Zombie Food Culture

entries.content:
Memory absorption gives Zombies a unique role in supernatural investigation.

A brain taken from a deceased victim can produce involuntary visions of locations, faces, arguments, injuries, relationships, or the circumstances surrounding death.

Skill absorption may temporarily provide the victim's professional expertise, language ability, technical knowledge, or behavioral familiarity with a relevant place.

These abilities are powerful but unreliable. Visions are fragmentary, triggers are unpredictable, and personality overlays can bias interpretation.

Brain-derived memories should therefore be treated as supernatural evidence requiring corroboration rather than perfect recordings.

Ethically regulated communities may require legal permission before investigative consumption of a known deceased person's brain because the process exposes private memories as well as useful evidence.
entries.name: 🧠Zombie Investigative Use of Brains

entries.content:
Zombie law focuses on feeding, infection, memory privacy, and prevention of feral outbreaks.

Common principles include:

1. **Law of Brain Supply** — Do not sabotage communal food systems or deliberately starve dependent Zombies.
2. **Law of Infection** — Deliberately transmitting the virus without informed consent is a major crime.
3. **Law of Wounds** — Zombies must take reasonable precautions when bleeding, scratching, or handling infectious material around humans.
4. **Law of Feeding** — Human brains must be obtained through sanctioned, donated, legally acquired, or otherwise community-approved channels where such systems exist.
5. **Law of Memory Privacy** — Consuming a known person's brain does not automatically grant the right to publicly reveal every private memory absorbed.
6. **Law of Feral Responsibility** — A Zombie approaching dangerous deprivation must seek food, treatment, or voluntary containment.
7. **Law of FOZM** — Emergency transformation does not excuse deliberate violence committed after control is regained.
8. **Law of Siring** — A person who knowingly creates a new Zombie is responsible for explaining feeding needs, transmission risks, and concealment.
9. **Law of the Veil** — Public exposure of the Zombie population is restricted to protect both humans and undead.

Penalties include quarantine, feeding supervision, restricted access to humans, imprisonment, exile, or permanent execution for repeated catastrophic offenses.
entries.name: ⚖Zombie Laws

entries.content:
Zombies are extraordinarily difficult to kill through ordinary human trauma but have clear limits.

**Brain Destruction:** The transformed brain is the central organ of Zombie identity and animation. Sufficient destruction of the brain or brainstem is permanently lethal.

**Cremation:** Complete destruction of the body and brain through extreme heat prevents continued animation.

**Starvation:** Brain deprivation usually does not kill quickly, but it destroys higher cognition and creates a feral predator.

**Neurological Damage:** Injuries that remove specific brain regions can impair memory, speech, movement, personality, or viral regulation even if the Zombie remains technically alive.

**Anti-Undead Magic:** Powerful magic can suppress, purge, or sever the supernatural component of the virus.

**FOZM Exhaustion:** Repeated emergency transformation rapidly consumes neurological reserves and can accelerate starvation.

Blood loss, ordinary disease, and conventional organ failure are far less reliable methods of killing a Zombie than they are against a human.
entries.name: ⚠️Zombie Weaknesses & Death

entries.content:
Although both races are Carrion Undead, they behave very differently.

**Base Mind:** Ghouls normally preserve their original mind permanently unless starvation buries it. Zombies require regular brains to chemically and supernaturally maintain higher cognition.

**Food:** Ghouls consume broad human/humanoid flesh and can strip a body to bone. Zombies require specifically human brain tissue.

**Feeding Effect:** Ghoul flesh primarily restores strength, regeneration, and curse stability. Zombie brains also transfer memories, personality traits, languages, and skills.

**Sleep:** Ghouls are naturally sleepless. Zombies can rest and sleep because their transformed nervous system still cycles through periods of reduced activity.

**Creation:** Ghoulhood is usually curse-based or necromantic and is not automatically contagious. Zombiehood spreads through a transmissible virus carried in bodily fluids.

**Starvation:** A Ghoul becomes a conscious Hollow and can remain starved indefinitely. A Zombie progressively loses higher cognition and becomes a classic mindless feral.

**Emergency Power:** Zombies possess FOZM. Ghouls instead rely on permanent undead strength, regeneration, senses, and an individual unique supernatural gift.

**Major Weakness:** Ghouls are strongly vulnerable to sunlight, silver, and fire. Zombies are most reliably killed through catastrophic brain destruction or complete cremation.
entries.name: ⚠️Ghoul vs Zombie — Practical Differences

entries.content:
Kresnik senses are specifically optimized for finding supernatural prey.

They can distinguish living human blood from vampire blood, detect the unnatural stillness of undead bodies, notice magical disturbances left by feeding, and identify the scent or energetic residue of a vampire that recently passed through an area.

Older Kresniks can often estimate vampire age, hunger state, injury, or bloodline strength from subtle sensory clues.

Their tracking is not omniscient. Heavy rain, strong magic, dimensional movement, deliberate masking, and dense supernatural populations can obscure a trail.

Because their senses are purpose-built rather than merely heightened, a Kresnik can sometimes notice a vampire that has successfully fooled ordinary humans, cameras, or animal trackers.
entries.name: 💀Kresnik Senses & Vampire Tracking

entries.content:
Kresnik bodies recover from injury far faster than human bodies because living tissue is reinforced by engineered supernatural energy.

Cuts and fractures can repair rapidly, severe internal injuries can stabilize without ordinary medicine, and the body resists infection and blood-loss shock.

Unlike vampire regeneration, Kresnik healing remains a living biological process. It requires energy, nutrition, hydration, and intact tissue rather than simply restoring an undead template.

Powerful magic, Original-level wounds, extreme bodily destruction, or attacks specifically designed to disrupt Kresnik physiology can overwhelm recovery.

Vampire blood can accelerate healing because the Kresnik metabolism is designed to process vampiric essence safely.
entries.name: ☀Kresnik Healing & Recovery

entries.content:
Kresnik power is biological, but effective hunting is a learned discipline.

Young Kresniks train in supernatural identification, vampire psychology, tracking, anti-compulsion awareness, magical containment, close combat, ranged weapons, first aid, evacuation, and evidence control.

They are taught to separate **species detection** from **proof of wrongdoing** so natural predatory instinct does not become an excuse for indiscriminate killing.

Magic training emphasizes wards, immobilization, battlefield control, escape prevention, and protection of civilians before destructive output.

A mature Kresnik is therefore dangerous because physical power, magic, investigation, and tactical preparation reinforce one another.
entries.name: ⚔Kresnik Training & Hunter Development

entries.content:
Ghoul nourishment varies with the condition of consumed humanoid tissue.

Fresh remains provide the greatest regenerative value because cellular structure and residual life resonance are still intact. Refrigerated or properly frozen flesh remains highly usable for much longer.

Decomposed tissue can still sustain a Ghoul because its undead digestion is resistant to bacteria and ordinary foodborne toxins, but heavily decayed flesh provides less efficient nourishment.

Embalming chemicals, strong poisons, magical contamination, radiation, and anti-undead substances can make a corpse dangerous even to Ghouls.

Organized Ghoul communities therefore use cold storage, preservation, sealed transport, and careful source records rather than relying entirely on grave robbery.
entries.name: 🍖Ghoul Flesh Quality, Freshness & Preservation

entries.content:
Consumed flesh can retain faint supernatural impressions of the person it once belonged to.

Most Ghouls experience these only as vague emotional flavors: fear, calm, anger, illness, age, or the residual sense of a violent death.

Ghouls whose unique gift interacts with memory, spirits, blood, or psychic energy can perceive much more. For them, eating a specific piece of flesh may produce images, sensations, names, or fragments of the deceased person's experience.

Unlike Zombie brain visions, memory echoes are not a universal Ghoul ability and do not automatically transfer skills or personality.

This distinction is important: Zombie neural absorption is standard racial biology, while detailed Ghoul memory-feeding requires an appropriate personal supernatural gift.
entries.name: ✨Ghoul Memory Echoes in Flesh

entries.content:
Unlike naturally sleepless Ghouls, Zombies can sleep.

Their transformed brain no longer requires sleep at exactly the same rate as a living human, but periods of reduced neural activity help integrate consumed memories, stabilize personality, repair attention, and reduce FOZM irritability.

A well-fed Zombie can stay awake far longer than a human without immediate impairment, yet chronic sleep deprivation still increases confusion and makes borrowed brain traits harder to separate from personal identity.

Dreams can contain mixtures of the Zombie's own memories and fragments absorbed from recently consumed brains.

Feral starvation eventually destroys normal sleep patterns because hunger repeatedly forces the nervous system back into hunting behavior.
entries.name: 🧟Zombie Sleep, Rest & Circadian Function

entries.content:
A stable Zombie ages far more slowly than a living human because the virus continuously repairs many forms of ordinary cellular decline.

Transformation generally preserves the apparent age at which infection stabilized, although gradual changes can still occur over decades.

Regular brain feeding maintains neurological integrity and prevents the body from entering visible decay. A well-fed Zombie can remain physically stable for an exceptionally long time.

Repeated starvation, untreated injuries, chronic infection stress, severe brain damage, and frequent FOZM use accelerate visible deterioration.

Zombies are functionally ageless under ideal conditions but not absolutely immortal. Destruction of the brain, cremation, powerful anti-undead magic, or accumulated irreversible neural damage can permanently end the organism.
entries.name: 🧟Zombie Aging, Lifespan & Long-Term Stability

entries.content:
Gorgons are living serpent-aspected humanoids whose defining traits are living serpents in place of ordinary hair and a supernatural gaze capable of mineralizing living tissue into stone. They are a naturally reproducing race, though rare magical curses can also create Gorgon-like individuals.

Their permanent true body is humanoid rather than serpentine from the waist down. Skin can be humanlike or carry scales around the temples, throat, spine, forearms, hips, or legs. Eyes are often metallic, luminous, unusually vivid, or slit-pupiled.

Gorgons are fully sapient and are not inherently hostile. Their dangerous gaze is a biological-magical function that can be controlled with practice, making training and eye etiquette central parts of ordinary life.
entries.name: 🐍Gorgons

entries.content:
The serpents growing from a Gorgon’s scalp are living extensions of the same body, not separate pets. They share blood supply, nerves, magical energy, and sensation with the Gorgon while retaining limited independent movement and instinct.

Each serpent can see, smell, taste airborne chemicals, sense heat and vibration, and focus in a different direction. Their combined input gives the Gorgon unusually strong awareness around and behind the head.

The snakes can hiss, sleep, coil, bare fangs, react to threats, or investigate nearby objects. Severing one is painful like losing a finger; regrowth is possible if the root survives but can take months and may leave altered coloration or scarring.
entries.name: 🐍Gorgon Physiology & Serpent Hair

entries.content:
A Gorgon’s gaze creates a direct magical resonance between the eyes and a visible target, converting living tissue into magically stabilized stone.

Control exists on a spectrum. A trained Gorgon can make ordinary harmless eye contact, induce temporary stiffness, partially petrify a limb, place someone into temporary full petrification, or deliberately create permanent stone.

Young, frightened, injured, or emotionally overwhelmed Gorgons may trigger the power unintentionally. Closed eyes, opaque blindfolds, sufficiently strong visual wards, or simply refusing direct visual connection prevent normal activation.

The strongest gaze can spread through a target in seconds, while controlled partial effects can be deliberately slowed or confined.
entries.name: 👁Gorgon Petrifying Gaze

entries.content:
Petrification transforms the target into a unified magical mineral state rather than merely coating flesh with rock. Clothing and objects in close contact may be caught in the conversion as well.

Temporary petrification preserves the victim’s living template and reverses cleanly when released. Permanent petrification can still be undone by the originating Gorgon, a carefully designed reversal spell, powerful restoration magic, or specialized alchemy.

Breaking a petrified body is extremely dangerous. Restoring a shattered statue without correctly reassembling it can return the victim with catastrophic injuries or missing anatomy.

A permanently petrified person is therefore treated as a living person in magical suspension rather than as an ordinary statue.
entries.name: 👁Petrification Reversal & Stone State

entries.content:
Many Gorgons possess retractable fangs in the humanoid mouth, the scalp serpents, or both. Their venom is usually neurotoxic and magically paralytic rather than instantly lethal.

A typical bite causes burning pain, muscle weakness, slowed reflexes, and temporary paralysis. This naturally complements the gaze by making precise petrification easier.

Bloodlines vary. Some venom sedates, some damages tissue, some interferes with supernatural regeneration, and a few causes temporary sensory hallucinations.

Gorgons are highly resistant to their own venom and usually resistant to close relatives’ venom, although concentrated exposure can still cause illness.
entries.name: 🐍Gorgon Venom & Fangs

entries.content:
Gorgons combine humanoid senses with the distributed awareness of their serpent hair. Heat, vibration, scent, motion, and air changes can be noticed from multiple directions at once.

Many Gorgons also possess a weak Stone Sense. A person or creature petrified by their own gaze carries a familiar magical resonance that can be recognized by touch or at short range.

Stone Sense is strongest with the Gorgon’s own petrification and much weaker with ordinary rock or someone petrified by another Gorgon.

Crowds can overwhelm young Gorgons because dozens of serpent eyes and tongues may react to different stimuli simultaneously.
entries.name: 🐍Gorgon Senses & Stone Perception

entries.content:
Gorgons reproduce biologically and form stable family lines. Most lineages are live-bearing, though rare ancient lines produce soft-shelled magical eggs.

Children are born without a fully active petrifying gaze. The eye magic develops gradually with the nervous system, giving families time to teach safety before lethal output becomes possible.

The first accidental mineralization is considered a major developmental milestone and usually results in immediate control training.

Gorgon-human or other compatible humanoid hybrids can inherit partial traits such as a few living serpents among ordinary hair, scaled patches, slit pupils, venom, or a weaker gaze.
entries.name: 🥚Gorgon Reproduction & Development

entries.content:
Gorgon culture treats eye contact as meaningful because it can carry real physical danger. Direct eye contact may signal trust, challenge, intimacy, honesty, or deliberate vulnerability depending on context.

Veils, tinted glasses, enchanted lenses, mirrored jewelry, and decorative eye coverings are ordinary tools rather than symbols of shame.

Serpent grooming is both hair care and body care. Oils, warming stones, scale brushes, ornaments, and tiny protective jewelry for individual serpents are common.

Stonework has complicated cultural meaning. Some Gorgons avoid sculpture because of its association with petrification, while others become exceptional sculptors and mineral artisans.
entries.name: 🏛Gorgon Culture & Eye Etiquette

entries.content:
Gorgon law centers on responsible use of the gaze. Deliberate permanent petrification without lawful cause is murder, while reckless uncontrolled gaze use is treated like mishandling a deadly supernatural weapon.

Destroying or stealing a petrified person is a major crime because the victim may still be recoverable. Forcibly damaging a Gorgon’s eyes or serpent network is likewise treated as severe bodily assault.

Communities commonly require young Gorgons to demonstrate basic gaze control before entering crowded public spaces without protective eyewear.

Using petrification for imprisonment, medicine, preservation, or emergency protection requires consent or legal authority.
entries.name: ⚖Gorgon Laws

entries.content:
Gorgons are living supernatural humanoids and can be killed by sufficient blood loss, organ destruction, disease, poison, fire, decapitation, or other severe trauma.

Anti-magic can suppress the petrifying gaze and disrupt supernatural venom. Damage to the scalp-serpent network causes severe pain, sensory confusion, and loss of surrounding awareness.

Reflective environments can be tactically dangerous because a deliberately focused gaze may carry through reflections in weakened form or rebound unpredictably.

Blindness removes the normal gaze pathway but does not erase the Gorgon’s other senses or serpent awareness. A Gorgon without functioning eyes remains a full person rather than becoming magically powerless in every respect.
entries.name: ⚠Gorgon Weaknesses & Limits

entries.content:
Beastfolk are born humanoid-animal hybrids whose mixed body is their permanent true form. They are neither Werebeasts nor Beastweres and require no transformation to access their animal traits.

A Beastfolk individual may have animal ears, tail, fur, scales, claws, paws, hooves, wings, horns, feathers, whiskers, altered eyes, muzzles, digitigrade legs, gills, or other features depending on lineage.

Some are almost human except for ears and tail; others are strongly anthropomorphic animals with full fur, scales, animal-shaped heads, paws, or wings. Expression level does not change intelligence or personhood.

The defining rule is: **Beastfolk = stable humanoid-animal hybrid from birth.**
entries.name: 🐾Beastfolk

entries.content:
Beastfolk are biologically separate from transformation-based animal races.

**Beastfolk:** permanent humanoid-animal hybrid true form.
**Werebeast:** human true form that transforms into animal or hybrid.
**Beastwere:** animal true form that temporarily becomes humanlike.

A wolf Beastfolk, Werewolf, and Wolfwere can therefore all possess wolf traits while having completely different childhoods, medical needs, instincts, and transformation rules.

Beastfolk generally cannot become fully human or fully animal unless they separately possess shapeshifting magic.
entries.name: 🐾Beastfolk vs Werebeasts & Beastweres

entries.content:
Beastfolk anatomy ranges from lightly expressed to heavily anthropomorphic.

Light-expression individuals may have mostly human bodies with animal ears, tail, eyes, claws, fangs, or small fur patches. Mixed-expression individuals can have digitigrade legs, paws, muzzles, extensive fur, feathers, scales, horns, wings, or powerful tails.

Heavy-expression Beastfolk resemble upright sapient animals with functional hands and human-level speech and reasoning.

Traits must remain anatomically coherent. Functional wings require reinforced shoulders and enlarged respiratory systems; aquatic traits require compatible gills and circulation; large tails alter balance, seating, and clothing.
entries.name: 🐾Beastfolk Phenotype Spectrum

entries.content:
Beastfolk physiology integrates humanoid organs with real animal adaptations rather than attaching cosmetic traits to a human body.

Feline lineages may possess flexible spines, retractable claws, exceptional balance, and low-light vision. Canine lineages emphasize scent, hearing, stamina, and social recognition. Reptilian lineages may possess scales, tails, altered temperature regulation, or unusual metabolism.

Avian Beastfolk require lightweight reinforced bones and powerful chest musculature for true flight. Aquatic lineages may possess gills, webbing, pressure tolerance, and water-sensitive sensory organs.

Medical care must account for the individual’s actual lineage rather than assuming human anatomy under the visible traits.
entries.name: 🐾Beastfolk Physiology

entries.content:
Beastfolk inherit enhanced senses and instinctive tendencies from their animal lineage while retaining full sapient reasoning.

Animal ears may swivel automatically toward sound. Predatory lineages track sudden movement strongly; prey-species lineages often maintain wide peripheral awareness. Scent-oriented Beastfolk can recognize family, fear, illness, familiar rooms, and recent visitors through smell.

Instinct influences attention and emotional reflexes but does not dictate personality. A rabbit Beastfolk is not automatically timid, a wolf Beastfolk is not automatically dominant, and a cat Beastfolk is not automatically solitary.

Mature Beastfolk learn to interpret instinct as useful sensory information rather than as commands.
entries.name: 🐾Beastfolk Senses & Instincts

entries.content:
Beastfolk physical abilities depend on the animal structures actually present.

Predatory lineages may possess claws, fangs, powerful jaws, reflexes, or burst speed. Large mammalian lineages can have major strength and endurance. Hooved lineages may run efficiently, arboreal species climb naturally, and aquatic species swim with little training.

Natural weapons can break, dull, become infected, or require grooming. They are biological anatomy rather than indestructible magical equipment.

Beastfolk are not universally superior to humans in every category; their advantages are concentrated around the physiology of their lineage.
entries.name: 🐾Beastfolk Physical Abilities

entries.content:
Beastfolk diets reflect both humanoid digestion and ancestral animal biology.

Carnivorous lineages generally need more protein and fat. Herbivorous lineages can process larger amounts of plant fiber. Omnivorous lineages are highly flexible. Aquatic and avian lineages may have unusually high mineral, salt, hydration, or calorie requirements.

Foods toxic to the ancestral animal can remain dangerous in some bloodlines, though others have lost those restrictions through hybrid evolution.

Diet does not dictate personality or ethics. Any lineage can use culturally appropriate foods or substitutes as long as its actual nutritional requirements are met.
entries.name: 🐾Beastfolk Diet & Biological Needs

entries.content:
Beastfolk reproduce as living biological humanoids. Two Beastfolk of the same lineage usually produce children of that lineage with natural variation in expression.

Different lineages can have children when biologically compatible. Offspring usually inherit one dominant animal template with secondary traits from the other parent rather than an incoherent mixture of every structure.

A Beastfolk and a human can produce a Beastfolk child, a lightly expressed hybrid, or a mostly human child carrying dormant traits depending on inheritance.

Children are born with the anatomy they will grow into. Ears, tails, scales, fur, horns, or wings develop as normal body structures rather than appearing through a later curse.
entries.name: 🧬Beastfolk Reproduction & Inheritance

entries.content:
Beastfolk societies treat body diversity as an ordinary design requirement. Clothing can include tail openings, wing slits, horn clearance, ear-friendly hoods, digitigrade footwear, scale-safe fabrics, and adjustable sizing for different builds.

Furniture and architecture account for tails, wings, paws, claws, hooves, perches, climbing access, water areas, and different resting postures.

Ears, tails, wings, horns, whiskers, and fur are personal body parts. Touching them without permission is socially equivalent to touching any other sensitive part of someone’s body.

Mixed-lineage communities often develop accessibility systems far more varied than human-only spaces because a single building may serve dozens of stable body plans.
entries.name: 🏙Beastfolk Culture & Everyday Design

entries.content:
Beastfolk are living mortal beings. Lifespan varies by lineage but usually falls within human to long-lived humanoid ranges rather than supernatural immortality.

They can suffer blood loss, infection, disease, poison, broken bones, organ failure, and ordinary physical trauma. Animal-derived anatomy also creates lineage-specific vulnerabilities such as fragile wings, temperature sensitivity, respiratory needs, or extremely sensitive hearing.

Human medications, anesthesia, and dosages may not always be safe because metabolism can differ substantially.

Beastfolk have no universal silver weakness because their condition is stable biology rather than a transformation curse.
entries.name: ⚖Beastfolk Lifespan, Medicine & Weaknesses

entries.content:
True Dragons are enormous ancient supernatural reptiles whose natural bodies are scaled, winged or serpentine, heavily magical, and far larger than humans. Body plans vary between four-legged dragons, wyvern-like dragons, long serpentine dragons, aquatic dragons, feathered dragons, and other draconic lineages.

Dragons are fully sapient and possess language, culture, families, personal morality, long memory, and individual interests.

Most mature dragons can assume a human disguise through extreme magical compression. The human body is useful for interacting with smaller species but is never the dragon’s true form.

Their defining organ is the **Dragonheart**, a dense magical core that sustains breath weapons, flight, transformation, regeneration, and elemental power.
entries.name: 🐉True Dragons

entries.content:
The Dragonheart is a crystalline-organic magical organ integrated with the physical heart, lungs, spine, blood vessels, and nervous system.

It reinforces scales, bones, muscles, wings, claws, and internal organs while storing the enormous power required by draconic biology. Dragon bones are unusually strong for their weight and contain channels that conduct magic.

Specialized chambers around the lungs and throat condense elemental energy for breath attacks. Scales overlap in armored layers and continue thickening throughout life.

Dragon blood is hot and magically saturated. Destroying the Dragonheart faster than it can regenerate is one of the most reliable ways to permanently kill a dragon.
entries.name: 🐉Dragon Anatomy & the Dragonheart

entries.content:
Dragons grow for most of their lives. Hatchlings may be small enough to carry, juveniles become horse- or vehicle-sized, mature adults can reach building scale, and exceptional ancients can become vastly larger.

Growth slows with age rather than stopping completely. Increased size normally brings thicker scales, larger magical reserves, stronger breath, and greater physical strength.

Healthy dragons can live for thousands of years. The oldest individuals may personally remember dead languages, vanished cities, and historical events preserved nowhere else.

They are extremely long-lived rather than absolutely immortal; Dragonheart failure, catastrophic injury, or sufficiently powerful magic can still kill them.
entries.name: 🐉Dragon Size, Growth & Lifespan

entries.content:
A dragon’s human form is produced through **magical compression**, not a visual illusion. The Dragonheart forces an enormous draconic body into a human-scale template while wings, tail, horns, scales, claws, and most apparent mass are folded into the dragon’s magical structure.

The result often feels cramped. Dragons describe phantom wings that cannot stretch, an absent tail that still feels folded behind them, lungs that seem too small, limbs held unnaturally close together, and the sensation of their whole body being packed into a space far below its natural size.

Some dragons find the sensation merely inconvenient or even enjoy feeling compact. Others experience genuine claustrophobia, agitation, panic, irritability, or an urgent need to return to true form.

Human shape is practical, but comfort varies enormously by individual.
entries.name: 🐲Dragon Human Form & Magical Compression

entries.content:
Maintaining human compression produces **Compression Strain**. Early signs include stiffness, phantom tail or wing sensations, cramped muscles, headaches, shallow-feeling breaths, restlessness, and irritability.

As strain increases, the disguise can leak: pupils become draconic, scale patches appear, nails become claws, horns begin emerging, body heat changes, or the voice gains unnatural resonance.

Experienced dragons can deliberately release selected traits—eyes, horns, scales, claws, fangs, tail, or reduced wings—without returning fully to true form. Partial reversion lowers the pressure of compression and is useful in combat or private spaces.

Some dragons can remain human for weeks; others need to return to full size every few hours. Tight rooms and physical confinement often feel much worse when a dragon is already compressed.
entries.name: 🐲Compression Strain & Partial Reversion

entries.content:
Dragon breath is produced when the Dragonheart channels elemental power into specialized respiratory chambers. Fire is the most famous expression, but lineages may produce frost, lightning, acid, poison mist, superheated steam, concussive force, radiant energy, shadow, or other supernatural emissions.

Breath type usually corresponds to the dragon’s elemental affinity and natural habitat. A dragon is normally highly resistant to its own element.

True-form breath can devastate large areas. Human-form output is drastically reduced because the compressed throat and lungs cannot safely channel the same volume.

Repeated maximum attacks overheat or exhaust the Dragonheart and respiratory system, forcing even powerful dragons to pause.
entries.name: 🔥Dragon Breath & Elemental Lineages

entries.content:
Dragons are innately magical even without formal spell training. The Dragonheart supports elemental shaping, aura pressure, protective magic, shapeshifting, and magically reinforced flight.

Wings provide physical control while Dragonheart energy supplies additional lift, allowing bodies far heavier than natural aerodynamics should support. Large dragons require enormous open spaces to maneuver safely.

Dragon sight can track movement over great distances and often perceives heat or magic. Hearing catches low-frequency vibration, and smell identifies blood, smoke, metals, weather, and familiar individuals.

Older dragons frequently learn formal spellcraft, using their huge reserves for wards, weather magic, treasure protection, spatial enlargement, and long-duration enchantments.
entries.name: ✨Dragon Magic, Flight & Senses

entries.content:
A dragon hoard is a supernatural attachment to objects, knowledge, places, promises, or collections the dragon personally considers valuable. Gold and gems are common but not mandatory.

A modern dragon might hoard books, cars, computers, art, fossils, rare media, historical objects, research, property, photographs, or carefully preserved memories.

Long-held hoard items develop weak sympathetic links to the Dragonheart. Remaining near them improves emotional comfort and magical recovery, while theft feels deeply invasive.

Territory is equally practical: a true dragon needs room to fly, rest, transform, and exist without crushing buildings. Many modern dragons maintain remote true-form territories while using human identities in cities.
entries.name: 💎Dragon Hoards & Territory

entries.content:
Dragons reproduce slowly because creating a new Dragonheart requires enormous biological and magical investment. Most lineages lay one or a few heavily protected eggs after a long gestational period.

Dragon eggs require stable elemental conditions and periodic parental magic while the young Dragonheart crystallizes. Fire lineages may need heat, frost lineages deep cold, and aquatic lineages pressure and water.

Hatchlings are intelligent but physically immature. Breath, controlled flight, magic, and human compression develop gradually rather than appearing fully formed at birth.

Dragon parents are often intensely protective because eggs are rare and may represent years or decades of investment.
entries.name: 🥚Dragon Reproduction, Eggs & Hatchlings

entries.content:
Dragon culture values long memory, territory, hospitality, oath-keeping, and respect for another dragon’s hoard and eggs. Destroying an egg, stealing a bonded hoard object, forcing prolonged compression, or deliberately damaging a Dragonheart are among the most serious offenses.

Dragons are extraordinarily durable but not invulnerable. Eyes, wing membranes, joints, mouth, and parts of the underside are less armored than the back and shoulders.

Human form sacrifices much of true-form armor and makes the dragon easier to injure. Anti-dragon weapons, powerful magic, elemental counters, Dragonheart poisons, and direct Core destruction can overcome regeneration.

A dragon dies permanently when the Dragonheart is destroyed or when bodily destruction overwhelms it faster than it can restore the true template.
entries.name: ⚠Dragon Culture, Laws, Weaknesses & Death

entries.content:
Merfolk are a fully sapient aquatic humanoid race. **Mermaid** traditionally refers to an adult female, **Merman** to an adult male, and **Merfolk** to the species as a whole.

Their permanent aquatic body combines a humanoid upper torso with a powerful fishlike tail beginning around the hips. Tail forms vary by lineage and can resemble reef fish, sharks, eels, rays, deep-sea species, or supernatural marine creatures.

Merfolk possess both gills and lungs, allowing them to breathe underwater indefinitely and survive on land when properly hydrated.

They are not Sirens. Merfolk civilization is not built around magical vocal compulsion or predatory luring.
entries.name: 🧜Merfolk — Mermaids & Mermen

entries.content:
The Merfolk tail contains most of the body’s swimming musculature and is far stronger than human legs. A flexible spine continues deep into the tail and drives powerful fins through coordinated muscle groups.

The humanoid torso contains expanded lungs, pressure-resistant organs, highly efficient blood chemistry, and paired gill structures along the ribs, neck, or sides.

Hands are often webbed, eyes have protective membranes, and skin contains oils or fine scales that reduce drag and water damage.

Different lineages specialize for reef, open ocean, deep sea, freshwater, arctic, or tropical environments.
entries.name: 🧜Merfolk Physiology & Tails

entries.content:
Most Merfolk can temporarily reshape their tail into a pair of humanlike legs through inherited aquatic magic called **Shoreform**.

Shoreform is a real physical transformation: bones, muscles, fins, and scales reorganize into functional legs and feet. It is not merely an illusion.

Newly transformed Merfolk often walk awkwardly because their nervous system expects a tail and water support. Practice makes the form natural enough for ordinary surface life.

Land gradually dries the skin and gills, so hydration, humidity, salt balance, and regular immersion remain important. Severe dehydration weakens the transformation and can force an unsafe reversion.
entries.name: 🌊Merfolk Shoreform & Human Legs

entries.content:
Merfolk hearing is extremely sensitive to waterborne vibration and low-frequency sound. They can notice approaching boats, large animals, storms, and distant movement long before a human swimmer would.

Eyes adjust quickly between bright surface water and dim depths. Deep-sea lineages often possess bioluminescent markings or enhanced low-light vision.

A lateral-line-like pressure sense detects nearby movement without direct sight.

Underwater language mixes voiced speech with clicks, whistles, resonant tones, hand signs, and body movement because sound travels differently through water. Skilled Merfolk can communicate across great distances in favorable conditions.
entries.name: 🌊Merfolk Senses & Underwater Communication

entries.content:
Merfolk possess a natural magical affinity for water. All are exceptional swimmers and instinctively understand currents, depth, pressure, and underwater orientation.

Most can produce small current shifts, push themselves forward with bursts of water, shape bubbles, calm local turbulence, or briefly maintain breathable air pockets.

Stronger bloodlines develop true hydrokinesis, controlling large amounts of water, mist, waves, or ice depending on training and environment.

Water magic is easiest while immersed. On dry land the same effect costs far more energy because the Merfolk must supply or draw water before shaping it.
entries.name: 🌊Merfolk Water Affinity & Powers

entries.content:
Merfolk are omnivorous aquatic humanoids with strong preferences for seafood, sea plants, shellfish, algae, fish, mineral-rich foods, and foods common to their home waters.

They can eat ordinary surface food in Shoreform, but dry diets require substantially more water and electrolytes.

Saltwater and freshwater lineages have different mineral needs. Keeping a freshwater Merfolk in high salinity or a saltwater Merfolk without enough minerals can cause illness.

Dehydration dulls scales, irritates gills, reduces water magic, causes muscle cramping, and makes Shoreform harder to maintain.
entries.name: 🐚Merfolk Diet & Hydration

entries.content:
Merfolk reproduce biologically and generally give live birth underwater. Pregnancy occurs in the humanoid torso while the developing child forms a tail, lungs, gills, and pressure-adapted circulation.

Newborn Merfolk can breathe water immediately but remain in protected nursery waters until tail strength and orientation develop.

Children learn swimming first, surface breathing second, and Shoreform walking later.

Merfolk-human hybrids are possible. Offspring may be born with a tail and easy Shoreform ability or with human legs plus hidden gills, webbing, and strong aquatic traits.
entries.name: 🐚Merfolk Reproduction & Childhood

entries.content:
Merfolk settlements are designed three-dimensionally because movement is not limited to floors and stairways. Homes, schools, farms, markets, and public chambers can connect vertically through reefs, caverns, kelp forests, tunnels, and towers.

Written knowledge uses etched stone, shell tablets, enchanted glass, waterproof inks, metal plates, or magic that protects ordinary materials underwater.

Surface trade is common where Shoreform is accepted. Pearls, coral, recovered artifacts, deep-sea minerals, fish, magical plants, navigation knowledge, and oceanic information can all become valuable goods.

Water quality is a major political issue because pollution can threaten an entire settlement at once.
entries.name: 🏛Merfolk Culture & Underwater Cities

entries.content:
Merfolk territory is defined by currents, reefs, trenches, migration routes, freshwater systems, nesting waters, and safe passages rather than only by fixed land borders.

Touch etiquette recognizes tails, fins, gills, and bioluminescent markings as sensitive body parts. Grabbing a tail or covering someone’s gills is considered physically invasive and potentially dangerous.

Songs and long-distance calls are used for navigation, celebration, mourning, and community signaling but do not possess the compulsive power of Siren Song.

Surface visitors are often expected to respect water access, avoid contaminating communal waters, and understand that a dry room can be physically uncomfortable even when breathable air is available.
entries.name: 🏛Merfolk Social Customs & Territory

entries.content:
Merfolk are living and can be injured by ordinary trauma, disease, poison, blood loss, organ damage, or sufficiently powerful magic.

Their central environmental weakness is dehydration. Prolonged dry conditions damage gills, scales, eyes, and transformed leg tissues. Extreme heat accelerates the problem.

Polluted water can be even more dangerous than open air because gills expose a large surface directly to contaminants.

Shoreform reduces swimming power and water magic. A Merfolk trapped far inland can remain alive with careful hydration but gradually becomes weaker without proper immersion and mineral balance.
entries.name: ⚠Merfolk Weaknesses & Land Limits

entries.content:
Sirens are a separate sapient aquatic race whose biology is organized around supernatural sound, resonance, and predatory attraction. They are often mistaken for Mermaids because many have humanoid torsos and aquatic tails, but they are not Merfolk.

Siren true forms are generally more predatory: sharp teeth, clawed webbed hands, elongated fins, reflective or luminous eyes, strong tails, and throats adapted to produce supernatural harmonics.

Their defining power is **Siren Song**, a magical resonance capable of altering attention, emotion, perception, and movement in listeners.

Sirens are intelligent people capable of peaceful society, but their evolutionary history is that of aquatic ambush predators using sound to draw prey toward water.
entries.name: 🎶Sirens

entries.content:
A Siren possesses a specialized structure around the throat, lungs, sinuses, skull, and upper chest called the **Resonance Organ**.

It allows several tones to be produced simultaneously, including frequencies above and below ordinary human hearing. These harmonics interact with the nervous system of listeners and carry magical influence through vibration.

Powerful lungs sustain long notes above water while gills support underwater respiration. Additional resonating chambers in the jaw, palate, skull, and chest give even normal speech an unusually layered quality.

Damage to the throat or Resonance Organ can weaken Siren Song without necessarily preventing ordinary speech.
entries.name: 🎶Siren Physiology & Resonance Organ

entries.content:
Siren Song carries supernatural influence through audible and subaudible resonance.

At low intensity it can make the singer seem unusually calming, fascinating, beautiful, frightening, trustworthy, or difficult to ignore. Stronger song can induce trance, suppress panic, encourage sleep, redirect movement, or compel a listener to approach a particular place.

Full predatory song can overwhelm an unprotected human’s judgment and draw them toward water despite obvious danger.

The effect weakens with distance, poor acoustics, competing noise, magical protection, hearing impairment, or barriers that block the relevant frequencies. It is powerful influence rather than omnipotent control over every possible action.
entries.name: 🎵Siren Song & Compulsion

entries.content:
Sirens possess exceptional control over pitch, tone, cadence, resonance, and vocal texture. After hearing a voice clearly, a trained Siren can reproduce it with near-perfect accuracy.

They can imitate accents, age impressions, emotional tone, animal calls, alarms, music, or many mechanical sounds within the limits of the Resonance Organ.

Mimicry does not automatically carry supernatural compulsion. The Siren can reproduce a harmless voice or deliberately layer magic into it.

Predatory Sirens historically copied familiar voices calling for help to lure people away from safety, which is why impersonation is heavily regulated in organized Siren communities.
entries.name: 🎵Siren Voice Mimicry

entries.content:
Sirens perceive their surroundings through reflected sound as well as sight. Clicks, humming, and short song fragments can map caves, shipwrecks, dark water, submerged buildings, and moving bodies.

Their hearing is sensitive to heartbeat, breathing, motion through water, and tiny changes in acoustics. Familiar people can sometimes be recognized by movement and heartbeat alone.

This sensitivity also creates vulnerability. Sonic weapons, magical dissonance, sudden pressure waves, and conflicting frequencies can cause pain, nausea, disorientation, or loss of song control.

Experienced Sirens learn to dampen their hearing reflexively in loud surface environments.
entries.name: 🎵Siren Echolocation & Sonic Senses

entries.content:
Sirens are carnivorous aquatic humanoids. Fish, marine mammals, large aquatic animals, and other meat can fully satisfy their nutritional needs; human flesh is not biologically required.

Their instincts are nevertheless strongly tuned to humanlike voices, heartbeats, fear responses, and surface movement because coastal humans were historically easy prey.

A hungry Siren may feel a powerful urge to sing when isolated prey is nearby, but sapient Sirens can control that impulse.

Modern communities distinguish biological hunting instinct from permission to hunt people. A Siren can live completely healthily without ever consuming a human.
entries.name: 🦷Siren Diet & Predatory Instinct

entries.content:
A Siren’s true body is aquatic and built for sudden acceleration, tight turns, ambush, and powerful underwater pursuit. Most possess large tails, fins, webbed claws, gills, sharp teeth, and streamlined musculature.

Many bloodlines can create a temporary **Shore Guise**. The tail becomes legs, obvious gills retract, claws shorten, and teeth appear less predatory.

Unlike Merfolk Shoreform, Siren transformation usually contains a glamour component. Reflective eyes, cool skin, unusually sharp canines, or impossible vocal resonance may remain.

The guise is easiest to maintain near water and becomes harder with dehydration. Vocal powers usually remain fully usable while human-presenting.
entries.name: 🌊Siren Aquatic Form & Shore Guise

entries.content:
Sirens reproduce biologically and usually give live birth in protected coastal caves, lagoons, reefs, or underwater nesting territories.

Children are born aquatic and develop the Resonance Organ gradually. Juvenile voices cannot produce full adult compulsion, though emotional resonance may appear early.

Social family groups are often called **pods**. A group trained to combine song is commonly called a **choir**. These are broad social terms rather than named factions.

When several Sirens harmonize deliberately, their resonance can multiply rather than merely add together, allowing large-area calming, concealment, communication, or dangerous mass compulsion.
entries.name: 🪺Siren Reproduction, Pods & Choirs

entries.content:
Siren culture treats voice as both identity and potential weapon. A private song, natural voice, or personal harmonic pattern can be intimate in the same way a face, name, or magical signature is intimate to another race.

Deliberately copying someone’s private voice, secretly enchanting ordinary conversation, or forcing another Siren into an unwanted harmonic resonance is considered invasive.

Music, oral history, acoustic architecture, underwater performance, and complex choral traditions are central to many communities.

Silence also has cultural meaning. Choosing to communicate by gesture around someone vulnerable to song can be a deliberate sign of trust and restraint.
entries.name: 🏛Siren Culture & Voice Etiquette

entries.content:
Siren law commonly prohibits coercive predatory song against uninvolved people, voice impersonation for fraud, mass compulsion in public spaces, and using a choir to overwhelm another person’s will without lawful cause.

Their principal weaknesses center on sound and hydration. Severe throat injury, lung damage, Resonance Organ trauma, magical silence, sonic dissonance, and prolonged dehydration can weaken or remove their defining abilities.

Hearing protection reduces ordinary song influence when it blocks enough relevant frequencies. Magical sound wards and anti-compulsion protections are stronger defenses.

Sirens remain living beings and can die from severe physical trauma, blood loss, organ destruction, poison, disease, or sufficiently powerful magic.
entries.name: ⚖Siren Laws, Weaknesses & Song Defense

entries.content:
Mermaids are female Merfolk: amphibious aquatic humanoids whose natural body has a humanoid upper torso, functional lungs and gills, and a powerful fishlike tail. Mermaid is a gendered term within the broader Merfolk species, not a separate species from Mermen.

They are fully sapient, can live in underwater civilizations, possess exceptional swimming and aquatic senses, and commonly have inherited Shoreform magic that temporarily replaces the tail with humanlike legs.

Mermaids are not automatically Sirens. Sirens are a separate resonance-based predatory aquatic race with supernatural song biology.
entries.name: 🧜Mermaids — Direct Race Overview

entries.content:
Mermen are male Merfolk and share the same aquatic physiology, gills, lungs, tail-based locomotion, Shoreform transformation, water affinity, and environmental needs as Mermaids.

They are ordinary members of Merfolk civilizations rather than a lesser or rarer form. Tail shape, coloration, size, powers, occupation, and culture vary by bloodline and region rather than gender alone.

Like all Merfolk, Mermen require regular water access and suffer under prolonged dehydration. They remain biologically distinct from Sirens despite occupying many of the same oceans and coastlines.
entries.name: 🧜Mermen — Direct Race Overview

entries.content:
Kresnik bloodlines emerged as a supernatural counterweight to expanding vampire populations. Their oldest traditions describe themselves less as heroes than as an ecological answer to immortal predation.

Modern Kresniks do not experience that history as a single uninterrupted tradition. Regional populations preserve different versions, and old conflicts often survive as etiquette, law, inherited caution, or stereotypes long after the original event has passed.
entries.name: 💀Kresniks — History & Historical Eras

entries.content:
Vampire scent and aura naturally capture attention. Hunting instinct encourages tracking and threat assessment but does not automatically determine guilt or morality.

These instincts are biological pressures rather than mandatory personalities. Culture, training, individual temperament, trauma, ethics, and experience determine whether an instinct becomes a habit, a private sensation, a useful skill, or something actively resisted.
entries.name: 💀Kresniks — Instincts & Behavioral Drives

entries.content:
They can eat ordinary food, but vampire blood is a potent supernatural nutrient that strengthens healing, magic, and hunting ability.

Daily routine is built around the species' real physiology rather than a generic human schedule. Activity, feeding, recovery, power use, environmental access, and social obligations all affect how a healthy Kresnik organizes an ordinary day.
entries.name: 💀Kresniks — Daily Biological Rhythm

entries.content:
They can eat ordinary food, but vampire blood is a potent supernatural nutrient that strengthens healing, magic, and hunting ability.

Stable communities treat nourishment as infrastructure. Reliable supply reduces desperation, predatory accidents, black markets, and social coercion; shortages make every other part of law and culture harder to maintain.
entries.name: 💀Kresniks — Feeding Needs & Resource Security

entries.content:
They sleep like living humanoids, though supernatural endurance allows longer wakefulness than ordinary humans during hunts.

Rest also has a social role: it creates private time, recovery rituals, shared nesting or sleeping customs, and expectations about when an exhausted individual should withdraw rather than continue using powers unsafely.
entries.name: 💀Kresniks — Sleep, Rest & Recovery

entries.content:
They live comfortably in human society but tend to establish bases near vampire population centers, transport routes, hospitals, archives, and places useful for investigation.

Environmental mismatch does not always cause immediate death, but prolonged exposure can reduce comfort, power efficiency, healing, concentration, or disguise control. Mature communities design homes and workplaces around these needs.
entries.name: 💀Kresniks — Hydration & Environmental Needs

entries.content:
They are living humanoids with dense supernatural tissue, powerful senses, rapid healing, resistance to vampire abilities, and blood capable of safely processing vampiric essence.

Because Kresnik senses are shaped by their supernatural biology, crowds, bright light, strong smells, loud machinery, magical noise, blood, fear, water pressure, or other stimuli may be far more intense than they are for humans. Training teaches selective attention rather than simply enduring everything at full sensitivity.
entries.name: 💀Kresniks — Sensory Overload & Adaptation

Nonverbal communication often uses anatomy humans do not possess or interpret correctly. Posture, eye behavior, scent, tail or wing position, stillness, distance, breath, aura, vocal resonance, or transformation tells can communicate mood before speech does.
entries.name: 💀Kresniks — Body Language & Nonverbal Signals

entries.content:
