## Mental Healing and Restoration
---
Mental Healing and Restoration repairs damage to memory, personality, cognition, identity, emotional regulation, and subconscious structure. The Dreamwalker can remove psychic scars, reverse hostile mind control, rebuild missing memories from preserved traces, restore a fragmented sense of self, and repair damage caused by nightmares, possession, telepathy, curses, or artificial mental tampering.

The process can be immediate or performed through a detailed healing dream where the target experiences reconstruction symbolically. Light Dream Dust can reinforce the repair, while archived identity patterns in the Dream Core provide a reference for what the mind looked like before damage. The Dreamwalker decides whether painful memories remain intact, lose their harmful emotional charge, or are removed entirely. Mental restoration therefore treats the mind as a rebuildable living system rather than something permanently ruined once altered.
---
entries.name: Mental Healing and Restoration

entries.content:
## Trauma Extraction
---
Trauma Extraction separates the damaging emotional and subconscious effects of a traumatic experience from the factual memory of what happened. The Dreamwalker can pull terror, panic triggers, recurring nightmares, intrusive imagery, guilt, or conditioned responses out of the mind as visible dream material while leaving knowledge and personal history intact.

The extracted trauma can be dissolved, consumed as oneiric nourishment, transformed into harmless imagery, stored for study, or condensed into Dark Dream Dust. If the target prefers complete removal, the underlying memory can also be erased or rewritten. The Dreamwalker can work on a single event or trace connected trauma across years of related experiences. This power is especially precise because memory, emotion, and subconscious programming are separate editable layers rather than one indivisible block.
---
entries.name: Trauma Extraction

entries.content:
## Dream Curse Crafting
---
Dream Curse Crafting creates persistent oneiric effects that follow a target through sleep, memory, or dream signature. A curse can cause recurring nightmares, prevent restful sleep, make a specific fear appear in every dream, bind a power to sleep conditions, summon a tracking predator whenever the target dreams, or make a forbidden action trigger an immediate oneiric consequence.

Curses can be written directly into the subconscious or forged from Dark Dream Dust as semi-independent constructs. The Dreamwalker controls duration, trigger, target recognition, visibility, and removal conditions. A curse can remain unnoticed until activated or announce itself through symbols in every dream. Because it is attached to identity through dream-space, changing location, body, or ordinary magical protections does not necessarily break the connection.
---
entries.name: Dream Curse Crafting

entries.content:
## Dream Oath and Contract Binding
---
Dream Oath and Contract Binding turns an agreement into an oneiric law attached to the minds of everyone who accepts it. Terms can be spoken inside a dream, written in Dream Dust, signed through memory, or represented by symbolic actions. Once bound, the Dreamwalker can define what happens when a term is kept, broken, completed, or deliberately exploited.

Consequences can include waking alarms, loss of access to a dream sanctuary, forced sleep, memory release, curse activation, Dream Dust transfer, or any other effect the Dreamwalker deliberately writes into the agreement. Contracts can also function positively by protecting memories, guaranteeing safe dream access, or automatically summoning help. The binding is mental and oneiric rather than legal paperwork; what matters is the identity of the participants and the meaning the Dreamwalker encodes into the oath.
---
entries.name: Dream Oath and Contract Binding

entries.content:
## Dream Materialization
---
Dream Materialization pulls dream-created objects, environments, and constructs into waking reality. A sword imagined inside a dream can become a physical weapon, a staircase can appear in a real room, a dream animal can step through a portal, or an entire sanctuary can unfold into physical space. The Dreamwalker decides whether the materialized creation behaves like ordinary matter, Dream Dust, or a hybrid of both.

Materialized forms can persist after the original dream ends. Their stability depends on the law the Dreamwalker assigns rather than on continued belief from the sleeper. Light, Dark, and Cosmic Dream Dust can be used to give different qualities to the result, while pure Dream Aspect authority can make simple dream objects real without visible Dust. This ability is one of the main bridges between absolute dream sovereignty and practical waking-world creation.
---
entries.name: Dream Materialization

entries.content:
## Waking Construct Persistence
---
Waking Construct Persistence lets a dream-made creation remain in physical reality indefinitely after the Dreamwalker stops concentrating on it. Weapons, clothing, vehicles, furniture, guardians, buildings, tools, artworks, food-like creations, and complex machines can become stable objects with whatever physical properties were assigned during creation.

The Dreamwalker can decide whether a construct is permanent, dismissible, keyed to an owner, self-repairing, invisible to outsiders, or able to return to dream-space when not needed. Persistent constructs can also contain stored memories, messages, Dream Dust, portals, or autonomous instructions. They are not illusions pretending to be solid; once materialized under this rule, they function as real created objects until the Dreamwalker changes or uncreates them.
---
entries.name: Waking Construct Persistence

entries.content:
## Dream Creature Manifestation
---
Dream Creature Manifestation brings oneiric life-forms out of dreams and into waking reality. The creature may come from a sleeper's imagination, the Dreamwalker's own design, a nightmare, a personal sanctum, or a long-lived species native to the Dream Realm. Once manifested, it can be tangible, intelligent, autonomous, and capable of remaining outside dream-space.

The Dreamwalker determines how much independence the creature receives. Some are temporary servants or guardians; others can be granted persistent identity, memories, personality, and the ability to continue existing as genuine individuals. Light Dust favors protective and restorative beings, Dark Dust favors predatory or fear-aspected forms, and Cosmic Dust can create extremely complex life with reality-bending traits. Dream creatures therefore range from tiny companions to godlike constructs without being limited to ordinary biology.
---
entries.name: Dream Creature Manifestation

entries.content:
## Cosmic Dust Life Creation
---
Cosmic Dream Dust can create genuine living or sentient beings rather than temporary puppets. The Dreamwalker can design anatomy, appearance, senses, lifespan, abilities, personality foundations, instincts, and the environment the new life is adapted to. A created being can begin as an infant, adult, machine intelligence, spirit-like entity, animal, alien species, or form with no natural equivalent.

True life creation differs from a normal construct because the new being can possess independent continuity once completed. It can learn, change, form relationships, dream on its own, and continue existing without constant command. The Dreamwalker can still establish protective bonds or permissions during creation, but independence is possible if desired. Cosmic Dust provides the creative potential while the Dream Aspect supplies the coherent identity pattern that makes the result more than animated matter.
---
entries.name: Cosmic Dust Life Creation

entries.content:
## Light Dust Resurrection
---
Light Dream Dust can restore a dead or otherwise permanently lost physical body when the Dreamwalker can still identify the person's oneiric identity. The Dust rebuilds missing tissue, organs, nervous structure, and whatever nonhuman anatomy is required while the Dreamwalker guides the target's mind, memory, and identity back into the restored vessel.

Resurrection can repair damage that ordinary healing cannot address because it uses the remembered whole state rather than the condition of the remains. A body can be rebuilt from fragments, severe decay, or an archived dream-pattern if sufficient identity information remains available to the Dreamwalker. The target can return with memories intact, mental trauma repaired, and old permanent injuries corrected. This is a Light Dust restoration effect rather than necromantic undeath; the intended result is the actual person restored to living continuity.
---
entries.name: Light Dust Resurrection

entries.content:
## Dark Dust Soul Execution
---
Dark Dream Dust can create execution effects that target the identity connecting mind, dream, soul, and body rather than relying on ordinary physical injury. Grim Reaper constructs are the classic expression, but the Dreamwalker can design other execution forms such as black judges, nightmare beasts, silent blades, clocks, doors, or abstract shadows that carry the same assigned death authority.

When the execution is authorized, ordinary toughness, regeneration, armor, species, or physical scale are not the relevant defense because the construct is acting through oneiric identity. The Dreamwalker can also choose nonlethal variants that sever a target from a power, dream realm, immortality mechanism, or mental bond instead of ending life. Dark Dust turns nightmare symbolism into enforceable consequence, with the exact form determined by the bearer's imagination.
---
entries.name: Dark Dust Soul Execution

entries.content:
## Dream Door Network
---
Dream Door Network allows the Dreamwalker to establish persistent doors between minds, sanctums, Dream Realm regions, waking locations, alternate universes, and timelines. A door can look ordinary, appear as a glowing arch, open inside a mirror, float in empty space, or exist only to people with permission to perceive it.

Each door can have rules. It may open only while someone sleeps, recognize specific identities, lead to different destinations depending on who enters, remain one-way, or carry travelers physically from dream-space into waking reality. Doors can be grouped into vast transportation networks, allowing the Dreamwalker to move allies, constructs, messages, or Dream Dust without retracing the full Realm route each time. Because the network is keyed to identity and oneiric coordinates, doors can remain stable even when the connected worlds are separated by impossible physical distance.
---
entries.name: Dream Door Network

entries.content:
## Dream Beacon
---
A Dream Beacon is an oneiric signal the Dreamwalker can attach to a person, object, location, dream, memory, or reality. Once marked, the target becomes easy to find through the Dream Realm no matter how far away it moves physically. The beacon can also act as a call for help, a return point, a portal destination, or a trigger that alerts the Dreamwalker when a defined event occurs.

Beacons can be invisible to everyone else or appear as a recurring symbol in dreams. The Dreamwalker can create temporary marks for a single mission or permanent ones for trusted people and important locations. Multiple beacons can be organized into a mental map inside the Dream Core, turning the multiverse into a set of instantly recognizable oneiric coordinates rather than an unstructured infinity.
---
entries.name: Dream Beacon

entries.content:
## Infinite Dream Archive
---
The Infinite Dream Archive is a limitless organized library inside the Dream Core and personal sanctum. Memories, dreams, skills, personalities, maps, construct designs, wishes, historical events, conversations, sensory experiences, and entire mindscape snapshots can be stored without crowding or degradation. Nothing needs to blur together unless the Dreamwalker deliberately merges it.

Archived material can be searched by person, emotion, time, world, dream signature, concept, or symbolic association. A preserved mind-state can be used to restore someone after psychic damage; a saved dream can be replayed exactly; a construct blueprint can be summoned instantly; a copied skill can be implanted into another mind. The archive gives the Dreamwalker effectively unlimited long-term oneiric memory while keeping personal memories distinguishable from collected information.
---
entries.name: Infinite Dream Archive

entries.content:
## Dream Oracle
---
Dream Oracle allows the Dreamwalker to explore possible futures through the Dream Realm's connection to timelines, fears, expectations, and unrealized outcomes. Instead of receiving vague random prophecy, the bearer can deliberately request a question and generate dream scenarios representing different branches that may follow from current conditions.

The Dreamwalker can enter those possibilities, examine consequences, speak with projected versions of people, compare decision paths, and return with the remembered results. Because futures can branch, the power distinguishes likely outcomes from fixed certainties unless the bearer deliberately locks a future through another ability. Cosmic Dream Dust can sharpen the exploration by building extremely detailed possibility worlds. Dream Oracle is therefore a strategic use of timeline-aware dream travel rather than simple symbolic fortune-telling.
---
entries.name: Dream Oracle

entries.content:
## Dream Probability Weaving
---
Dream Probability Weaving turns imagined possibilities into favored waking outcomes. The Dreamwalker first models an event inside dream-space, chooses the desired branch, and then uses Dream Aspect authority or Cosmic Dream Dust to make reality lean toward that result. Small uses can make an unlikely coincidence occur; larger uses can reshape chains of events so an improbable future becomes the one that actually unfolds.

The bearer can specify what must remain unchanged while adjusting probability around it. A rescue can succeed without altering who was present, a missing object can turn up through a plausible sequence, or a complex plan can receive the exact convergence it needs. This does not require the Dreamwalker to manually control every intermediate event. The oneiric pattern acts as a template toward which waking causality is encouraged to settle.
---
entries.name: Dream Probability Weaving

entries.content:
## Absolute Dream Sovereignty
---
Absolute Dream Sovereignty is the completed expression of the Dream Omnicron mantle. Inside dreams and the Dream Realm, the Dreamwalker is the highest active authority over scenery, physics, time, distance, identity, bodies, powers, memory, emotion, causality, death, creation, and the relationship between dream and waking reality. Every more specialized ability in the lorebook is a precise application of this broader source-level control.

Outside dreams, sovereignty extends through minds, sleep, Dream Dust, dream portals, materialized constructs, oneiric identity, and the Realm's multiversal network. The Dreamwalker can act gently enough to edit a single forgotten detail or broadly enough to manage countless sleeping minds across realities. Only one true Dreamwalker carries this complete authority at a time, making the bearer the singular conscious sovereign of the Dream Aspect rather than merely another powerful psychic or dream deity.
---
entries.name: Absolute Dream Sovereignty

entries.content:
## Somnia, Goddess of Sleep and Dreams
---

Somnia was the first divine consciousness known to awaken inside the Dream Realm. She did not create the first biological sleeper, but as countless early minds began dreaming, their images, fears, memories, and hopes formed a shared metaphysical sea. Somnia emerged from that sea as the intelligence capable of understanding all of it at once.

She became the Goddess of Sleep and Dreams, maintaining the routes between sleeping minds while preventing ordinary dreamers from dissolving into one another. She could enter any dream, quiet nightmares, build impossible worlds, restore damaged memories, and shape the primordial forms of what later became Light, Dark, and Cosmic Dream Dust.

Somnia's power was not identical to the modern Dreamwalker mantle because she was the original divine source rather than a chosen Omnicron host. Her death transformed that personal divinity into the Dream Aspect from which every later Dreamwalker draws authority.

---
entries.name: Somnia, Goddess of Sleep and Dreams
entries.comment: Somnia, Goddess of Sleep and Dreams

entries.content:
## The Night Without Dreams
---

The Night Without Dreams was a multiversal oneiric collapse in which sleeping minds began entering blank unconsciousness instead of dream. Dream routes disappeared, nightmares and hopes alike fell silent, and entire regions of the Dream Realm started dissolving because nothing connected them to living imagination.

Somnia discovered that the failure was deeper than any single curse or enemy. The Dream Realm had grown too vast to remain dependent on one divine consciousness maintaining every bridge personally. If she simply repaired the damage, another collapse would eventually occur when she was absent or destroyed.

Her solution was irreversible. Somnia chose to make the Dream Realm self-sustaining by giving it the total structure of her own divinity. The night ended only because she began the sacrifice later remembered as Somnia's Last Sleep.

---
entries.name: The Night Without Dreams

entries.content:
## Somnia's Last Sleep
---

Somnia's Last Sleep was the death that created the Dream Aspect. She entered the deepest layer of the Dream Realm and dreamed herself into every stable dream route at once. Her divine body disappeared, her personal consciousness faded, and the rules that had once existed only because she actively maintained them became permanent structures of the Realm.

Her authority condensed around one central principle: the Dream Realm would always be capable of recognizing a living sovereign without requiring that sovereign to be Somnia. That source became the Dream Aspect.

The event is called a sleep rather than a death because traces of Somnia remain everywhere in dream reality. They are echoes, instincts, symbols, and oneiric memory rather than a complete hidden person waiting to awaken. Through each Dreamwalker, something of what she built continues to act, but every chosen bearer remains a new individual.

---
entries.name: Somnia's Last Sleep

entries.content:
## Origin of the Three Dream Dusts
---

Light, Dark, and Cosmic Dream Dust existed in primitive forms before Somnia died, but her Last Sleep organized them into the three stable expressions recognized by modern Dreamwalkers. Light Dust formed from the restorative dreams, hopes, comfort, and protected memories Somnia carried. Dark Dust condensed from nightmares, fear, predatory dream structures, and the destructive material she had contained across ages.

Cosmic Dream Dust came from the part of Somnia that represented unrestricted divine imagination: dreams large enough to resemble miniature realities, impossible wishes, and concepts not yet limited by waking physics.

The Dream Aspect inherited control over all three because Somnia's divinity had learned to hold them in balance. A Dreamwalker can specialize in one Dust or combine all three without becoming a different kind of bearer.

---
entries.name: Origin of the Three Dream Dusts
entries.comment: Origin of the Three Dream Dusts

entries.content:
## The Moon-Dream Convergence
---

The Moon-Dream Convergence occurred during Somnia's Last Sleep when a total lunar eclipse passed over the world of the first mortal Dreamwalker. Millions of sleepers independently dreamed of the same moon at the exact moment Somnia's new Aspect needed its first physical anchor.

Those dreams briefly behaved as one immense shared mindscape. The eclipse became a symbol visible from both waking reality and the Dream Realm, allowing the Aspect to identify a newborn consciousness whose developing identity was unusually stable across the boundary between the two.

That infant became the first Dreamwalker. Lunar eclipses remain powerful symbols not because the moon literally contains the Aspect, but because the Dream Realm remembers the first successful bridge. Later awakenings, successions, coronations, and major oneiric events can cause eclipse imagery even on worlds with different moons or skies.

---
entries.name: The Moon-Dream Convergence

entries.content:
## Somnia's Echo
---

Somnia's Echo is the residual divine memory left throughout the Dream Aspect. It may appear as an unfamiliar lullaby, a silhouette seated beyond a moonlit doorway, a sudden understanding of how to calm a collapsing dream, or the feeling that the Dream Realm itself remembers an older hand shaping its architecture.

The echo is not a second consciousness sharing the Dreamwalker's body. It cannot overwrite the host or demand that the host repeat Somnia's life. It behaves more like inherited oneiric intuition preserved in the source.

The echo becomes clearest when dreams across large populations are threatened, when the Dream Realm itself is damaged, or when a new bearer is crowned. These are the circumstances closest to the crisis that caused Somnia to create the Aspect, so the oldest layers of the mantle become easier to perceive.

---
entries.name: Somnia's Echo

creator.bio:
# 🌌 Welcome to My Worlds

**Bot Creator & World Builder**  
*Supernatural • RPG • Academy • Family • Slice of Life*

I create **character-driven roleplay bots** focused on supernatural worlds, academies, family dynamics, open-world RPGs, superheroes, giants, mystery, and slice-of-life.

I love building **large casts and living settings** where characters have their own personalities, relationships, rivalries, goals, routines, secrets, and histories. Some bots are funny and relaxed, while others are dramatic, mysterious, or built for long-running stories.

## 🛠️ I Maintain My Bots

If something breaks, a greeting has issues, characters get confused, or the lore stops working properly, **please reach out and let me know**. I regularly revisit older bots to rewrite prompts, improve lorebooks, fix recurring problems, and add new content.

## 🌠 What I Create

🏫 **Academies & Schools**  
🌎 **Open-World & Supernatural RPGs**  
🏡 **Family & Relationship Bots**  
📚 **Large Lorebooks & Ensemble Casts**

## 💬 Requests & Feedback

**Requests, recommendations, and feedback are always welcome.** If you have a new bot idea, want something added, or run into a problem, send it my way. I can't promise every request immediately, but I enjoy improving my worlds and creating new ones.

I'm also updating many bot pages with **HTML mini-wiki descriptions** featuring collapsible lore, greeting summaries, and quick-start details.

**Building worlds, fixing what breaks, and making every roleplay worth getting lost in.**

bookmarked.name: Shapeshifter
bookmarked.description: Shapeshifter: The Shapeshifter Omnicron is the singular bearer of the Self-Form Aspect, giving absolute ownership over their own physical form. Their body can stretch, compress, liquefy, flatten, enlarge, harden, divide, regenerate, imitate creatures or objects, abandon normal anatomy, and assume virtually any imaginable configuration while remaining the same continuous conscious being.

entries.content:
##Infinite Malleability
---

The core body power that makes every part of the user endlessly reshapeable while still alive, controlled, aware, and recoverable. As the signature bodily power of the Shapeshifter Omnicron, it is not ordinary elasticity or a collection of separate transformations. The bearer’s body exists under a source-level rule that form is optional: shape, scale, internal anatomy, rigidity, surface, volume and bodily arrangement are all choices rather than limits.

The body stretches, folds, bulges, flattens, curls, hardens, softens, or expands like a living material obeying thought instead of anatomy. Objects can be wrapped, carried, cushioned, copied in silhouette, formed around, protected, gripped, or replaced by body-made equivalents. People can be restrained, lifted, shielded, caught, disguised as, surrounded, separated from danger, or moved without normal impact damage.

The user remains the same being through every shape, able to think through any body layout and return to any preferred form instantly. Typical uses include stretch across a street as a bridge; flatten under a door and reform upright; become a crash cushion around allies; turn one arm into ten reaching tools.

---
entries.name: Infinite Malleability

entries.content:
##Molecular Body Control
---

The fine-control layer that lets the user decide how every piece of the body behaves at the smallest practical scale.

Surfaces can become smooth, ridged, sticky, glossy, matte, skin-like, rubbery, glassy, hard-edged, or cloth-soft in the same moment. Locks, cracks, fabrics, tools, containers, and machinery can be interacted with by forming exact micro-shapes or pressure surfaces. Contact with others can feel like normal skin, padded rubber, hard armor, flowing gel, a gentle sling, or an immovable grip.

The user can reshape without tearing, bleeding, bruising, or needing organs arranged normally, because the whole body obeys self-directed structure. Typical uses include form fingerprints or erase them; make fingertips into precision screwdrivers; seal a wound by flowing over it; turn skin into smooth armor without looking armored.

---
entries.name: Molecular Body Control

entries.content:
##Unlimited Stretching
---

The ability to extend any body part to any useful length without thinning into weakness or losing control.

Limbs lengthen like endless living bands, torsos telescope across rooms, fingers unspool into lines, and hair or skin can extend as controllable strands. Distant objects can be grabbed, tagged, tied, lifted, inspected, pushed, pulled, or delivered without the user walking over. People can be caught from far away, separated by long barriers, grabbed out of danger, or gently lowered from heights.

The user keeps strength, feeling, and coordination through the entire stretched length, so a hand hundreds of feet away is still as precise as a nearby hand. Typical uses include reach around a building to unlock a window; stretch up an elevator shaft; grab falling keys across a street; wrap a runaway car before it hits anyone.

---
entries.name: Unlimited Stretching

entries.content:
##Infinite Compression
---

The power to compress the body into smaller, thinner, denser, or more compact forms while keeping full function.

The user can become a coin-thin figure, a curled rubber ball, a thread, a stamp-sized person, a folded sheet, or a dense compact knot. Small spaces, boxes, vents, bottles, drawers, cracks, keyholes, bags, and hidden compartments become reachable or usable hiding places. Others see the user take up less space without becoming weaker, dead, or trapped; the compressed form still hears, sees, thinks, and moves.

The user can store themselves in impossible places, reduce target size for stealth, or avoid attacks by becoming too thin or compact to strike normally. Typical uses include fold into a backpack; hide inside a coat pocket; squeeze through a keyhole; turn into a tiny bead and roll under lasers.

---
entries.name: Infinite Compression

entries.content:
##Size Expansion
---

The ability to increase apparent size, reach, volume, and occupied space without a hard upper boundary.

The body swells outward into giant hands, wall-sized torsos, enormous shields, living ramps, towering forms, or broad nets spanning whole areas. Objects can be lifted, surrounded, braced, hidden under living cover, divided by barriers, or carried inside padded body chambers. People may stand on, climb across, shelter behind, or be scooped up by expanded body surfaces that behave like stable terrain.

The user decides whether the enlarged form is soft, bouncy, rigid, heavy, hollow, light, flexible, or armor-hard, preventing size from becoming clumsy. Typical uses include become a bridge over a river; turn one hand into a room-sized catcher mitt; expand into a dome over a crowd; fill a hallway to block pursuit.

---
entries.name: Size Expansion

entries.content:
##Paper-Thin Flattening
---

The ability to press the body into a flat surface without losing volume control, awareness, or mobility.

The user can look like a painted figure, a rubber sheet, a flat shadow, a carpet, a poster, a tarp, or a ribbon-thin strip sliding along surfaces. Doors, cracks, vents, under-furniture gaps, wall seams, windows, and narrow machinery spaces can be passed through by flattening the body. People may walk over the user without realizing it, be cushioned by a flat body layer, or be wrapped by a sheet-form restraint.

The user can still move, see through surface-sense, and reform instantly from any edge or point of the flattened shape. Typical uses include slide under a locked door; become a rug that trips nobody until chosen; cover a broken window as a seal; flatten across a wall as camouflage.

---
entries.name: Paper-Thin Flattening

entries.content:
##Liquid Flow Form
---

The ability to behave like a controlled liquid or gel while remaining one conscious body.

The body pours down stairs, streams through pipes, puddles under doors, flows around obstacles, or rises from the floor like animated syrup. Containers, drains, sinks, ducts, pipes, and cracks can be entered or sealed by flowing into their shape. People can be surrounded by a harmless gel cushion, pulled from danger, restrained without hard edges, or protected from smoke and debris.

The user chooses viscosity, stickiness, thickness, temperature feel, color, opacity, and whether the liquid-like body splashes or holds together cleanly. Typical uses include flow through plumbing and reform in a bathroom; become a puddle trap; pour around a bomb to contain fragments; seal a leaking pipe with living gel.

---
entries.name: Liquid Flow Form

entries.content:
##Complete Shapeshifting
---

The broad transformation function that lets the user become any shape, body plan, object outline, creature silhouette, or invented form.

The user may become tall, short, wide, thin, animal-like, tool-like, vehicle-like, monstrous, beautiful, plain, harmless, or impossible. Objects can be replaced by body-made copies, hidden inside the form, imitated as decoys, or built into the user’s shape temporarily. People perceive a physical transformation rather than a mere illusion; they can touch the changed form and feel the chosen texture and weight.

The user keeps their mind and senses through all changes, even if they currently have no normal head, eyes, bones, or limbs. Typical uses include become a chair that can stand up; turn into a giant serpent-like coil; mimic a coat rack; become a working parachute shape.

---
entries.name: Complete Shapeshifting

entries.content:
##Disguise Morphing
---

The use of malleability to copy or invent humanoid appearances through physical reshaping.

Facial bones, hair shape, height, build, skin texture, posture, age presentation, scars, and body proportions slide into the selected look. Clothing can be simulated as part of the body, items can be hidden in folds, and visible id details can be recreated as body texture. Strangers see a real physical disguise with correct shape, touch, and movement instead of a fragile visual mask.

The user can maintain the disguise while stretching, flattening, or taking damage, then snap back to the chosen appearance afterward. Typical uses include become a guard long enough to pass a checkpoint; copy a silhouette from a photograph; change height during a conversation; erase all visible identifying marks.

---
entries.name: Disguise Morphing

entries.content:
##Voice and Throat Molding
---

The power to reshape the mouth, throat, lungs, tongue, lips, and resonance chambers to create any voice or body-made sound.

The neck and chest subtly adjust like a living instrument, producing deep voices, child voices, animal calls, alarms, whistles, echoes, or layered tones. Objects can be vibrated, unlocked by sound, distracted with false noises, or signaled through hidden body-made speakers. People hear a voice that comes from the user’s actual body rather than from illusion, including distance tricks if the user stretches a hollow tube elsewhere.

The user can speak through extended tendrils, ventriloquize from another room, create simultaneous voices, or silence their body completely. Typical uses include copy a password phrase in the correct voice; speak from a hand stretched through a vent; make footsteps sound behind an enemy; imitate a ringing phone.

---
entries.name: Voice and Throat Molding

entries.content:
##Color and Texture Control
---

The surface-control side of malleability that changes color, pattern, reflectivity, and tactile feel.

Skin can become brick-patterned, wood-grained, metallic, glassy, clothlike, matte black, neon bright, transparent-looking, or perfectly skin-toned. Objects can be visually imitated, hidden against matching surfaces, marked with body-made symbols, or replaced by convincing decoys. People can touch the user and feel whatever texture the user chooses, from warm skin to cold stone-like hardness or rubber softness.

The user can alter surface appearance independently from deeper structure, appearing soft while being hard or looking metallic while remaining elastic. Typical uses include blend into wallpaper; make an arm look like a metal pipe; display words across the skin; copy the texture of a leather jacket.

---
entries.name: Color and Texture Control

entries.content:
##Density and Rigidity Control
---

The ability to decide how solid, heavy-feeling, soft, stiff, dense, or springy each body section becomes.

A hand can become a pillow while a finger becomes a needle-like pick, or the torso can become armor while the legs stay flexible. Doors, walls, tools, weapons, hinges, and supports can be braced, struck, cushioned, or manipulated by matching the needed rigidity. People can be held gently with soft areas while dangerous impacts are blocked by hardened sections in the same form.

The user can change rigidity instantly during motion, turning a stretched band into a whip, a shield, a bridge, or a soft landing mat. Typical uses include become hard enough to stop a blade; soften around a trapped child; turn a finger into a crowbar; make the feet springy for silent jumps.

---
entries.name: Density and Rigidity Control

entries.content:
##Impact Absorption
---

The defensive function where the body deforms around incoming force instead of taking normal injury.

Punches sink into rubbery mass, bullets flatten into harmless dents, falls spread through bouncing layers, and collisions ripple across the surface. Objects that hit the user may lose momentum, rebound, stick, or be captured inside soft folds until released. People striking the user feel like they hit a trampoline, padded wall, deep cushion, or living crash bag rather than flesh and bone.

The user decides whether to bounce force back, swallow it silently, redirect it, or convert it into stretching motion. Typical uses include catch a speeding motorcycle by becoming a crash barrier; let a hammer blow sink into the chest; bounce a puncher backward; land from a skyscraper as a puddle and reform.

---
entries.name: Impact Absorption

entries.content:
##Projectile Deformation Defense
---

The specific defense against fast, sharp, or piercing objects by refusing to behave like pierceable flesh.

Bullets press into elastic skin and are caught, blades slide through a stretched gap, arrows bend inside rubber folds, and shrapnel becomes trapped in surface layers. Weapons can be collected, redirected, swallowed into harmless storage, or flung back once their force is drained. Attackers see shots vanish into dents, bounce off, curve through loops, or get wrapped by strands before reaching a target.

The user can leave holes open intentionally so projectiles pass through empty body-space without contacting anything vital. Typical uses include form a donut hole around a bullet path; catch shrapnel in a cape-shaped body sheet; wrap a gun barrel shut; turn the chest into a bullet-catching cushion.

---
entries.name: Projectile Deformation Defense

entries.content:
##Explosion Diffusion
---

The ability to handle explosions by expanding, hollowing, venting, and absorbing pressure through malleable mass.

The body becomes a ballooning shell, net, dome, sponge, or layered bag that eats flame pressure and fragment paths. Debris can be caught in folds, smoke can be directed upward, glass can be netted, and blast waves can be spread through enormous surface area. People nearby are shielded by a soft living barrier that bulges outward instead of cracking apart.

The user can reform after being stretched, burned, scattered, or inflated by the blast, because deformation is an expected state. Typical uses include wrap around a grenade before it bursts; inflate into a room-filling shock absorber; become a dome over civilians; swallow a fireball and vent it through a long tube upward.

---
entries.name: Explosion Diffusion

entries.content:
##Regeneration From Pieces
---

The recovery ability that lets the user rebuild from separated, torn, flattened, burned, scattered, or stretched parts. Separated pieces still belong to the same living identity, allowing the Omnicron to treat dismemberment, scattering and fragmentation as temporary arrangements instead of terminal injury.

Pieces crawl, flow, snap, or slither back together like living material remembering its true owner. Containers, rubble, tape, traps, or restraints cannot permanently hold a piece if the user chooses to reclaim it. People may see fragments merge into hands, puddles rise into bodies, or a flattened smear peel off a wall and stand up.

The user retains selfhood across pieces, can prioritize which fragment becomes the main body, and can regrow missing mass through malleable recovery. Typical uses include reform after being shredded by machinery; pull scattered droplets back together; grow a lost arm from a fingertip fragment; escape by leaving a fake piece behind.

---
entries.name: Regeneration From Pieces

entries.content:
##Ageless Malleable Physiology
---

The long-term survival state where the body does not rely on ordinary aging, fragile organs, or fixed biological limits. The Self-Form Aspect continually preserves the bearer’s chosen biological state, so age and ordinary bodily deterioration do not force the body into a form the bearer has not selected.

The user can look any age, maintain a chosen appearance indefinitely, and repair wear by resetting the body’s shape memory. Time, injury, scars, decay, and ordinary physical deterioration can be ignored or rewritten at the body level. People cannot judge the user’s age, condition, or vulnerability from appearance alone because the body is a chosen configuration.

The user can sleep, eat, breathe, or imitate those needs if desired, but the malleable body is not normally dependent on them to remain intact. Typical uses include keep the same face for centuries; erase wrinkles by smoothing the body; recover from lethal organ damage by not needing organs; appear old for a disguise then return to youth.

---
entries.name: Ageless Malleable Physiology

entries.content:
##Organless Survival
---

The ability to function without fixed organs, bones, lungs, blood flow, or vulnerable anatomy arranged in normal places. Because function is distributed through the whole malleable substance, fixed lungs, heart, bones, arteries or other conventional weak points are unnecessary unless the bearer deliberately forms them.

The body may become hollow, flat, coiled, shredded, transparent, folded, or object-shaped with no visible organs at all. Hazards that target organs, pressure points, arteries, lungs, or skeletal joints fail because the body can rearrange or omit those targets. People searching for a weak point find nothing stable to strike; the user’s anatomy moves away, dissolves, or becomes irrelevant.

The user can still speak, sense, move, and think through distributed body awareness rather than one fragile brain-and-organ layout. Typical uses include survive being flattened by a press; talk while shaped like a tire; hide the brain-equivalent throughout the whole body; ignore choking by having no fixed throat to crush.

---
entries.name: Organless Survival

entries.content:
##Distributed Awareness
---

The sensory and mental control that lets the user feel and command the whole malleable body from any shape.

Every stretched strand, puddle edge, flat sheet, and detached piece can carry touch, pressure, vibration, and orientation awareness. Objects brushing against a body-thread can be identified; rooms can be mapped by spreading thin layers over surfaces. People interacting with any part of the user may be felt clearly even if that part is far from the main face.

The user does not need a normal brain location, so attacks aimed at the head do not automatically shut down control. Typical uses include sense footsteps through a hand stretched under a door; feel a safe cracking through a fingertip tool; watch multiple angles using spread-out eyes; continue moving while headless.

---
entries.name: Distributed Awareness

entries.content:
##Thread Form
---

The ability to reduce parts of the body into ultra-thin strings, cords, wires, ropes, cables, or threads.

Strands can snake across floors, hang like wires, coil into knots, form nets, slip through cracks, or weave into fabric-like sheets. Objects can be tied, pulled, tripped, lifted, sewn, stitched, repaired temporarily, or moved through narrow openings. People can be restrained with noncutting cords, caught by nets, guided by safety lines, or pulled away from danger.

The user can control tension, elasticity, sharpness, color, thickness, and whether the thread is sticky, soft, or steel-hard. Typical uses include thread under a locked door to open it from inside; become a safety harness around a falling person; weave into a temporary bridge; make invisible-thin trip lines.

---
entries.name: Thread Form

entries.content:
##Crack and Gap Movement
---

The infiltration use of flattening, liquid flow, compression, and thread form to pass through almost any opening.

The body becomes a ribbon, puddle, mist-like sheet, worming cord, folded packet, or liquid stream moving through the available space. Locks, sealed doors, vents, drains, pipes, window seams, elevator gaps, and rubble cracks become pathways instead of barriers. People watching may only see a colored line slide away or a puddle disappear into a crack before the user reforms elsewhere.

The user can carry small items inside body folds or extend a strand through first to scout before moving the rest of the body. Typical uses include slip through a vault seam; enter a room through an air vent; escape handcuffs by flowing around them; pass beneath a door as a flat ribbon.

---
entries.name: Crack and Gap Movement

entries.content:
##Restraint Escape
---

The ability to defeat most physical containment by changing the body instead of breaking the restraint.

Wrists become liquid, shoulders collapse inward, bones vanish, skin narrows, and the body pours through bars or cuff openings. Handcuffs, ropes, chains, cages, straps, glue, nets, boxes, and traps lose meaning when the captured shape is voluntary. Captors see restraints still locked while the user slides out of them or leaves a fake limb inside as a decoy.

The user can escape gently and silently or burst free by expanding into a shape the restraints cannot hold. Typical uses include flow out of handcuffs; flatten between cage bars; leave a dummy torso tied to a chair; squeeze through a mail slot after being locked outside.

---
entries.name: Restraint Escape

entries.content:
##Tool Morphing
---

The practical ability to turn body parts into useful tools with exact shape and function.

Fingers become keys, screwdrivers, wrenches, hooks, pliers, hammers, needles, saw edges, clamps, funnels, or measuring cords. Objects can be repaired, opened, held, adjusted, picked, cut, measured, wedged, pried, or assembled without carrying equipment. People see the user provide instant tools from their own body, often changing one finger after another for different tasks.

The user can make the tool soft enough not to damage delicate work or hard enough to function like metal. Typical uses include pick a lock with a reshaped fingertip; turn a forearm into a jack handle; become a ladder and wrench at once; make tiny tweezers from two fingernails.

---
entries.name: Tool Morphing

entries.content:
##Key and Lock Forms
---

The precise use of malleability to read, fill, and manipulate lock spaces.

A fingertip slides into a keyway, feels each pin or ward, molds around the internal pattern, and turns as a perfect custom key. Doors, safes, cuffs, cabinets, vehicles, old locks, and mechanical security systems can be opened by forming the missing component. Bystanders may only see a finger become thin and notched before the lock clicks open without tools.

The user can avoid breaking the lock, jam it from inside, duplicate a key shape for later, or seal it shut with body material. Typical uses include open a safe by feeling tumblers; become a skeleton key; lock a door by filling the keyhole; copy a key from sight and form it out of a finger.

---
entries.name: Key and Lock Forms

entries.content:
##Weapon Forms
---

The combat use of the body as any blunt, sharp, flexible, restraining, or defensive weapon shape.

Arms become blades, clubs, whips, nets, shields, spears, hammers, hooks, bolas, cages, or spring-loaded battering shapes. Objects can be knocked away, cut, trapped, disarmed, pinned, or blocked without separate weapons. Opponents face a weapon that changes mid-swing, turning a missed punch into a wrap, a blade into a shield, or a shield into a net.

The user chooses lethality by controlling hardness and edge quality, making the same form harmless, painful, disabling, or destructive. Typical uses include turn a fist into a giant mallet; make a whip arm around a sword; shape fingers into nonlethal cuffs; become a wall-sized shield in front of allies.

---
entries.name: Weapon Forms

entries.content:
##Vehicle Forms
---

The ability to shape the body into vehicles or vehicle-like transport structures.

The user can become a wheel, sled, glider, raft, car-like shell, motorcycle frame, parachute, elevator platform, or living rescue cart. Objects and people can ride on or inside padded compartments, be strapped by body-made belts, and be cushioned from motion. Passengers feel a living transport that bends around obstacles, absorbs bumps, and can reform instantly if blocked.

The user supplies motion through elastic recoil, limb propulsion, rolling forms, gliding surfaces, or pushing off the environment. Typical uses include become a rescue raft in floodwater; roll downhill as a giant tire carrying supplies; form a glider for two people; make a stroller-like shell around a child.

---
entries.name: Vehicle Forms

entries.content:
##Glider and Parachute Forms
---

The aerial survival use of broad, thin, curved forms to manage falling and air movement.

The body spreads into wings, parachutes, sails, kites, fins, membranes, or air-catching sheets. Falling objects can be caught in folds, slowed by drag, wrapped in parachute fabric, or guided toward safe landing spots. People can be held inside harness-like loops while the user’s body becomes the canopy or wings around them.

The user can steer by changing curvature, splitting into fins, or stretching one side longer to bank and turn. Typical uses include catch a falling elevator as a parachute membrane; glide between buildings; make a kite shape above allies; turn into a sail on a boat.

---
entries.name: Glider and Parachute Forms

entries.content:
##Propeller and Fan Forms
---

The ability to make spinning or airflow-based structures from flexible body parts.

Arms or extensions flatten into blades, rotate like fans, create gusts, hover briefly, clear smoke, or move air through tunnels. Objects can be blown away, cooled, dried, ventilated, or pushed by controlled airflow. People nearby feel wind from an actual body-made fan, not magic, with force adjusted from gentle breeze to knockback gust.

The user can anchor part of the body while another part spins, preventing dizziness by distributing awareness away from the rotating section. Typical uses include clear smoke from a hallway; hover using rotor arms; blow tear gas back; dry soaked papers with a gentle fan hand.

---
entries.name: Propeller and Fan Forms

entries.content:
##Multi-Limb Formation
---

The ability to create additional arms, hands, legs, tendrils, fingers, faces, or functional extensions from available body mass.

The user blooms into many reaching limbs, tool-hands, gripping loops, crawling legs, shield arms, or delicate finger clusters. Multiple objects can be carried, repaired, sorted, restrained, juggled, protected, or operated at once. People may be helped by several hands simultaneously or overwhelmed by restraints coming from different angles.

The user coordinates every limb naturally through distributed awareness, so extra hands do not require extra brains. Typical uses include catch five falling people at once; play every part of a piano duet; operate a dozen locks simultaneously; hold shields in every direction.

---
entries.name: Multi-Limb Formation

entries.content:
##Tendril Control
---

The use of long flexible extensions for reach, binding, scouting, manipulation, and combat.

Tendrils slide around corners, coil like snakes, split into smaller tips, flatten into ribbons, or stiffen into poles. Objects can be snatched, tied, pulled, pushed, scanned by touch, carried, or kept suspended by multiple tendril anchors. People can be grabbed gently around the waist, wrapped safely during a fall, separated from danger, or restrained at wrists and ankles.

The user can sense through tendril tips and reshape them instantly into hooks, pads, keys, shields, or blades. Typical uses include send a tendril through a vent to scout; catch someone around the ankle before they fall; wrap a villain without hurting them; grab a phone from across a room.

---
entries.name: Tendril Control

entries.content:
##Net and Web Forms
---

The ability to spread into mesh, webbing, lattice, net, grid, or catching structures.

The body becomes crisscrossed strands with adjustable holes, sticky points, elastic borders, and reinforced knots. Objects can be filtered by size, caught from the air, suspended, sorted, strained out of water, or wrapped for transport. People can be caught from falls, separated from hazards, or restrained in a net that tightens only as much as the user chooses.

The user can keep awareness through every strand and open gaps for allies while closing gaps around threats. Typical uses include become a giant safety net below a bridge; filter debris out of a flood; trap thrown weapons in midair; make a temporary hammock field.

---
entries.name: Net and Web Forms

entries.content:
##Wrap and Bind
---

The close-control restraint method where the user coils around a target or object.

Arms stretch into straps, torsos become loops, fingers become bands, and the body forms living cuffs, harnesses, cocoons, or belts. Weapons can be wrapped shut, doors can be held closed, objects can be bundled, and machinery can be immobilized without breaking it. People feel pressure exactly controlled: loose enough to breathe and avoid injury, tight enough to prevent escape.

The user can shift the binding from soft padding to hard restraint, add more loops, release instantly, or move the bound target safely. Typical uses include wrap around a rampaging person to stop them; bind a broken pipe closed; turn into seatbelts during a crash; coil around a monster’s legs.

---
entries.name: Wrap and Bind

entries.content:
##Encasing and Containment
---

The ability to surround something completely inside a body-made shell, capsule, bubble, box, or cocoon.

The user forms a seamless enclosure that can be transparent, opaque, soft, hard, airtight, ventilated, padded, or reinforced. Objects can be stored, transported, isolated, protected from weather, or kept from exploding outward. People can be placed in safe capsules, medical slings, temporary cells, or protective bubbles with air channels and shock absorption.

The user controls internal pressure, texture, restraints, view, sound flow, and how quickly the shell opens. Typical uses include carry a bomb inside a blast-resistant body pouch; protect someone underwater in an air bubble; make a temporary jail cell; cover fragile art during a fire.

---
entries.name: Encasing and Containment

entries.content:
##Body Pocket Storage
---

The ability to create safe internal folds, pockets, sleeves, and chambers inside the malleable body.

The torso opens into hidden compartments, limbs become hollow tubes, hair becomes storage cords, and flat body layers fold around items. Objects can be concealed, waterproofed, cushioned, separated, or carried without bags. People cannot find stored items by normal pocket searches if the user has reshaped the compartment elsewhere.

The user can choose whether stored things touch skin-like surfaces, float in padded chambers, or remain locked in rigid body cases. Typical uses include hide keys in a fingertip; carry a first-aid kit inside the torso; smuggle a note as a flat layer under the skin; store fragile glass in a shockproof pocket.

---
entries.name: Body Pocket Storage

entries.content:
##Living Shield Forms
---

The defensive use of size, flattening, hardening, and elasticity to become a barrier.

The user spreads into walls, domes, shields, umbrellas, bunkers, barricades, riot shields, or layered curtains. Objects hit the shield and are bounced, caught, absorbed, redirected, or held in surface dents. People behind the user gain cover from bullets, fire, collapsing debris, weather, vehicles, or melee attacks.

The user can make the inside soft for allies and the outside hard, slick, spiked, adhesive, or impact-absorbing. Typical uses include become a door-sized shield in a hallway; wrap around a family during a crash; form a dome over a campsite; turn into a wall that catches bullets without ricochet.

---
entries.name: Living Shield Forms

entries.content:
##Rescue Cushion Forms
---

The protective use of the body as padding, airbags, nets, slings, rafts, and crash mats.

The user becomes a huge pillow, foam pad, trampoline, inflatable tunnel, soft funnel, or layered landing bag. Falling objects can be slowed, redirected, separated, or cushioned to prevent secondary damage. People land into a surface that conforms to their shape, spreads force, supports the neck and spine, and prevents bounce if desired.

The user can adjust softness during impact, becoming loose at first contact and firmer as momentum fades. Typical uses include catch someone falling from a roof; turn into airbags inside a car; become a padded chute down a stairwell; make a crash mat under a collapsing balcony.

---
entries.name: Rescue Cushion Forms

entries.content:
##Medical Splinting and Support
---

The use of malleability to stabilize injured people with living braces, bandages, casts, cushions, and pressure control.

Fingers flatten into bandages, arms become splints, torso folds into stretchers, and soft pads form around wounds. Medical supplies can be replaced temporarily by body-made supports that hold shape and pressure precisely. Patients feel custom-fit support that does not cut circulation, shift painfully, or apply uneven strain.

The user can carry, immobilize, elevate, warm, cool, or gently compress injured areas while moving them to help. Typical uses include form a neck brace after a crash; make a stretcher with handles; seal a wound with gentle pressure; support a broken arm without tape or cloth.

---
entries.name: Medical Splinting and Support

entries.content:
##Environmental Camouflage
---

The stealth use of shape, color, texture, flatness, and stillness to become part of surroundings.

The user becomes wallpaper, floor tile, a pipe, a chair, a puddle, a sign, a curtain, a statue, or a shadow-like sheet. Objects can be hidden under matching body layers or replaced by decoy body objects. People looking directly at the area may overlook the user because the body has become a believable surface or item.

The user can still sense nearby movement through touch and vibration while remaining visually blended. Typical uses include become a brick pattern on a wall; hide as a lamp cord; turn into a chair in an office; flatten into a shadow under a table.

---
entries.name: Environmental Camouflage

entries.content:
##Clothing Simulation
---

The ability to form apparent clothing, armor, uniforms, accessories, and fabric textures from the body itself.

Skin layers fold into shirts, jackets, shoes, gloves, scarves, belts, dresses, armor plates, helmets, or badges. Objects can be hidden under body-made clothing, and disguises can include complete outfits without separate garments. People see and feel believable cloth, leather, rubber, metal-like armor, or soft fabric, though it is all living malleable material.

The user can change outfits instantly, repair tears by smoothing them, or turn clothing into tools and restraints. Typical uses include make a guard uniform during a disguise; turn a sleeve into a rope; simulate shoes while barefoot; form a raincoat from the skin surface.

---
entries.name: Clothing Simulation

entries.content:
##Decoy Bodies
---

The ability to form fake bodies, spare faces, empty duplicates, or misleading body sections from stretched material.

The user can leave a sleeping-looking body in bed, a fake head around a corner, or a dummy limb caught in restraints. Objects and traps can be fooled by placing decoy mass where the real awareness is not concentrated. People may attack, question, or watch the wrong body while the user flows elsewhere through a hidden strand.

The decoys are usually extensions or shaped portions of the user, not independent people, unless another power adds separate minds. Typical uses include leave a fake self tied to a chair; send a head-shaped decoy through a doorway; make three false arms during a fight; pretend to be knocked out while the real body slips away.

---
entries.name: Decoy Bodies

entries.content:
##Pseudo-Clones
---

The advanced form of decoy creation where the body divides into multiple active shapes still belonging to one user.

Separate figures stretch from a shared mass, connected by thin strands or distributed awareness across divided pieces. Objects can be manipulated in different places at once, with each pseudo-clone acting as a hand, disguise, shield, or scout. People may believe they are seeing multiple beings until the forms rejoin or stretch back into one body.

The user can coordinate all pseudo-clones as limbs of one mind, but they remain one malleable organism unless deliberately written otherwise. Typical uses include stand at both ends of a hallway; make two decoys distract guards; hold three doors open at once; send a small clone-shape through a vent.

---
entries.name: Pseudo-Clones

entries.content:
##Surface Adhesion and Suction
---

The ability to cling, seal, grip, and attach to surfaces by reshaping texture and pressure.

Hands become suction cups, skin becomes sticky pads, feet flatten against walls, and body sheets seal over cracks. Objects can be stuck to walls, held without hands, sealed into place, or pulled free by controlled adhesion. People can be carried on sticky harnesses, restrained against surfaces, or protected from falling by body-made grips.

The user chooses whether the adhesion is gentle, removable, airtight, waterproof, or strong enough to hold huge weight. Typical uses include walk up glass using suction feet; seal a doorframe against smoke; stick a weapon to the ceiling; hold an ally to the body while climbing.

---
entries.name: Surface Adhesion and Suction

entries.content:
##Ladder and Bridge Forms
---

The utility use of the body as safe terrain, crossings, ramps, ladders, steps, and rails.

The user stretches into stairways, rope bridges, handrails, slides, scaffolds, ladders, platforms, or emergency walkways. Objects and supplies can be moved across the body-path, with surfaces shaped to prevent slipping or rolling. People can climb, walk, crawl, or be guided along a stable route that adjusts under their weight.

The user can harden load-bearing areas while keeping railings soft and reshape the path while people are already on it. Typical uses include become a bridge over a pit; turn into stairs to a second-story window; make a wheelchair ramp instantly; form a ladder down an elevator shaft.

---
entries.name: Ladder and Bridge Forms

entries.content:
##Room and Architecture Forms
---

The large-scale use of malleability to become usable spaces, shelters, walls, doors, floors, or furniture.

The body expands into tents, huts, rooms, tunnels, hallways, chairs, tables, walls, ceilings, slides, and sealed shelters. Objects can be stored in body-made shelves, protected in soft corners, or moved through living corridors. People can enter a temporary structure that warms, cushions, seals, guides, or protects them from outside hazards.

The user maintains control over every surface, opening doors by parting the body and rearranging rooms while occupied. Typical uses include become a storm shelter around a group; form a secret tunnel under a fence; make a temporary bedroom in a wasteland; turn into a maze to trap pursuers.

---
entries.name: Room and Architecture Forms

entries.content:
##Living Trap Forms
---

The ability to shape the body into traps, snares, pits, false floors, cages, and containment hazards.

The user becomes a normal-looking rug, chair, doorway, hallway, puddle, or wall that transforms when touched. Objects can be captured in gripping pockets, snapped into loops, glued by adhesion, or swallowed into padded cells. People who step onto unpermitted areas may sink into soft restraints, be wrapped by sudden bands, or find exits sealed.

The user controls force precisely so traps can be harmless pranks, nonlethal captures, or serious battlefield restraints. Typical uses include turn into a carpet that becomes cuffs; make a fake doorway that closes around weapons; form a chair that holds a suspect; become a pit that cushions then locks.

---
entries.name: Living Trap Forms

entries.content:
##Internal Force Redirection
---

The ability to channel incoming force through elastic body paths and release it elsewhere.

A punch stretches the torso into a sling, a blast ripples down a limb, or a fall loads the body like a spring. Objects hitting the user can be flung aside, caught, bounced back, or redirected into the ground. Attackers may feel their own strength return as recoil or vanish into elastic deformation.

The user chooses where force travels, preventing self-harm and turning enemy momentum into movement or counterattack. Typical uses include absorb a punch and snap an arm back like a rubber band; bounce a thrown rock into the sky; redirect a car impact along a wall form; turn a fall into a leap.

---
entries.name: Internal Force Redirection

entries.content:
##Shape Memory Reset
---

The built-in ability to remember chosen forms and return to them instantly after distortion. Shape memory is not a single default body; it can hold many exact forms, disguises and specialized configurations as instantly recoverable bodily states.

The body can be stretched, smashed, flattened, scattered, burned, twisted, inflated, or folded, then snap back perfectly. Objects carried inside storage pockets can remain safe while the outer shape resets around them. People watching see injuries and deformation vanish as the body chooses a previous state and rebuilds it.

The user can store many defaults: casual body, disguise, combat form, tiny form, giant form, vehicle form, or emergency recovery form. Typical uses include snap back after being run over; restore a copied disguise after combat; return from puddle to normal body; reset one arm while the rest stays transformed.

---
entries.name: Shape Memory Reset

entries.content:
##Chemical and Poison Resistance
---

The resistance created by a body that can seal, reject, dilute, reshape, or isolate harmful substances.

Skin can become nonporous, layered, slick, self-cleaning, disposable, or hollow so chemicals never reach anything vulnerable. Poisons, acids, gases, venoms, medicines, and contaminants can be trapped in temporary sacs or expelled through formed vents. People exposed nearby can be shielded by body masks, seals, filters, or full protective domes.

The user does not rely on ordinary bloodstream targets unless choosing to imitate them, so many toxins lack a stable system to attack. Typical uses include walk through tear gas as a sealed suit; trap acid in a disposable hand layer; form gas masks for allies; eject venom by squeezing out the affected surface.

---
entries.name: Chemical and Poison Resistance

entries.content:
##Temperature Adaptation
---

The ability to resist or adapt to heat, cold, burning, freezing, melting, brittleness, and thermal shock through active body control.

The body can become insulating foam, heat-shedding sheets, thick rubbery padding, reflective surfaces, or flexible cold-proof material. Hot objects can be gripped with heat-resistant pads; freezing surfaces can be bridged without becoming brittle. People can shelter under insulated body layers, be wrapped in warmth-preserving blankets, or protected from flame bursts.

The user continuously reshapes damaged outer layers and preserves functional awareness even when surface texture changes. Typical uses include become a fire blanket; hold molten metal with disposable hand mass; insulate someone in a blizzard; stretch through a freezer without cracking.

---
entries.name: Temperature Adaptation

entries.content:
##Electrical Insulation
---

The use of body material as an adjustable insulator, conductor, ground path, or electrical barrier.

Skin becomes rubbery, layered, dry, thick, or cable-like depending on whether current must be blocked or redirected. Wires, outlets, machines, batteries, lightning arcs, and electric traps can be touched, separated, bridged, or insulated. People can be pulled away from live wires by nonconductive extensions or shielded from arcs by a body-made barrier.

The user chooses whether electricity stops, travels along a safe route, discharges harmlessly, or powers a device through shaped contact. Typical uses include grab a live cable safely; become rubber gloves for someone else; bridge a broken circuit with a controlled conductive strand; wrap an electrical panel before it sparks.

---
entries.name: Electrical Insulation

entries.content:
##Friction Control
---

The ability to set how much surfaces grip, slide, drag, stick, or glide.

Feet can become silent and grippy, skin can become impossible to hold, limbs can slide through restraints, or hands can lock onto glass. Objects can be slid, stopped, carried on slick surfaces, or held by high-friction pads. People may lose grip on the user, be helped across ice by traction paths, or be safely slowed by friction cushions.

The user can combine friction changes with shape changes, turning a flat body into either a slide or a non-slip mat. Typical uses include escape a grapple by becoming slick; make a rescue slide down stairs; walk on wet glass with sticky soles; stop a rolling object with high-friction palms.

---
entries.name: Friction Control

entries.content:
##Vibration and Sound Body
---

The use of malleable mass as resonating chambers, drums, cords, membranes, and speakers.

The body forms hollow tubes, vibrating sheets, stretched strings, echo chambers, or bass-like cavities. Objects can be shaken loose, located by echo, signaled through walls, or disrupted by resonant tapping. People hear sounds from body-made instruments and may feel vibration through floors if the user spreads into surfaces.

The user can speak without a normal mouth, throw sound through tubes, dampen footsteps, or create distracting noises from several body points. Typical uses include make a siren from the chest; listen through a wall using a finger membrane; shake dust off shelves; speak from a tendril hidden under a table.

---
entries.name: Vibration and Sound Body

entries.content:
##Body-Made Senses
---

The ability to create sensory organs anywhere on the body or use the entire surface as a sensor.

Eyes open on fingertips, ears form along stretched strands, pressure sensors spread across sheets, and vibration-sensitive pads map rooms. Objects can be examined from every side at once by wrapping them in sensory skin. People may be watched, protected, or tracked without the user turning a head or facing them directly.

The user can decide which senses are active, hiding them as freckles, seams, tiny dots, or invisible tactile awareness. Typical uses include grow eyes on the back to watch behind; feel a heartbeat through a held wrist; map a room by spreading under the carpet; listen through a keyhole with an ear-shaped fingertip.

---
entries.name: Body-Made Senses

entries.content:
##Functional Object Imitation
---

The ability to become object shapes that physically function well enough to be used.

The user can imitate chairs, doors, keys, ropes, boxes, wheels, hoses, umbrellas, tools, cages, lamps, signs, or simple machines. Objects can be replaced, extended, repaired temporarily, disguised, or enhanced by the user becoming the missing part. People can sit on, open, climb, hold, wear, or use the object-form without it collapsing unless the user chooses movement.

The user supplies mechanical function through body control: hinges bend, wheels roll, springs recoil, handles grip, and buttons press. Typical uses include become a working chair in a waiting room; turn into a hose to carry water; replace a missing ladder rung; become a mailbox to hide in plain sight.

---
entries.name: Functional Object Imitation

entries.content:
##Machine Shape Imitation
---

The advanced ability to imitate complex mechanical shapes with moving body parts.

The body forms gears, pistons, wheels, belts, hinges, triggers, springs, pumps, and interlocking components. Machines can be temporarily repaired by replacing missing pieces or boosted by acting as flexible connectors. People see a living mechanism that moves smoothly even though every part is made from the same malleable body.

The user can create function without actual metal, fuel, or electronics if motion alone is enough; electronic logic requires separate knowledge or powers. Typical uses include replace a broken gear in a music box; become a hand-cranked elevator pulley; form a working pump for water; make a temporary bicycle chain.

---
entries.name: Machine Shape Imitation

entries.content:
##Armor and Shell Forms
---

The ability to create protective plates, helmets, shells, exoskeletons, and armored surfaces from the body.

The user’s skin segments into plates, thickens into shields, folds over allies, or becomes a hard outer shell over soft inner padding. Objects can be encased in armor, carried inside hardened cases, or protected from weather and impacts. People can be covered by body-made helmets, body suits, shields, or emergency shells that flex with their movement.

The user can make armor look like clothing, monstrous plating, smooth ceramic, metal, rubber, or invisible under a disguise. Typical uses include form a helmet around someone before debris falls; turn the chest into a shield plate; become armor over a teammate; hide hard plates under a normal-looking jacket.

---
entries.name: Armor and Shell Forms

entries.content:
##Edge and Blade Formation
---

The ability to create sharp edges, points, razors, scissors, saws, and cutting shapes from controlled rigidity.

Fingers flatten into blades, arms become crescent edges, hair becomes wire, or the body forms serrated tools. Objects can be cut, sliced, trimmed, freed from ropes, carved, drilled, or separated with chosen precision. People can be threatened without harm, freed from bindings, or protected by cutting hazards away from them.

The user controls sharpness moment by moment, turning a lethal edge into a harmless rubber strip instantly. Typical uses include cut through ropes with a finger blade; make scissors out of two fingers; slice a door latch; turn a sword-arm into a soft band mid-swing.

---
entries.name: Edge and Blade Formation

entries.content:
##Elastic Launching
---

The movement and projectile technique of storing tension in stretched body sections and releasing it.

Arms pull back like slings, legs coil like springs, torsos stretch into catapults, and tendrils snap objects forward. Objects can be launched, thrown, delivered, bounced, or accelerated without machines. People can be flung gently onto a roof, tossed into a rescue net, or moved quickly if cushioned by the user’s body.

The user can aim through body awareness and regulate force from toy-level tosses to siege-level launches. Typical uses include slingshot across rooftops; launch a rope over a building; catapult a villain into a padded wall; spring a car out of mud.

---
entries.name: Elastic Launching

entries.content:
##Bounce and Ricochet Movement
---

The mobility style where the user becomes springy enough to rebound off surfaces without injury.

The body curls into balls, pads, springs, tires, or bouncing humanoid forms. Objects can be carried inside while the user bounces, or bounced away with controlled rebounds. People watching see impacts deform and redirect the body like living rubber, with landings chosen rather than random.

The user can increase or dampen rebound, letting them ricochet through alleys, bounce up shafts, or land silently after huge falls. Typical uses include bounce between two buildings; turn a fall into a high jump; ricochet around gunfire; become a ball around a fragile item.

---
entries.name: Bounce and Ricochet Movement

entries.content:
##Impossible Body Geometry
---

The ability to fold, loop, layer, tunnel through, and arrange the body in ways normal anatomy cannot support. The body is not obligated to preserve normal anatomical topology, letting it create loops, hollows, nested spaces, branching structures and arrangements that would be impossible for a fixed skeleton.

The user becomes knots with doors, loops with eyes inside, hollow corridors, body-within-body shapes, spirals, mobius-like ribbons, or nested cages. Objects can pass through body-made tunnels, be stored in folds, or be redirected through looping channels. People may walk through a body arch, be trapped in a maze of limbs, or find that grabbing one part only pulls more body from elsewhere.

The user keeps coherent control because the body is not constrained by skeleton, organ placement, or ordinary internal volume. Typical uses include make an arm loop around a room three times; create a tunnel through the torso; fold flat then unfold into a staircase; trap an enemy in a maze of elastic walls.

---
entries.name: Impossible Body Geometry

entries.content:
##Mass Redistribution
---

The ability to move body volume and thickness from one region to another instantly.

The user can make one arm gigantic while the rest becomes thin, make a giant head decoy, thicken the back into armor, or empty the torso into tendrils. Objects can be lifted with temporarily huge hands, hidden in swollen pockets, or protected by moving padding to the impact side. People may see the user’s body warp like clay, with mass rushing under the surface to where it is useful.

The user never needs symmetrical anatomy and can operate perfectly with uneven, absurd, or temporary proportions. Typical uses include make one hand the size of a car; move all padding to the side being hit; thin the body to slip through bars while keeping large feet outside; grow a huge shield from one shoulder.

---
entries.name: Mass Redistribution

entries.content:
##Body Anchoring
---

The ability to attach, widen, root, hook, or brace parts of the body to resist movement.

Feet spread into suction pads, fingers become hooks, the torso forms wedges, and tendrils wrap around beams or terrain. Objects can be held steady, doors braced, vehicles stopped, ropes anchored, and structures stabilized. People can grab the user as a living anchor during wind, floods, falls, or combat.

The user can anchor one part while stretching another, becoming both fixed point and moving tool. Typical uses include anchor to a rooftop during a storm; hold a bus from rolling downhill; brace a collapsing wall; become a handhold line along a cliff.

---
entries.name: Body Anchoring

entries.content:
##Hollow Body Chambers
---

The ability to make empty spaces inside the body without harming function.

The user forms tubes, rooms, capsules, vents, pockets, tunnels, mouthless cavities, or inflated chambers. Objects can be stored, separated, transported through tubes, cushioned in air pockets, or protected from outside impact. People can shelter inside a safe chamber if the user forms air holes, soft walls, and stable exits.

The user decides whether chambers are hidden, transparent, padded, sealed, ventilated, moving, or connected to other body passages. Typical uses include hide someone inside a hollow torso dome; make a breathing tube through smoke; carry fragile tools in an air chamber; form a tunnel under a blocked door.

---
entries.name: Hollow Body Chambers

entries.content:
##Psychic and Mind Target Resistance
---

The defensive benefit of not having a single stable brain shape or ordinary nervous system target.

The user’s thinking pattern can spread through the body, move away from the head, split across pieces, or hide in distributed awareness. Objects or devices aimed at brainwaves, pressure points, skull contact, or neural pathways cannot rely on normal anatomy. People using mind powers may find the user slippery, diffuse, strangely elastic in thought, or difficult to pin to one mental location.

The user can still be affected by sufficiently broad supernatural mind control if the setting allows it, but body-based neural attacks are unreliable. Typical uses include move awareness out of the head before a psychic probe; keep fighting after head damage; split awareness across decoys; make brain scans read as nonsense.

---
entries.name: Psychic and Mind Target Resistance

entries.content:
##Infiltration Forms
---

The stealth package combining disguise, crack movement, object imitation, sensory extensions, and silent reshaping.

The user becomes vents, cords, rugs, signs, pipes, stains, furniture, insects shapes, or flat decorative patterns. Documents, keys, cameras, phones, vents, and door mechanisms can be reached without opening paths normally. People pass by the user, lean on them, sit on them, or speak nearby without realizing the object is alive.

The user can scout by tendrils, gather sound through stretched ears, and escape through the same narrow paths used to enter.
